Table fan.household {
  household_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the household record in the fan domain. Primary key for the household data product. Entity role: MASTER_PARTY — represents a family/household unit that the business interacts with as a B2C counterparty.']
  fan_club_membership_id varchar [note: 'Identifier for the household\'s official fan club membership, if applicable. Links the household to a specific fan club organization for club-level benefits, communications, and event access.']
  franchise_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the household\'s primary preferred team or franchise. Drives team-specific marketing, merchandise recommendations, and event notifications for home games.']
  household_fan_profile_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the primary account holder fan profile within this household. The designated head-of-household fan who holds primary contractual and billing responsibility. Used for season ticket holder family accounts and loyalty aggregation. PARTY_REFERENCE category.']
  merged_into_household_id varchar [note: 'If this household record was merged into another household (status = \'merged\'), this field references the surviving household_id. Enables data lineage tracking and ensures historical records can be traced to the canonical household.']
  preferred_team_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the household\'s primary preferred team or franchise. Drives team-specific marketing, merchandise recommendations, and event notifications for home games.']
  preferred_venue_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the household\'s most frequently attended or preferred venue. Used for venue-specific promotions, parking pre-sales, and facility upgrade notifications.']
  primary_fan_fan_profile_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the primary account holder fan profile within this household. The designated head-of-household fan who holds primary contractual and billing responsibility. Used for season ticket holder family accounts and loyalty aggregation. PARTY_REFERENCE category.']
  season_ticket_account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to ticketing.season_ticket_account. Business justification: Household-level STH management — renewal campaigns, family account benefit allocation, and household LTV reporting require a direct household-to-STH-account link. season_ticket_account_number on house']
  acquisition_channel varchar [note: 'The channel through which the household was first acquired as a fan relationship. \'dtc_app\' refers to Direct-To-Consumer (DTC) mobile or web application. Used for Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) analysis and channel ROI (Return on Investment) reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ticketing|merchandise|dtc_app|event_registration|fan_club|referral|social_media|venue_kiosk — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  acquisition_date date [note: 'Date on which the household was first established as a fan relationship record. Used for cohort analysis, tenure-based loyalty calculations, and LTV (Lifetime Value) trajectory modeling.']
  address_line1 varchar [note: 'Primary street address line for the household. Used for direct mail campaigns, season ticket holder correspondence, merchandise shipping, and deduplication of household records. Critical for direct mail deduplication per product description.']
  address_line2 varchar [note: 'Secondary address line for the household (apartment, suite, unit number). Supplements address_line1 for complete postal address resolution and direct mail accuracy.']
  annual_spend_usd decimal(18,2) [note: 'Total spend in US dollars attributed to the household across all revenue streams (ticketing, merchandise, concessions, streaming) in the current or most recent fiscal year. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA FI. Used for household-level revenue reporting and tier qualification.']
  ccpa_opt_out_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the household has exercised their CCPA right to opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information. When True, the household\'s data must not be sold or shared with third parties for commercial purposes.']
  city varchar [note: 'City of the household\'s primary mailing address. Used for geographic market segmentation, regional event targeting, and RSN (Regional Sports Network) audience analysis.']
  combined_ltv_usd decimal(18,2) [note: 'Aggregated Lifetime Value (LTV) in US dollars across all fan members within the household, sourced from SAP S/4HANA SD and Ticketmaster transaction history. Represents total cumulative revenue attributed to the household. Used for household-level spend analysis, VIP qualification, and retention investment prioritization. Note: this is a sourced/loaded value from the operational system, not a real-time calculation.']
  country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the household\'s primary address (e.g., USA, GBR, CAN). Determines applicable privacy regulation (GDPR for EU households, CCPA for California/USA households) and international fan base reporting.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the household record was first created in the system of record. Conforms to ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category per MASTER_PARTY role.']
  crm_account_reference varchar [note: 'External identifier for this household as recorded in the Salesforce CRM system. Enables cross-system reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational CRM. Serves as the business-facing household reference number.']
  data_enrichment_source varchar [note: 'Indicates the origin of demographic and enrichment data for this household record. \'self_reported\' means data was provided directly by the household; \'third_party\' means sourced from a data provider; \'inferred\' means derived from behavioral signals; \'crm_import\' means loaded from Salesforce CRM; \'combined\' means multiple sources merged.']
  deduplication_key varchar [note: 'Composite hash or normalized key used for direct mail deduplication and household matching across source systems. Typically derived from a normalized combination of household name, address, and postal code. Critical for preventing duplicate mailings and double-counting in household-level spend analysis.']
  gdpr_consent_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the household has provided valid GDPR consent for data processing and marketing communications. Mandatory for EU-resident households. When False, data processing must be restricted to legitimate interest or contractual necessity bases only.']
  household_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable display name for the household unit, typically the family surname or a chosen household label (e.g., \'The Johnson Family\'). Used in direct mail, CRM correspondence, and fan engagement communications. IDENTITY_LABEL category per MASTER_PARTY role.']
  household_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the household record. \'active\' indicates an engaged household with at least one active fan member. \'merged\' indicates the household was consolidated into another. \'deceased\' indicates all primary members are deceased. LIFECYCLE_STATUS category per MASTER_PARTY role.']
  household_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the household composition. \'family\' denotes a multi-generational unit; \'couple\' denotes a two-adult unit; \'individual\' denotes a single-person household; \'corporate\' denotes a business account grouped as a household; \'fan_club\' denotes an organized fan club treated as a household unit. CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category per MASTER_PARTY role.']
  income_band varchar [note: 'Estimated annual household income range derived from third-party demographic enrichment or self-reported data. Used for premium product targeting (VIP packages, luxury suites, premium season tickets), sponsorship audience profiling, and household-level spend propensity modeling.']
  is_season_ticket_holder boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the household currently holds at least one active season ticket package across any league or venue. Critical flag for season ticket holder family account management, priority renewal communications, and dedicated account services.']
  is_vip_member boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the household holds an active VIP (Very Important Person) membership entitling members to premium hospitality, exclusive event access, and dedicated concierge services.']
  last_engagement_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent engagement activity recorded for any member of the household (ticket purchase, event attendance, app login, merchandise purchase, or content interaction). Used for churn risk scoring and re-engagement campaign targeting.']
  loyalty_points_balance varchar [note: 'Current aggregate loyalty points balance accumulated across all household members. Used for redemption eligibility checks, tier qualification calculations, and household-level loyalty reporting.']
  loyalty_tier varchar [note: 'Current loyalty program tier assigned to the household based on aggregated member spend, attendance, and engagement. Determines household-level benefits including priority ticketing access, merchandise discounts, and VIP event invitations. Supports multi-member loyalty aggregation as described in the product scope.']
  marketing_opt_in_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the household has opted in to receive marketing communications across all channels. Distinct from GDPR consent (which is jurisdiction-specific); this is the operational marketing suppression flag used by Salesforce CRM and Adobe Experience Platform campaign tools.']
  member_count varchar [note: 'Total number of individual fan profiles currently associated with this household. Used for family ticket package eligibility, loyalty tier aggregation, and household-level capacity planning.']
  nps_score varchar [note: 'Most recent Net Promoter Score (NPS) recorded for the household, ranging from 0 to 10. Captures household-level fan satisfaction and likelihood to recommend. Supports household-level NPS tracking as specified in the product scope. Used for churn risk identification and fan experience improvement initiatives.']
  nps_survey_date date [note: 'Date on which the most recent NPS survey response was recorded for the household. Used to determine survey recency, schedule follow-up surveys, and track NPS trend over time.']
  postal_code varchar [note: 'Postal or ZIP code of the household\'s primary mailing address. Used for direct mail deduplication, geographic segmentation, and proximity-based venue targeting.']
  preferred_communication_channel varchar [note: 'Household\'s preferred channel for receiving marketing and operational communications. Drives outbound campaign channel selection in Salesforce CRM and Adobe Experience Platform to maximize engagement and respect household preferences.']
  preferred_language varchar [note: 'BCP 47 language tag representing the household\'s preferred language for communications and digital content (e.g., \'en\', \'es\', \'fr\', \'pt-BR\'). Supports multilingual fan engagement across global markets.']
  preferred_sport varchar [note: 'Primary sport preference declared or inferred for the household (e.g., \'NFL\', \'NBA\', \'MLB\', \'NHL\', \'MLS\', \'UFC\'). Used for targeted event recommendations, broadcast content personalization, and sponsorship audience segmentation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NFL|NBA|MLB|NHL|MLS|UFC|ATP|FIFA|other — promote to reference product]']
  primary_email varchar [note: 'Primary email address for household-level communications including family ticket offers, loyalty program statements, and newsletter distribution. PRIMARY_CONTACT category per MASTER_PARTY role.']
  primary_phone varchar [note: 'Primary contact phone number for the household. Used for outbound fan engagement calls, event notifications, and emergency contact for season ticket holders.']
  segment_code varchar [note: 'CRM-assigned segmentation code classifying the household into a strategic fan segment (e.g., \'SUPER_FAN\', \'CASUAL_ATTENDEE\', \'LAPSED\', \'HIGH_VALUE\'). Drives targeted marketing campaigns, loyalty tier assignment, and personalization strategies via Adobe Experience Platform. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product as segment codes are business-defined and numerous]']
  state_province varchar [note: 'State or province of the household\'s primary mailing address. Used for regional compliance (CCPA for California households), tax jurisdiction determination, and geographic fan base analysis.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the household record in the system of record. Conforms to ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change data capture (CDC) processing in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.']

  Note: 'Groups individual fan profiles into a household or family unit for B2C relationship management. Tracks household name, primary account holder reference, number of members, household address, combined lifetime value, household income band, and household segment classification. Enables family ticket packages, household-level NPS tracking, multi-member loyalty aggregation, and season ticket holder family accounts. Critical for direct mail deduplication and household-level spend analysis.'
}

Table fan.loyalty_transaction {

  points_multiplier decimal(5,2) [note: 'The multiplier factor applied to the base points calculation for this transaction, driven by membership tier, active promotions, or special event bonuses.   processing_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the loyalty transaction was processed and applied to the fan\'s balance by the loyalty management system. May differ from transaction_timestamp for batch-processed or delayed-confirmation transactions (e.g., post-event check-in reconciliation).']
  redemption_value decimal(12,2) [note: 'The monetary equivalent value of the points redeemed in this transaction, expressed in the operating currency. Populated only for redemption-type transactions. Used for loyalty liability accounting, reward cost tracking, and EBITDA impact analysis.']
  reversal_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded explanation for why a transaction was reversed or adjusted. Populated only when transaction_status is \'reversed\' or transaction_type is \'adjust\'. Supports audit compliance and customer service resolution tracking.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record that originated this loyalty transaction event. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and system-of-record traceability across the loyalty ecosystem. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: salesforce_crm|adobe_aep|ticketmaster|axs|shopify|sap_s4|archtics|manual — promote to reference product]']
  source_transaction_reference varchar [note: 'The native transaction identifier from the originating source system (e.g., Ticketmaster order number, Shopify order ID, SAP document number). Enables cross-system reconciliation and traceability back to the system of record.']
  tier_qualifying_points decimal(12,2) [note: 'The number of points from this transaction that count specifically toward the fan\'s tier qualification balance, which may differ from the total points_amount when bonus or promotional points are excluded from tier calculations.']
  transaction_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally visible, human-readable reference number assigned to this loyalty transaction. Used in fan-facing communications, customer service lookups, and audit trails. Format: LT- followed by 10 digits.']
  transaction_status varchar [note: 'Current workflow state of the loyalty transaction.   transaction_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time at which the loyalty point event occurred in the real world (e.g., when the ticket was purchased, when the check-in was recorded, when the content was viewed). This is the principal business event time, distinct from record audit timestamps.']
  transaction_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the nature of the loyalty point movement: earn (points awarded for qualifying activity), redeem (points spent by fan), adjust (manual correction or bonus), expire (points removed due to inactivity or policy), transfer (points moved between accounts).']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this loyalty transaction record was most recently modified in the data platform (e.g., status update from pending to confirmed, or reversal applied). Supports change data capture and audit trail completeness.']

  Note: 'Transactional ledger of all loyalty point earning and redemption events for a fan. Captures transaction type (earn, redeem, adjust, expire, transfer), points amount, transaction date, triggering activity (ticket purchase, merchandise buy, check-in, content view, referral), reference order or event ID, running balance after transaction, and transaction status.   benefit_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the benefit definition within the benefit catalogue (e.g., PRIO-TKT-001, MERCH-DISC-15, VIP-LOUNGE-ACC). Used for benefit fulfilment lookups and cross-system reconciliation.']

  redemption_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time after which the benefit can no longer be redeemed. Provides finer-grained control than effective_until for time-sensitive benefits such as pre-event VIP access windows or flash merchandise discounts.']
  redemption_method varchar [note: 'The technical mechanism by which the fan redeems the benefit. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: barcode|qr_code|rfid|voucher_code|digital_wallet|manual|auto_applied — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  redemption_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time from which the fan may begin redeeming this benefit. May differ from effective_from when a benefit window opens at a specific time (e.g., priority ticket sales opening at 10:00 AM on a specific date). Used for time-gated benefit activation.']
  season_year varchar [note: 'The sports season year to which this benefit applies (e.g., 2024 for the 2024 season, or 2024 for a 2024/25 season). Used to scope benefits to a specific competitive season for season ticket holders and annual membership programs.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The operational system of record from which this benefit record originated or is primarily managed. Used for data lineage, integration audit, and conflict resolution in the Silver layer of the Databricks Lakehouse. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: salesforce_crm|adobe_experience_platform|archtics|ticketmaster_axs|shopify_plus|sap_s4hana|manual — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  terms_and_conditions_url varchar [note: 'URL linking to the full terms and conditions governing the use of this benefit. Required for GDPR and CCPA compliance to ensure fans have access to the conditions under which their benefit entitlements are granted and may be revoked.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this membership benefit record was last modified. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail compliance.']
  usage_limit_per_event varchar [note: 'Maximum number of times this benefit can be redeemed at a single event. For example, a VIP lounge pass may allow entry once per event, or a priority ticket window may allow purchase of up to 4 tickets per event. Null indicates no per-event restriction.']
  venue_zone varchar [note: 'The specific zone or area within the venue where this benefit is applicable or redeemable (e.g., \'VIP Lounge Level 3\', \'Club Concourse\', \'Premium Parking Zone A\'). Used by Archtics for access control configuration and venue operations staff for benefit fulfilment.']
  vip_tier_level varchar [note: 'The VIP tier classification associated with this benefit, indicating the prestige level of the benefit within the fan loyalty hierarchy. Used for VIP experience management, venue access prioritisation, and fan segmentation in Adobe Experience Platform and Salesforce CRM.']

  Note: 'Defines the specific benefits attached to a membership tier or individual membership record. Captures benefit type (priority ticketing, parking pass, merchandise discount, VIP lounge access, meet-and-greet, exclusive content access), benefit description, quantity or usage limit, redemption method, benefit value, and validity period.   rfm_tier varchar [note: 'RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) tier classification assigned to fans in this segment, applicable when segment_type is \'rfm\'. Champions are high-value frequent buyers; lost fans have not engaged recently. Drives targeted retention and reactivation campaigns.']

  segment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the segment definition. Active segments are available for campaign targeting; draft segments are under construction; archived segments are retained for historical reference but not used in live campaigns.']
  segment_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the segmentation methodology applied: RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary), behavioral (engagement actions), demographic (age, gender, location), psychographic (interests, values), predictive (ML-model-driven), or geographic. Drives which analytics model and personalization engine is applied.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Operational system of record from which this segment definition was sourced or created. Adobe Experience Platform is the primary source for behavioral and predictive segments; Salesforce CRM is the primary source for relationship-based and campaign segments.']
  subtype varchar [note: 'Secondary classification providing finer granularity within the segment type (e.g., \'churn_risk\', \'upsell_candidate\', \'loyalty_tier_upgrade\', \'event_attendee\', \'merchandise_buyer\').   tags varchar [note: 'Comma-separated business tags or labels applied to the segment for discoverability, governance, and categorization (e.g., \'retention, q4_campaign, nfl_season, vip, churn_prevention\').   updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this segment record was most recently modified, including changes to definition criteria, status, configuration, or metadata. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Supports change tracking and data lineage.']

  is_primary_segment boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this segment is the fan\'s primary or highest-priority segment assignment when a fan belongs to multiple segments simultaneously. Used for personalization and communication preference resolution.']

  next_evaluation_date date [note: 'The scheduled date for the next automated re-evaluation of this fan\'s segment eligibility. Supports segment refresh scheduling and ensures time-sensitive segments (e.g., event-proximity segments) are kept current.']
  nps_cohort_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this segment assignment is specifically designated for NPS (Net Promoter Score) survey cohort analysis. When true, the fan is included in NPS measurement campaigns for fan satisfaction tracking.']
  override_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text justification provided by a CRM analyst when manually assigning or revoking a fan\'s segment membership, overriding automated rule-based or ML-predicted assignment. Populated only when assignment_method is \'manual\'.']
  priority_rank varchar [note: 'Numeric rank indicating the priority of this segment assignment relative to other active segment memberships for the same fan. Lower values indicate higher priority. Used for conflict resolution when a fan belongs to multiple segments with competing campaign rules.']
  revocation_date date [note: 'The date on which this fan\'s segment membership was revoked or removed, either by automated rule exit, manual override, or consent withdrawal. Null if the membership has not been revoked.']
  revocation_reason varchar [note: 'The reason code explaining why this fan\'s segment membership was revoked. \'rule_exit\' = fan no longer meets segment criteria; \'consent_withdrawn\' = GDPR/CCPA consent revoked; \'manual_removal\' = analyst override; \'data_quality\' = data integrity issue; \'segment_deprecated\' = segment definition retired; \'opt_out\' = fan opted out of communications.']
  score_model_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the ML model or rule engine that produced the assignment_score. Enables model governance, reproducibility, and performance tracking over time. Applicable when assignment_method is \'ml_predicted\'.']
  score_percentile decimal(5,2) [note: 'The percentile rank of the fan\'s assignment score within the segment population at the time of assignment (0.00–100.00). Used for tiered targeting and prioritization within a segment cohort.']
  segment_category varchar [note: 'The analytical category of the segment to which the fan is assigned. Denormalized from the segment definition for query performance. Supports filtering and reporting by segment type without joining to the segment master.']
  segment_version varchar [note: 'Version label of the segment definition that was active at the time of this assignment. Enables historical analysis of how segment criteria evolved and ensures reproducibility of cohort membership.']
  source_record_reference varchar [note: 'The native record identifier from the originating source system (e.g., Salesforce CRM Campaign Member ID, Adobe AEP Segment Membership ID). Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and cross-system traceability.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The operational system of record that originated this segment assignment. Identifies the upstream data source for lineage and reconciliation purposes.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this segment assignment record was most recently modified in the data platform. Supports change data capture, incremental processing, and audit trail requirements.']

  Note: 'Association table recording which fans belong to which CRM segments at a given point in time. Tracks fan profile ID, segment ID, assignment date, assignment method (rule-based, manual, ML-predicted), assignment score or confidence, expiry date, and active flag. Supports time-variant segment membership for campaign targeting, personalization, and NPS cohort analysis. Carries its own business data (assignment method, score) beyond a simple M:N link.'
}

  consent_version varchar [note: 'The version identifier of the privacy consent notice presented to the fan at the time of survey submission. Enables compliance audit trails demonstrating which consent terms were in effect when data was collected.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this NPS response record was first ingested and created in the Silver layer data product. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance.']
  data_retention_expiry_date date [note: 'The date after which this NPS response record must be purged or anonymised in accordance with the applicable data retention policy. Supports GDPR right to erasure and CCPA deletion request compliance.']
  device_type varchar [note: 'The type of device used by the fan to complete the NPS survey. Enables channel and device-level analysis of survey completion rates and score distributions.']
  external_response_ref varchar [note: 'The externally-known unique identifier for this response as assigned by the survey platform (e.g., Adobe Experience Platform response GUID or third-party NPS tool reference). Used for cross-system reconciliation.']
  fan_locale_country_code varchar [note: 'The ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the fan\'s locale at the time of survey response. Enables geographic segmentation of NPS scores across global markets.']
  fan_tenure_days varchar [note: 'The number of days the fan has been a registered member as of the response date. Enables cohort analysis of NPS scores by fan tenure and lifecycle stage.']
  follow_up_completed_date date [note: 'The actual date on which the follow-up action for this NPS response was completed and resolved. Used to measure SLA adherence and time-to-resolution for detractor recovery.']
  follow_up_due_date date [note: 'The target date by which the follow-up action for a detractor response must be completed, as defined by the fan engagement Service Level Agreement (SLA). Null if no follow-up is required.']
  follow_up_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this NPS response requires a follow-up action, typically triggered for detractor scores (0-6) to initiate CRM recovery workflows. True = follow-up action is required; False = no follow-up needed.']
  follow_up_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the follow-up action for this NPS response. Tracks the detractor recovery workflow lifecycle from initial identification through resolution. \'not_required\' for passive and promoter responses where no action was triggered.']
  is_anonymous boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the fan opted to submit this NPS response anonymously. True = anonymous submission where fan identity is not linked; False = identified submission linked to fan profile. Impacts GDPR data subject rights applicability.']
  is_first_response boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this is the fan\'s first-ever NPS survey response on record. Used for new fan onboarding analytics and baseline satisfaction benchmarking.']
  membership_tier_at_response varchar [note: 'The fan\'s loyalty membership tier at the time of survey response (e.g., standard, silver, gold, platinum, VIP). Captured as a snapshot to enable NPS analysis by membership tier without dependency on current tier status. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|silver|gold|platinum|vip|season_ticket_holder — promote to reference product]']
  nps_category varchar [note: 'Derived classification of the fan based on their NPS score: \'promoter\' (score 9-10), \'passive\' (score 7-8), or \'detractor\' (score 0-6). Used for CRM segmentation, detractor recovery workflows, and NPS calculation reporting.']
  nps_score varchar [note: 'The fan\'s raw NPS rating on a scale of 0 to 10, where 0 is extremely unlikely to recommend and 10 is extremely likely to recommend. The principal quantitative measurement of fan satisfaction. Scores 0-6 = Detractor, 7-8 = Passive, 9-10 = Promoter.']
  primary_feedback_theme varchar [note: 'The dominant topic or theme identified from the verbatim comment through NLP text classification (e.g., \'venue_experience\', \'ticketing\', \'broadcast_quality\', \'athlete_performance\', \'food_beverage\', \'customer_service\'). Used for root cause analysis of NPS drivers. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: venue_experience|ticketing|broadcast_quality|athlete_performance|food_beverage|customer_service|merchandise|parking|app_experience — promote to reference product]']
  prior_nps_score varchar [note: 'The fan\'s NPS score from their most recent previous survey response, captured as a snapshot at the time of this response. Enables score delta analysis and trend tracking without requiring a self-join.']
  response_channel varchar [note: 'The channel through which the fan received and submitted the NPS survey. Used to analyze satisfaction scores by engagement channel and optimize survey distribution strategy.']
  response_latency_minutes varchar [note: 'The elapsed time in minutes between the survey invitation being sent and the fan submitting their response. Used to assess recency bias and optimize survey timing for maximum response quality.']
  response_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the NPS response record. \'submitted\' = complete and valid; \'partial\' = survey started but not fully completed; \'withdrawn\' = fan requested removal; \'invalid\' = failed validation rules; \'duplicate\' = identified as a duplicate submission.']
  response_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time when the fan submitted the NPS survey response. Principal business event timestamp representing the moment of fan satisfaction measurement. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.']
  score_change_direction varchar [note: 'Categorical indicator of whether the fan\'s NPS score improved, declined, or remained unchanged compared to their prior response. \'first_response\' when no prior score exists. Supports trend analysis and loyalty program effectiveness measurement.']
  sentiment_label varchar [note: 'Categorical sentiment classification derived from NLP analysis of the verbatim comment. Complements the numeric sentiment score for reporting and CRM segmentation purposes.']
  sentiment_score decimal(5,4) [note: 'Numeric sentiment polarity score derived from NLP analysis of the verbatim comment, ranging from -1.0000 (most negative) to 1.0000 (most positive). Populated by the Adobe Experience Platform AI/ML sentiment analysis pipeline.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational system of record from which this NPS response was ingested into the Silver layer. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and multi-platform survey consolidation.']
  survey_completion_time_seconds varchar [note: 'The elapsed time in seconds from when the fan opened the survey to when they submitted it. Used to assess survey engagement quality and identify potentially rushed or bot-generated responses.']
  survey_invitation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the NPS survey invitation was sent to the fan. Used to calculate response latency (time between invitation and submission) and to assess survey recency bias.']
  survey_language_code varchar [note: 'The ISO 639-1 language code (optionally with ISO 3166-1 country subtag) in which the survey was presented and the fan responded. Supports multilingual NPS analysis across global markets.']
  survey_trigger_type varchar [note: 'The business event or rule that triggered the NPS survey invitation to the fan. Enables analysis of satisfaction scores by trigger context and optimization of survey timing strategy.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this NPS response record was last modified, such as when follow-up status was updated or a CRM case was linked. Supports audit trail and change tracking.']
  verbatim_comment varchar [note: 'The free-text open-ended comment provided by the fan explaining their NPS score. Contains qualitative feedback used for sentiment analysis, theme identification, and CRM case management. May contain sensitive personal opinions.']

  Note: 'Individual fan NPS survey response record. Captures fan profile ID, survey ID, NPS score (0-10), promoter/passive/detractor classification, verbatim comment text, response channel, response timestamp, follow-up action flag, follow-up status, and associated event or purchase reference. SSOT for fan satisfaction measurement. Feeds CRM case management for detractor recovery workflows.'
}

Table fan.payment_method {
  payment_method_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for payment_method']
  account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to fan.account. Business justification: Payment methods are stored on operational accounts, not just fan profiles. The account table contains payment-related context (pci_payment_token, card_brand, card_last_four, card_expiry_date, default_']

  auto_renewal_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this payment instrument is authorized by the fan for automatic recurring charges such as season ticket renewals, membership subscriptions, and OTT streaming plan renewals. Requires explicit fan consent per GDPR and CCPA mandates.']
  avs_response_code varchar [note: 'Response code returned by the card issuer\'s Address Verification Service (AVS) during the enrollment authorization.   bank_account_last_four varchar [note: 'Last four digits of the bank account number for direct debit payment methods. Displayed to the fan for identification purposes. Applicable only when payment_method_type is \'direct_debit\'. Null for card-based instruments.']
  bank_routing_code varchar [note: 'Bank routing number (US ACH) or sort code (UK/EU) associated with a direct debit payment method. Used for ACH or SEPA payment processing. Stored in truncated or tokenized form. Null for non-direct-debit instruments.']
  billing_address_line1 varchar [note: 'Primary street address line of the billing address associated with this payment instrument. Used for Address Verification Service (AVS) checks during card-not-present transactions on ticketing and merchandise platforms.']

  billing_country_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the billing address (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU). Determines applicable privacy regulation (GDPR for EU/EEA, CCPA for California), currency routing, and cross-border payment processing rules.']
  billing_postal_code varchar [note: 'Postal or ZIP code of the billing address. Critical input for Address Verification Service (AVS) checks on card-not-present transactions. Also used for geographic segmentation and tax jurisdiction mapping.']
  billing_state_province varchar [note: 'State or province component of the billing address. Used for AVS verification, tax jurisdiction determination, and CCPA/GDPR applicability assessment for fan data privacy compliance.']
  bin_number varchar [note: 'First 6–8 digits of the payment card number identifying the issuing institution and card product type. Used for routing decisions, interchange category determination, and fraud analysis. Stored as a non-sensitive BIN (not the full PAN) per PCI-DSS truncation rules.']
  card_brand varchar [note: 'Payment network or card scheme brand associated with the instrument (e.g., Visa, Mastercard, Amex). Applicable for credit and debit card types. Impacts interchange fee rates, refund processing timelines, and eligibility for certain promotional financing offers on season tickets.']
  card_last_four varchar [note: 'Last four digits of the payment card Primary Account Number (PAN). Displayed to the fan in account management and checkout screens to identify their saved card without exposing the full PAN. Permitted display element under PCI-DSS truncation rules.']
  cardholder_name varchar [note: 'Name of the individual as it appears on the payment card or as registered with the payment instrument. Used for display in account management screens and for AVS/identity verification during high-value transactions. Stored only where operationally required per PCI-DSS data minimization principles.']
  consent_capture_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the fan explicitly consented to storing this payment instrument and authorizing recurring charges. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Required for GDPR Article 6 lawful basis documentation and CCPA compliance audit trails.']
  consent_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the terms and conditions or privacy policy under which the fan consented to storing this payment instrument. Enables compliance teams to identify fans who consented under outdated policy versions requiring re-consent.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code associated with the payment instrument (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Supports multi-currency fan accounts across global markets. Relevant for gift card balances, direct debit mandates, and cross-border transaction routing.']
  direct_debit_mandate_ref varchar [note: 'Unique mandate reference number assigned for SEPA Direct Debit or ACH authorization agreements. Required for recurring direct debit collections such as installment-based season ticket payment plans. Null for non-direct-debit instruments.']
  enrollment_channel varchar [note: 'Channel through which the fan added this payment instrument to their account. Supports fraud analysis, channel attribution, and UX optimization. \'pos\' — Point of Sale terminal at venue; \'partner_api\' — enrolled via third-party integration (e.g., Ticketmaster, Shopify Plus).']
  enrollment_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the payment instrument was first added to the fan account. Used for lifecycle management, fraud velocity checks, and compliance audit trails. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.']
  expiry_month varchar [note: 'Two-digit calendar month (1–12) in which the payment card expires. Used in conjunction with expiry_year to determine card validity and trigger pre-expiry notification workflows for membership auto-renewal continuity.']
  expiry_notification_sent boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a pre-expiry notification has been dispatched to the fan via their preferred communication channel (email, SMS, push) to prompt card update before membership or season ticket auto-renewal fails. Managed by Adobe Experience Platform journey automation.']
  expiry_year varchar [note: 'Four-digit calendar year in which the payment card expires. Combined with expiry_month to assess card validity. Triggers automated pre-expiry fan communications to update payment details and prevent lapsed season ticket or membership renewals.']
  fraud_risk_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric risk score (0.00–100.00) assigned to this payment instrument by the fraud detection engine at enrollment or last transaction.   gift_card_balance decimal(12,2) [note: 'Current monetary balance remaining on a stored-value gift card payment instrument. Applicable only when payment_method_type is \'gift_card\'. Updated after each redemption transaction. Null for non-gift-card instruments. Denominated in the currency indicated by currency_code.']
  is_default boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this payment instrument is the fan\'s designated default method for one-click purchases, membership auto-renewals, and express checkout. Only one payment method per fan account should have this flag set to True at any time.']
  issuer_country_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the financial institution that issued the payment card. Derived from the card BIN (Bank Identification Number). Used for cross-border transaction fee assessment, currency mismatch detection, and regulatory reporting.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this payment method record was most recently modified (e.g., billing address update, status change, token refresh). Supports audit trail requirements and Silver Layer data lineage tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.']
  last_used_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time of the most recent successful transaction processed against this payment instrument. Used to identify dormant payment methods for cleanup workflows and to assess instrument activity for fraud monitoring.']
  method_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the payment instrument. \'active\' — valid and available for transactions; \'expired\' — card expiry date has passed; \'suspended\' — temporarily blocked due to fraud or dispute; \'removed\' — fan has deleted the instrument; \'pending_verification\' — awaiting micro-deposit or 3DS verification.']
  network_transaction_reference varchar [note: 'Unique identifier assigned by the card network (Visa, Mastercard) during the initial card-on-file enrollment authorization. Required for subsequent MIT (Merchant-Initiated Transaction) recurring charges such as season ticket auto-renewals, ensuring compliance with card network stored credential mandates.']
  payment_method_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the payment instrument category. Drives checkout flow logic, fee structures, and refund eligibility across ticketing (Ticketmaster/AXS), merchandise (Shopify Plus), and membership auto-renewal workflows.']
  pci_compliance_status varchar [note: 'Indicates the PCI-DSS compliance posture of this payment instrument record. \'compliant\' — token and data handling meet PCI-DSS v4.0 requirements; \'non_compliant\' — a compliance gap has been identified requiring remediation; \'pending_review\' — under compliance assessment. Supports PCI SSC audit reporting.']
  source_system_token_ref varchar [note: 'External reference identifier for this payment token as recorded in the originating operational system (e.g., Ticketmaster/AXS vault ID, Shopify Plus payment method ID, Salesforce CRM payment record ID). Enables cross-system reconciliation and lineage tracing in the Silver Layer.']
  token_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'Opaque tokenized representation of the underlying payment instrument issued by the tokenization provider (e.g., Braintree, Stripe, Adyen). Replaces the raw PAN in all downstream systems. Never stores the actual card number. Compliant with PCI-DSS tokenization standards.']
  tokenization_provider varchar [note: 'Name of the third-party PCI-DSS compliant tokenization service provider that issued and manages the payment token. Used for routing, reconciliation, and vendor management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Braintree|Adyen|Stripe|CyberSource|Worldpay|Checkout.com|Spreedly — promote to reference product if provider list grows beyond 6]']
  verification_method varchar [note: 'Method used to verify the payment instrument at enrollment. \'3ds\' — 3-D Secure authentication (Visa Secure / Mastercard Identity Check); \'avs\' — Address Verification Service; \'micro_deposit\' — two small deposits for bank account verification; \'cvv_check\' — card security code validation; \'none\' — no additional verification performed.']
  verification_status varchar [note: 'Outcome of the payment instrument verification process. \'verified\' — successfully authenticated; \'unverified\' — verification not yet completed; \'failed\' — verification attempt was unsuccessful; \'pending\' — verification in progress. Determines eligibility for high-value transactions such as season ticket purchases.']
  wallet_provider varchar [note: 'Name of the digital wallet service when payment_method_type is \'digital_wallet\'. Identifies the wallet ecosystem for routing, reconciliation, and fan experience analytics. Null for non-wallet payment types.']

  Note: 'Tokenized payment instrument records stored on file for a fan account. Captures payment method type (credit card, debit card, digital wallet, direct debit, gift card), card brand, last four digits, expiry month/year, billing address reference, tokenization provider, token value, default payment flag, and PCI-DSS compliance status. Enables one-click ticket purchases, auto-renewal of memberships, and merchandise checkout. Compliant with PCI-DSS tokenization standards.'

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|silver|gold|platinum|founding|vip — promote to reference product if tiers expand beyond 6]']

Table fan.personalization_rule {
  personalization_rule_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the personalization_rule association']
  asset_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this personalization rule to the content asset being assigned']
  fan_segment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this personalization rule to the fan segment being targeted']
  ab_test_variant varchar [note: 'Identifier of the A/B or multivariate test arm under which this segment-asset assignment is active (e.g., CONTROL, VARIANT_A, VARIANT_B). Belongs to the assignment, not to the segment or asset independently.']
  activation_status varchar [note: 'Current operational state of this personalization rule assignment. Controls whether the asset is actively being served to the segment. Belongs to the relationship lifecycle, not to either entity alone.']
  assignment_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this content asset was assigned to the fan segment by a CRM or content operations user. Belongs to the relationship record, not to either entity alone.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which this specific segment-to-asset assignment expires and the content ceases to be served under this rule. Distinct from the asset\'s own expiry_date (rights/licence expiry) — this expiry governs the targeting assignment window.']
  priority_rank varchar [note: 'Numeric ranking that determines the delivery priority of this asset relative to other assets assigned to the same fan segment. A lower value indicates higher priority. Belongs to the segment-asset pairing, not to either entity alone.']
  rule_logic varchar [note: 'The structured expression or named rule governing how and when this content asset is delivered to the fan segment. Sourced from the detection phase as personalization_rule. Belongs to the assignment, not to the segment or asset independently.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Content Personalization Rule — the operational contract between a fan segment and a content asset within the sports entertainment personalization engine. Each record captures a deliberate, managed assignment of a specific digital content asset to a specific fan segment, including the activation window, priority ranking, A/B test variant, and rule logic governing delivery. Records are created, updated, and retired by CRM and content operations teams as part of campaign and DTC personalization workflows.. Existence Justification: In sports entertainment personalization, content teams actively assign specific digital assets (video highlights, editorial articles, social media content) to fan segments as part of campaign and personalization workflows. A single fan segment (e.g., \'High-Value Season Ticket Holders\') can be targeted with many different content assets, and a single asset (e.g., a playoff highlight reel) can be assigned to multiple segments simultaneously. This relationship is operationally managed — marketers create, update, and retire these assignments with specific activation windows, priority rankings, and A/B test variants.'
}

Manifest approval and league sign-off process']
  event_fixture_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific event for which this inventory unit is allocated. Links the seat record to the event scheduling master.']
  fixture_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific event for which this inventory unit is allocated. Links the seat record to the event scheduling master.']
  price_zone_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the event-specific price zone assigned to this inventory unit. Price zones define the base pricing tier and dynamic pricing eligibility for the seat.']
  pricing_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to event.event_pricing. Business justification: Seat inventory face_value_amount and dynamic_price_amount are set by the event_pricing configuration. Linking inventory to event_pricing enables pricing governance audit, ensuring each seat\'s price fa']
  seat_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to venue.seat. Business justification: Physical seat manifest validation — kill-seat enforcement, ADA accommodation tracking, and obstructed-view disclosure — requires linking each inventory record to the authoritative venue.seat record. T']
  seating_section_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to venue.seating_section. Business justification: Inventory allocation and manifest validation require linking each ticket inventory record to the canonical seating_section for ADA compliance, sightline disclosure, price zone enforcement, and kill-se']
  venue_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the venue where the event is hosted. Drives seating manifest configuration and ADA compliance mapping.']
  venue_manifest_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to ticketing.venue_manifest. Business justification: ticket_inventory represents individual sellable seat units; venue_manifest defines the physical seat configuration (section/row/seat layout, ADA status, sight lines, kill seats, price zones). Linking ']
  access_gate varchar [note: 'The designated entry gate or access point at the venue through which the holder of this inventory unit is directed. Used for access control configuration in AXS/Ticketmaster gate management and crowd flow planning.']

  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this inventory unit record was first created in the Silver layer, typically corresponding to the initial seating manifest load from Archtics for the event.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to all monetary amounts on this inventory record (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Supports multi-currency operations across global markets.']
  digital_delivery_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this inventory unit supports digital ticket delivery (mobile wallet, NFC, QR code). Drives delivery method options presented at checkout and access control configuration at venue gates.']
  dynamic_price_amount decimal(12,2) [note: 'The current dynamically adjusted price for this inventory unit, reflecting real-time demand signals, sell-through rates, and competitive pricing algorithms. Updated continuously by the dynamic pricing engine. Null if dynamic pricing is not enabled for this inventory unit.']
  face_value_amount decimal(12,2) [note: 'The printed face value price of the ticket for this inventory unit in the event\'s base currency. Represents the base price before dynamic pricing adjustments, fees, or discounts. Used for resale market regulation and revenue reporting.']
  hold_code varchar [note: 'The hold code applied to this inventory unit when status is HELD or RESERVED. Hold codes identify the reason or pool for the hold (e.g., \'SPONSOR\', \'MEDIA\', \'ARTIST\', \'GROUP\', \'SEASON\'). Sourced from Archtics hold code configuration.']
  hold_expiry_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which a temporary hold on this inventory unit expires, returning it to AVAILABLE status if not converted to a sale. Applicable when inventory_status = HELD.']
  host_inventory_code varchar [note: 'The inventory unit identifier assigned by the Ticketmaster Host system. Used for cross-system reconciliation between Archtics seating manifest and Ticketmaster ticketing platform.']
  inventory_status varchar [note: 'Current allocation state of the inventory unit: AVAILABLE (open for sale), SOLD (ticket issued), HELD (temporarily locked for a transaction or hold pool), KILLED (removed from sellable inventory), COMP (complimentary allocation), RESERVED (pre-allocated to a specific channel or package). SSOT for available-to-sell calculations.']
  inventory_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the inventory unit into its designated pool: General Admission (GA), Very Important Person (VIP), Standing Room Only (SRO), Press, Complimentary, or Accessible (ADA). Drives pricing, access control, and channel eligibility rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GA|VIP|SRO|PRESS|COMPLIMENTARY|ACCESSIBLE|SUITE|GROUP|SEASON — promote to reference product]']
  is_ada_accessible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this inventory unit is designated as ADA-accessible, meeting Americans with Disabilities Act requirements for wheelchair access, companion seating, or other accessibility accommodations.']
  is_aisle_seat boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this seat is positioned directly adjacent to an aisle. Used for accessibility filtering, premium seat designation, and fan preference matching in CRM-driven personalization.']
  is_dynamic_pricing_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this inventory unit is eligible for dynamic pricing adjustments. When true, the dynamic_price_amount field is actively maintained by the pricing engine.']
  is_obstructed_view boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this seat has a partially or fully obstructed sightline to the stage or playing field. Drives discounted pricing eligibility and mandatory disclosure requirements at point of sale.']
  is_season_ticket_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this inventory unit is eligible to be included in a season ticket package. Drives season ticket renewal workflows and package construction in Archtics.']
  kill_reason varchar [note: 'Reason code explaining why this inventory unit has been killed (removed from sellable inventory). Applicable only when inventory_status = KILLED. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: OBSTRUCTED_VIEW|STRUCTURAL|SAFETY|ADA_COMPANION|EQUIPMENT|SIGHTLINE|BROADCAST|STAGING — promote to reference product]']
  last_status_change_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the inventory_status of this unit was most recently updated. Supports audit trail, real-time inventory monitoring, and SLA tracking for hold-to-sale conversion.']
  manifest_section_type varchar [note: 'The physical section category within the venue manifest as defined in the Archtics seating configuration. Supports venue layout analytics and capacity planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: LOWER_BOWL|UPPER_BOWL|FLOOR|SUITE|CLUB|STANDING|PRESS_BOX|FIELD|MEZZANINE — promote to reference product]']
  manifest_version varchar [note: 'The version identifier of the venue seating manifest from which this inventory unit was loaded. Enables tracking of manifest changes (e.g., reconfiguration for different event types such as concert vs. sports) and supports rollback and audit.']
  off_sale_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this inventory unit is removed from public sale (e.g., event day cutoff). After this timestamp, the unit is no longer available through standard sales channels.']
  on_sale_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this inventory unit becomes available for public sale. Supports presale window management, channel release scheduling, and real-time available-to-sell calculations.']
  package_type varchar [note: 'Identifies whether this inventory unit is allocated to a single-event sale, a full season ticket package, a mini-plan, group sales block, flex plan, or suite package. Drives entitlement and renewal logic.']
  resale_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this inventory unit is eligible for listing on the official resale marketplace. Controlled by league rules, event-specific restrictions, and package terms (e.g., complimentary tickets are typically resale-ineligible).']
  resale_max_price decimal(12,2) [note: 'The maximum price ceiling enforced for resale of this inventory unit on the official resale marketplace. Applicable in jurisdictions or leagues with anti-scalping price cap regulations.']
  resale_min_price decimal(12,2) [note: 'The minimum price floor enforced for resale of this inventory unit on the official resale marketplace. Set by league policy or event-specific pricing rules to prevent below-face-value resale.']
  row_label varchar [note: 'The alphanumeric row identifier within the section (e.g., \'A\', \'12\', \'AA\'). Null for General Admission (GA) or Standing Room Only (SRO) inventory types.']
  row_sequence varchar [note: 'Numeric sequence of the row within the section, used for physical ordering and proximity-based seat grouping logic. Supports best-available seat algorithms and contiguous seat selection.']
  sale_channel varchar [note: 'The designated sales channel through which this inventory unit is authorized to be sold. Controls channel-specific routing in Ticketmaster/AXS and supports channel mix analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BOX_OFFICE|ONLINE|MOBILE|GROUP_SALES|SEASON_PACKAGE|RESALE|API_PARTNER|VIP_HOSPITALITY — promote to reference product]']
  seat_sequence varchar [note: 'Numeric sequence of the seat within the row, used for physical ordering and contiguous seat grouping. Supports best-available algorithms that prioritize adjacent seats for group purchases.']
  seat_tier varchar [note: 'The commercial tier classification of the seat within the venue manifest, used for pricing strategy and channel routing. Distinct from inventory_type (pool) — tier reflects the quality/experience level of the physical location.']
  seating_capacity_type varchar [note: 'Describes the physical seating configuration of this inventory unit: FIXED (permanent installed seat), PORTABLE (temporary/removable seat), STANDING (no seat, standing position), or LAWN (open lawn area). Affects ADA compliance and capacity calculations.']
  section_label varchar [note: 'The alphanumeric label of the venue section in which this inventory unit is located (e.g., \'101\', \'FLOOR A\', \'PRESS BOX\'). Sourced from the Archtics seating manifest.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which this inventory unit record originated: Archtics (venue seating manifest), Ticketmaster Host (TM_HOST), AXS, or MANUAL (manually entered override). Supports data lineage and reconciliation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this inventory unit record was most recently updated in the Silver layer. Supports incremental data pipeline processing and audit compliance.']

  Note: 'Master record of all available ticket inventory units within the venue seating manifest, sourced from Archtics/Ticketmaster Host. Tracks seat-level availability, hold status, kill status, accessibility designations (ADA), inventory pool assignments (GA, VIP, SRO, press, complimentary), and event-specific price zone mapping. SSOT for what seats exist per event and their current allocation state prior to sale. Supports real-time available-to-sell calculations across all channels.'
}

  eligibility_rule varchar [note: 'Free-text or structured rule expression defining who is eligible to purchase tickets at this tier (e.g., \'Season ticket holders only\', \'Members with Gold status\', \'Military/First Responder ID required\', \'Age 12 and under\').   external_tier_code varchar [note: 'The pricing tier identifier as assigned by the external ticketing system of record (Ticketmaster/AXS or Archtics).   tier_category varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the pricing tier aligned with industry-standard seating categories: GA (General Admission), VIP (Very Important Person), SRO (Standing Room Only), PREMIUM, SUITE, ACCESSIBLE (ADA-compliant), CLUB, or FIELD level.   tier_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the pricing tier across systems (e.g., GA01, VIP_PLAT, SRO_STD, SUITE_A). Used as the business key in Ticketmaster/AXS and Archtics integrations.']

  Note: 'Reference catalog of pricing tiers available for ticket inventory, including GA (General Admission), VIP, SRO (Standing Room Only), premium club, suite, and accessible seating tiers. Table ticketing.dynamic_price_rule {

Linking to employee enables approval chain audits, accountability']

  performance_stat_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to athlete.performance_stat. Business justification: Performance-Based Dynamic Ticket Pricing: Star player performance metrics (points, win streaks, milestones) are named demand signals for dynamic pricing engines. Linking dynamic_price_rule to performa']
  price_tier_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the ticket pricing tier (GA, VIP, SRO) to which this rule is scoped. Allows tier-specific dynamic pricing strategies.']
  pricing_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to event.event_pricing. Business justification: Dynamic price rules operate within bounds set by event_pricing (floor, ceiling, multiplier). Revenue management requires linking each rule to its parent pricing configuration to enforce pricing govern']
  season_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the league season or event season to which this pricing rule is scoped. Enables season-level yield management and financial planning alignment.']
  target_fan_segment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to platform.fan_segment. Business justification: Segment-aware dynamic pricing is standard in sports entertainment — loyalty members receive different price floors/ceilings than general public. Linking dynamic_price_rule to fan_segment enables segme']
  vendor_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to partner.vendor. Business justification: Dynamic pricing engines (e.g., Digonex, Qcue) are third-party vendors under contract. Linking enables vendor SLA compliance tracking for pricing accuracy, contract renewal decisions, and audit trails ']
  venue_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the venue whose ticket inventory is governed by this pricing rule. Enables venue-level yield management across all events hosted at that facility.']
  activation_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time after which this pricing rule ceases to execute. Defines the closing boundary of the rule\'s activation window. Null for open-ended rules. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  activation_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time from which this pricing rule becomes eligible to execute. Defines the opening boundary of the rule\'s activation window. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  adjustment_direction varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the rule can only increase prices, only decrease prices, or move in either direction based on demand signals. \'bidirectional\' rules are used in fully automated yield management.']
  adjustment_method varchar [note: 'Mechanism by which the price adjustment is calculated: \'percentage\' = adjust by a percentage of the current price; \'fixed_amount\' = add or subtract a fixed currency amount; \'multiplier\' = multiply the base price by a factor.']
  adjustment_value decimal(10,4) [note: 'The numeric magnitude of the price adjustment. Interpretation depends on adjustment_method: for \'percentage\' this is the percent (e.g., 15.00 = 15%); for \'fixed_amount\' this is the currency delta; for \'multiplier\' this is the factor (e.g., 1.25). Classified confidential as it represents proprietary pricing strategy.']
  approval_status varchar [note: 'Governance approval state of the pricing rule. Rules must be approved by the yield management team before activation. Supports SOX financial controls and internal audit requirements.']
  approval_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the pricing rule received formal approval from the yield management authority. Part of the SOX-compliant audit trail for financial controls. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  base_price decimal(10,2) [note: 'The reference starting price from which dynamic adjustments are calculated. Typically the face value or published price for the ticket tier before any dynamic adjustment is applied.']
  ceiling_price decimal(10,2) [note: 'Maximum allowable ticket price for this rule. The dynamic pricing engine will never increase the ticket price above this bound, managing fan experience and regulatory price-gouging considerations. Classified confidential as proprietary pricing strategy.']
  competitor_price_offset_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The percentage above or below the competitor benchmark price at which this rule targets ticket pricing. Positive = price above competitor; negative = price below. Classified confidential as proprietary competitive strategy.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this dynamic pricing rule record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to all monetary values in this rule (floor_price, ceiling_price, base_price, adjustment_value when fixed_amount). Supports multi-currency global market operations.']
  demand_threshold_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The inventory sold-through percentage that must be reached before this demand-based rule activates. For example, 75.00 means the rule fires when 75% of allocated inventory is sold. Applicable when rule_type = \'demand_based\' or \'inventory_threshold\'.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which this pricing rule first becomes binding for yield management operations. Used for season-level planning and financial forecasting in Workday Adaptive Planning.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which this pricing rule expires and is no longer applicable. Null for perpetual rules. Supports season-end rule lifecycle management.']
  external_rule_reference varchar [note: 'The native rule identifier from the source system (Ticketmaster, AXS, or Archtics) that corresponds to this record. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse Silver Layer and operational ticketing systems.']
  floor_price decimal(10,2) [note: 'Minimum allowable ticket price for this rule. The dynamic pricing engine will never reduce the ticket price below this bound, protecting revenue floor commitments. Classified confidential as proprietary pricing strategy.']
  inventory_allocation_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The percentage of total ticket inventory for the applicable tier/event that is subject to this dynamic pricing rule. Allows partial inventory to be dynamically priced while the remainder is held at fixed price.']
  is_event_override boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this rule is an event-specific override that supersedes standard dynamic pricing rules for a particular event. True = override rule; False = standard rule. Supports playoff, championship, and special event pricing exceptions.']
  is_resale_applicable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this dynamic pricing rule also applies to resale/secondary market ticket listings managed through the official resale marketplace. True = rule governs resale pricing; False = primary market only.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this dynamic pricing rule record was most recently updated. Tracks rule configuration changes for audit and compliance purposes. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  max_adjustment_pct_per_trigger decimal(5,2) [note: 'The maximum percentage change allowed in a single rule trigger event. Caps runaway price movements from a single demand spike. For example, 20.00 means no single trigger can move the price more than 20%.']
  max_adjustments_per_day varchar [note: 'Maximum number of times this rule may trigger a price change within a single calendar day. Prevents excessive price volatility that could damage fan trust and brand perception.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for yield managers to capture contextual notes, business rationale, or exception documentation related to this pricing rule. Supports operational knowledge management and audit review.']
  priority_rank varchar [note: 'Numeric priority order for rule execution when multiple dynamic pricing rules apply to the same ticket inventory simultaneously. Lower integer = higher priority. Prevents conflicting rule outcomes.']
  rule_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the pricing rule, used in Ticketmaster/AXS and Archtics integrations for rule traceability and audit. Format: DPR- followed by 4–12 uppercase alphanumeric characters.']
  rule_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative explaining the business intent, trigger conditions, and expected outcome of the pricing rule. Supports governance documentation and audit review.']
  rule_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable descriptive name for the pricing rule (e.g., \'NBA Finals Demand Surge – Floor Level VIP\', \'Last-72hr Time Decay – GA\'). Used by yield managers for identification and reporting.']
  rule_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the pricing rule. \'draft\' = under configuration; \'active\' = live and executing adjustments; \'paused\' = temporarily suspended; \'expired\' = past effective window; \'cancelled\' = permanently deactivated.']
  rule_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the pricing algorithm driving this rule. \'demand_based\' = adjusts price based on real-time demand signals; \'time_to_event\' = adjusts based on days/hours until event; \'competitor_benchmark\' = adjusts relative to competitor pricing; \'inventory_threshold\' = triggers on remaining inventory levels; \'manual_override\' = yield manager-initiated adjustment.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Operational system of record from which this pricing rule originated or is mastered. Supports data lineage tracking across Ticketmaster, AXS, and Archtics integrations in the Silver Layer.']
  ticket_category varchar [note: 'Ticket inventory category to which this rule applies: General Admission (GA), Very Important Person (VIP), Standing Room Only (SRO), season package, or group sales. Enables tier-specific yield management strategies.']
  time_to_event_hours varchar [note: 'Number of hours before the event start time at which this time-based pricing rule activates. For example, 72 means the rule fires 72 hours before the event. Applicable when rule_type = \'time_to_event\'.']

  Note: 'Business rules governing real-time dynamic pricing adjustments for ticket inventory. Captures demand signals, floor/ceiling price bounds, adjustment algorithms (demand-based, time-to-event, competitor benchmarking), activation windows, and event-specific overrides. Enables yield management across GA/VIP/SRO tiers.'
}

  payment_reference varchar [note: 'The tokenized or masked payment transaction reference number from the payment processor for the resale purchase. Stored in compliance with PCI-DSS tokenization requirements — no raw card data is stored.']
  platform_fee_amount decimal(12,2) [note: 'The fee charged by the marketplace platform (e.g., Ticketmaster, AXS) for facilitating the resale transaction. Deducted from the sale price before calculating seller proceeds.']
  price_uplift_pct decimal(7,4) [note: 'The percentage by which the sale_price exceeds the original_face_value, calculated as ((sale_price - original_face_value) / original_face_value) * 100. Used for anti-scalping compliance monitoring and dynamic pricing analytics.']
  revenue_share_amount decimal(12,2) [note: 'The portion of the resale sale price allocated back to the league, team, or rights holder per the applicable revenue share agreement. Calculated based on revenue_share_rate applied to the sale price.']
  revenue_share_rate decimal(5,4) [note: 'The contractual percentage rate (expressed as a decimal, e.g., 0.0500 = 5%) applied to the sale price to calculate the revenue_share_amount owed to the rights holder. Sourced from the applicable league or team revenue share agreement.']
  sale_price decimal(12,2) [note: 'The final price at which the ticket was sold on the secondary market. May differ from listing_price due to dynamic pricing adjustments or negotiated changes. Populated only when lifecycle_status is \'sold\'.']
  seat_number varchar [note: 'The individual seat number within the row for the resale ticket. Sourced from Archtics. Required for access control validation and buyer-facing listing accuracy.']
  seat_row varchar [note: 'The row designation within the section for the resale ticket (e.g., \'A\', \'12\'). Sourced from Archtics. Provides granular seat location for buyer transparency and pricing validation.']
  seat_section varchar [note: 'The venue section designation of the resale ticket (e.g., \'Lower Bowl\', \'101\', \'VIP Club\'). Sourced from Archtics venue seating inventory. Used for pricing tier validation and buyer-facing listing display.']
  seller_proceeds decimal(12,2) [note: 'Net amount remitted to the seller after deducting platform fees and any applicable revenue share from the sale price. Represents the seller\'s actual payout for the transaction.']
  seller_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the seller entity: season_ticket_holder (STH reselling allocated seats), individual_fan (casual reseller), broker (licensed ticket broker), corporate_account (business account holder). Drives anti-scalping rule applicability and revenue share tiers.']
  source_system_listing_code varchar [note: 'The native listing identifier from the originating marketplace system (Ticketmaster, AXS, or other platform). Enables reconciliation between the Silver layer resale record and the operational source system record.']
  ticket_tier varchar [note: 'The pricing and access tier of the resale ticket: GA (General Admission), VIP (Very Important Person), SRO (Standing Room Only), premium, or standard. Drives anti-scalping cap thresholds and revenue share tier applicability.']
  transaction_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the resale transaction was executed (purchase completed or transfer accepted). This is the principal business event timestamp for sold and transferred records. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  transfer_restriction_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the original ticket carried a transfer restriction (e.g., non-transferable VIP package, restricted season ticket). True = transfer restrictions applied; False = no restrictions. Used to validate eligibility for resale or transfer.']
  transfer_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when a peer-to-peer ticket transfer (gift or forward) was completed and the new entitlement was issued to the recipient. Distinct from transaction_timestamp which applies to commercial sales. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this resale lifecycle record was last modified in the Silver layer data product. Tracks status transitions, price updates, and entitlement token changes. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']

  Note: 'Unified lifecycle record for all secondary market and peer-to-peer ticket activity. Captures listing creation (price, channel, seller type, listing status), marketplace transaction execution (sale price, platform fees, seller proceeds, buyer reference), and peer-to-peer transfers (gift, forward). Tracks movement type, transfer timestamp, new entitlement token issuance, transfer restrictions, anti-scalping rule compliance, and revenue share calculations. SSOT for all secondary market listings, resale transactions, and fan-to-fan ticket transfers. Replaces separate listing and transaction records with a single lifecycle entity progressing through states: listed → sold/transferred/expired/withdrawn.'
}
