  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the payment transaction (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, CAD). Supports multi-currency operations across global markets and SAP S/4HANA FI foreign currency revaluation.']
  discount_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Total monetary discount applied to the payment, including promotional codes, group sales discounts, season ticket holder discounts, and sponsor-funded promotions. Used for revenue leakage analysis and promotion ROI reporting.']
  exchange_rate decimal(18,6) [note: 'The foreign exchange rate applied at the time of payment when the transaction currency differs from the organization\'s functional currency (USD). Used for multi-currency financial reporting and SAP S/4HANA FI currency revaluation. Null for transactions in the functional currency.']
  failure_reason_code varchar [note: 'Standardized decline or failure code returned by the payment processor or card network when a payment is not authorized (e.g., insufficient_funds, card_expired, do_not_honor, fraud_suspected). Used for failed payment analysis, retry logic, and fan communication. Null for successful transactions.']
  failure_reason_description varchar [note: 'Human-readable description of the payment failure reason corresponding to the failure_reason_code. Used by customer service teams in Salesforce CRM for fan outreach and dispute resolution. Null for successful transactions.']
  fraud_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Numeric fraud risk score assigned by the payment processor\'s fraud detection engine or an internal fraud scoring model at the time of payment (0.00–100.00, where higher values indicate greater fraud risk). Used for real-time payment decisioning, fraud trend analysis, and PCI-DSS fraud monitoring requirements.']
  gross_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'The total face value of the ticket order before any discounts, promotions, or adjustments are applied. Represents the base revenue figure used in financial reporting and EBITDA calculations in SAP S/4HANA FI.']
  installment_number varchar [note: 'The sequential installment number for recurring or installment-based payments (e.g., 1 of 4 for a season ticket payment plan). Null for one-time payments. Used for installment plan tracking and revenue recognition scheduling.']
  installment_total_count varchar [note: 'The total number of installments in the payment plan for season ticket or group sales installment arrangements (e.g., 4 for a quarterly payment plan). Null for one-time payments. Used alongside installment_number for plan completion tracking.']
  is_3ds_authenticated boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the payment was authenticated using 3D Secure (3DS) protocol (e.g., Visa Secure, Mastercard Identity Check). True if 3DS authentication was completed. Used for fraud liability shift determination and PCI-DSS compliance reporting.']
  is_recurring boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this payment is part of a recurring payment arrangement, such as a season ticket installment plan or subscription-based fan membership. True for recurring charges. Drives card-on-file compliance and CBA-related payment plan management.']
  masked_card_reference varchar [note: 'Masked representation of the payment card number or digital wallet identifier (e.g., last 4 digits of card, masked wallet token). Stored in PCI-DSS compliant masked format for customer service, receipt display, and dispute identification without exposing full PAN.']
  net_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'The final net amount charged to the fan after applying discounts and adding service fees and taxes (gross_amount - discount_amount + service_fee_amount + tax_amount). This is the actual amount captured from the fan\'s payment instrument. SSOT for revenue recognition.']
  payment_channel varchar [note: 'The interface or touchpoint through which the fan submitted the payment (e.g., web browser, mobile app, venue box office, self-service kiosk, call center, third-party resale platform). Distinct from payment method type; used for channel analytics and fraud detection.']
  payment_method_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the payment instrument used by the fan (e.g., credit card, debit card, digital wallet such as Apple Pay/Google Pay, bank transfer, gift card, cash at box office). Drives PCI-DSS scope determination and payment processing routing.']
  payment_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes or comments associated with the payment transaction, entered by customer service agents or system processes (e.g., manual override justification, special handling instructions for VIP fan payments, dispute context). Used in Salesforce CRM case management.']
  payment_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable payment reference number assigned by the payment processor or ticketing platform (e.g., Ticketmaster/AXS transaction reference). Used for customer-facing receipts, dispute resolution, and reconciliation with external systems.']
  payment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the payment transaction. Tracks the workflow from authorization through capture, failure, or refund. Critical for revenue recognition, reconciliation, and PCI-DSS compliance reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: authorized|captured|failed|refunded|voided|pending — promote to reference product if additional states are required]']
  pci_scope_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this payment record falls within the PCI-DSS cardholder data environment (CDE) scope. True for card-based payments subject to PCI-DSS controls. Used for PCI-DSS scope boundary management, audit reporting, and data classification governance.']
  processor_transaction_token varchar [note: 'Tokenized reference assigned by the payment processor to uniquely identify this transaction within the processor\'s system. Replaces raw card data per PCI-DSS tokenization requirements. Used for refund initiation, dispute management, and settlement reconciliation.']
  refund_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Total amount refunded to the fan for this payment transaction, applicable when payment_status is \'refunded\'. May be a partial or full refund. Used for revenue reversal accounting in SAP S/4HANA FI and fan satisfaction tracking.']
  refund_reason varchar [note: 'Categorized reason for the refund when payment_status is \'refunded\'. Supports refund trend analysis, event cancellation financial impact reporting, and fraud detection. Null for non-refunded transactions.']
  refunded_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the refund was processed and submitted to the payment processor. Null for non-refunded transactions. Used for refund SLA monitoring and fan experience reporting.']
  service_fee_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Ticketing service and convenience fees charged to the fan on top of the ticket face value (e.g., Ticketmaster facility charge, order processing fee). Reported separately for revenue transparency and regulatory compliance.']
  settlement_date date [note: 'The date on which the payment was settled by the acquiring bank and funds were transferred to the organization\'s account. Critical for cash flow reporting, SAP S/4HANA FI bank reconciliation, and revenue recognition timing.']
  settlement_reference varchar [note: 'The batch settlement reference number assigned by the payment processor or acquiring bank when the transaction is included in a settlement batch. Used for bank reconciliation, SAP S/4HANA FI bank statement matching, and financial close processes.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Identifies the originating operational system that generated this payment record (e.g., Ticketmaster, AXS, Archtics box office, resale marketplace). Used for data lineage tracking, system reconciliation, and Silver layer provenance in the Databricks Lakehouse.']
  tax_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Total tax amount applied to the ticket payment, including applicable sales tax, VAT, or entertainment tax based on the venue jurisdiction. Required for tax remittance reporting and SAP S/4HANA FI tax accounting.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this payment record was last modified (e.g., status change from authorized to captured, or refund applied). Supports change data capture, audit trails, and Silver layer incremental processing.']
  wallet_provider varchar [note: 'Name of the digital wallet provider used for payment when payment_method_type is digital_wallet (e.g., Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Venmo). Null for non-wallet payment methods. Supports DTC fan engagement analytics and wallet adoption reporting.']

  Note: 'PCI-DSS compliant payment transaction record associated with a ticket order. Captures payment method type, masked card/wallet reference, payment processor token, authorization code, amount charged, currency, payment status (authorized, captured, failed, refunded), and settlement reference. SSOT for ticketing payment financial records.'
}

  league_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the league or governing body associated with the waitlisted event or package (e.g., NFL, NBA, MLS). Supports cross-league demand analytics and league-specific waitlist governance rules.']
  price_tier_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific price tier or seating tier the fan has requested on the waitlist (e.g., VIP, GA, premium suite). Drives offer matching and dynamic pricing signals.']
  requested_seating_section_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to venue.seating_section. Business justification: Waitlist management for specific sections requires linking to the canonical seating_section for capacity availability checks, ADA accommodation matching, and STH renewal priority processing. Role-pref']
  season_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the league season associated with the waitlist request. Applicable for STH package waitlists and season-scoped event waitlists. Supports season-over-season demand trend analysis.']
  season_ticket_package_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the season ticket package (STH) for which the fan is waitlisted. Populated when the waitlist type is for a season ticket holder package rather than a single event.']
  team_franchise_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the home team associated with the waitlisted event or season package. Enables team-level demand reporting and capacity planning for franchise operations.']
  ticket_order_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the ticket order created when the fan converted their waitlist offer into a purchase. Links the waitlist record to the resulting transaction for revenue attribution and lifecycle tracking.']
  upgraded_from_waitlist_id varchar [note: 'Self-referencing FK on waitlist (upgraded_from_waitlist_id)']
  venue_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the venue associated with the waitlisted product. Used for venue-specific capacity planning and seating inventory management via Archtics.']
  cancellation_reason_code varchar [note: 'Coded reason for removal from the waitlist when status is \'cancelled\', \'expired\', or \'withdrawn\'. Supports demand analytics and queue management reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fan_withdrawn|offer_expired|operator_removed|duplicate|ineligible|event_cancelled — promote to reference product if additional codes are needed]']
  conversion_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the fan successfully converted the waitlist offer into a confirmed ticket purchase. Null if not yet converted. Used for conversion rate analytics and demand signal reporting.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this waitlist record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and Silver layer ingestion tracking.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to the price floor and ceiling values (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Supports multi-currency operations across global markets.']
  demand_signal_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this waitlist record has been included in the demand signal feed used by the dynamic pricing engine. Active waitlist entries contribute to demand pressure metrics that influence dynamic pricing rule triggers.']
  gdpr_consent_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the fan provided explicit GDPR consent for processing their personal data as part of the waitlist registration. Mandatory for EU-based fans. Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform consent management.']

  is_priority_override boolean [note: 'Indicates whether an operator has manually overridden the fan\'s queue position or priority rank outside of the standard algorithmic ranking. Supports audit trail for queue management decisions.']

  notification_preference varchar [note: 'Fan\'s preferred channel for receiving waitlist offer notifications. Drives outbound communication routing through Adobe Experience Platform and Salesforce CRM. Options: email, SMS, push notification, or combinations.']
  offer_count varchar [note: 'Total number of ticket offers that have been extended to this fan for this waitlist entry. Tracks repeat offer cycles where a fan declines or allows an offer to expire and is re-queued.']
  offer_expiry_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time by which the fan must accept and complete purchase of the offered tickets before the offer lapses and inventory is released to the next fan in queue. Critical for revenue recovery and queue throughput.']
  offer_extended_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when a ticket offer was formally extended to the fan from the waitlist. Marks the transition from \'active\' to \'offered\' status. Null if no offer has been made yet.']
  price_ceiling decimal(10,2) [note: 'Maximum ticket price the fan is willing to pay for the waitlisted product. Offers exceeding this threshold are not extended. Critical for demand segmentation and willingness-to-pay analytics.']
  price_floor decimal(10,2) [note: 'Minimum ticket price the fan is willing to accept for the waitlisted product. Used in dynamic pricing offer matching — offers below this threshold are not extended. Supports demand signaling for dynamic pricing models.']
  priority_override_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text explanation for why a manual priority override was applied to this waitlist record. Populated only when is_priority_override is True. Required for audit compliance.']
  priority_rank varchar [note: 'Business-assigned priority rank that may differ from raw queue position. Reflects STH loyalty tier, tenure, or operator-assigned priority overrides. Lower value = higher priority. Used for STH waitlists often 5,000+ deep at major franchises.']
  queue_position varchar [note: 'Current ordinal position of the fan in the waitlist queue. Recalculated dynamically as fans ahead convert, withdraw, or are removed. Position 1 is next in line for an offer.']
  registration_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time when the fan registered for the waitlist. This is the principal business event timestamp used to establish queue ordering and priority rank. Sourced from Ticketmaster/AXS or Archtics at point of registration.']
  requested_quantity varchar [note: 'Number of tickets the fan is requesting through the waitlist. Drives inventory matching logic — an offer is only extended when the requested quantity becomes available contiguously.']
  requested_seat_row varchar [note: 'Preferred row within the requested section. Optional granular seating preference used for premium upgrade waitlists and STH package matching.']
  requested_seat_section varchar [note: 'Specific seating section the fan has requested on the waitlist (e.g., \'Section 101\', \'Club Level\'). Optional preference used for offer matching in Archtics seating inventory.']
  sales_channel varchar [note: 'Channel through which the fan registered for the waitlist. Used for channel attribution analytics and fan engagement reporting. Sourced from Ticketmaster/AXS or Adobe Experience Platform.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational system of record from which this waitlist entry originated. Supports multi-system ingestion lineage in the Databricks Silver layer.']
  source_system_waitlist_code varchar [note: 'Original waitlist identifier from the operational source system (Ticketmaster, AXS, or Archtics). Preserved for lineage tracing, reconciliation, and cross-system deduplication in the Silver layer.']
  sth_loyalty_tier varchar [note: 'Loyalty tier of the fan at the time of waitlist registration. Higher tiers receive elevated priority rank in STH package waitlists. Sourced from Salesforce CRM loyalty program data.']
  sth_tenure_years varchar [note: 'Number of consecutive years the fan has held or previously held a season ticket. Used as a priority factor in STH waitlist ranking — longer tenure earns higher queue priority per league governance policies.']
  waitlist_number varchar [note: 'Human-readable, externally-visible reference number assigned to the waitlist registration. Used in fan communications, CRM records, and Ticketmaster/AXS correspondence.']
  waitlist_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the waitlist record. \'active\' = fan is queued; \'offered\' = ticket offer has been extended; \'converted\' = fan purchased; \'expired\' = offer window lapsed; \'cancelled\' = removed by operator; \'withdrawn\' = fan self-removed.']
  waitlist_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the waitlist request by product type. Distinguishes between single-event sold-out demand, Season Ticket Holder (STH) package waitlists, premium seating upgrades, suite requests, and group sales queues.']

  Note: 'Queue management record for fans seeking ticket access to sold-out events, season ticket packages, or premium seating upgrades. Captures fan reference, requested product (single event, STH package, suite), priority rank, registration timestamp, queue position, notification preferences, conversion status, and offer expiry. Supports season ticket holder waitlist management (often 5,000+ deep at major franchises), sold-out event demand capture, and premium upgrade queues. Enables demand signaling for dynamic pricing and capacity planning.'
}

  transfer_direction varchar [note: 'Indicates the directional nature of the transfer relative to the originating account. \'outbound\' — sender is giving away the ticket; \'inbound\' — recipient is receiving; \'return\' — ticket returned to original holder after a prior transfer.']
  transfer_method varchar [note: 'Channel or mechanism used to deliver the transfer invitation to the recipient. \'mobile_app\' — in-app transfer via Ticketmaster/AXS mobile; \'email\' — transfer link sent via email; \'sms\' — transfer link sent via SMS; \'platform_link\' — shareable URL generated for transfer.']
  transfer_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-visible alphanumeric reference number assigned to the transfer transaction, used for fan-facing communication, customer service lookup, and audit trail. Sourced from Ticketmaster/AXS transfer workflow.']
  transfer_restriction_reason varchar [note: 'Reason code explaining why a transfer was restricted or blocked. \'none\' — no restriction; \'price_tier_restricted\' — price tier does not permit transfer; \'event_restricted\' — event-level transfer lockout; \'package_restricted\' — season ticket package terms prohibit transfer; \'compliance_hold\' — regulatory or compliance hold; \'fraud_hold\' — fraud risk flag applied.']
  transfer_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the ticket transfer. \'pending\' — transfer initiated, awaiting recipient acceptance; \'accepted\' — recipient accepted and entitlement re-issued; \'declined\' — recipient declined; \'cancelled\' — sender cancelled before acceptance; \'expired\' — acceptance window elapsed; \'revoked\' — transfer voided by operator or compliance action.']
  transfer_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the transfer by business context. \'standard\' — ad hoc peer-to-peer transfer; \'season_ticket_forward\' — STH forwarding a game ticket; \'group_forward\' — group sale ticket forwarded to individual attendee; \'comp_forward\' — complimentary ticket forwarded by recipient.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this transfer record was last modified in the data platform. Used for incremental data processing, change detection, and audit trail maintenance.']

  Note: 'Peer-to-peer ticket transfer records between fan accounts — capturing sender, recipient, transfer method (mobile, email), transfer timestamp, and terms acceptance.'
}

Table ticketing.presale_access {
  presale_access_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the presale_access association']
  fan_segment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the fan segment that is granted access to this hold allocation']
  hold_allocation_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the hold allocation block to which this segment access entitlement applies']
  allocation_quantity varchar [note: 'Number of tickets from the parent hold allocation reserved for exclusive or priority access by this fan segment. Cannot live on hold_allocation (one record per block, not per segment) nor on fan_segment (a reference master with no event-specific inventory data).']
  conversion_rate decimal [note: 'Post-sale metric expressing the percentage of this segment\'s allocated quantity that was actually purchased during the presale window. Computed at the segment-allocation level and used for future presale sizing decisions. Cannot live on hold_allocation (aggregates across all segments) nor on fan_segment (aggregates across all events).']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this segment access entitlement was first created in the system, recording when the ticketing team granted this segment access to the hold block.']
  eligibility_group_code varchar [note: 'Structured code identifying the fan segment, loyalty tier, or partner group eligible for this hold (e.g., \'SEASON_HOLDER\', \'FAN_CLUB_GOLD\', \'SPONSOR_GUEST\'). Enables programmatic eligibility enforcement and CRM-driven targeting via Salesforce CRM and Adobe Experience Platform. [Moved from hold_allocation: This field on hold_allocation is a single-value text code that attempts to capture the fan segment or loyalty group eligible for the hold. In the true M:N model, multiple segments can be entitled to the same hold allocation, each with their own priority and quantity. The eligibility_group_code becomes redundant and misleading once the presale_access association table exists — segment identity is now captured via the FK to fan_segment. The field should be deprecated from hold_allocation and replaced by the association records.]']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this presale access record was last updated, supporting audit and change tracking for inventory management operations.']
  presale_access_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of this segment\'s access entitlement against the hold allocation. Tracks whether the access grant is active, expired, released, or consumed.']
  priority_rank varchar [note: 'Ordinal rank determining the access priority order when multiple fan segments are entitled to the same hold allocation. Lower values indicate higher priority. Belongs to the relationship because priority is relative to the specific hold block, not an intrinsic property of the segment or the hold.']
  quantity_consumed varchar [note: 'Number of tickets from this segment\'s allocation that have been purchased or issued during the presale window. Enables per-segment consumption tracking distinct from the hold-level quantity_consumed aggregate.']
  window_end timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the presale window closes specifically for this fan segment against this hold allocation. Unallocated quantity after this time may be released or reassigned per hold release rules.']
  window_start timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the presale window opens specifically for this fan segment against this hold allocation. May override the hold-level presale_window_start to provide staggered or segment-specific access timing. Belongs to the relationship because different segments on the same hold may have different window schedules.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Presale Access contract between a hold_allocation and a fan_segment. It captures the operational grant of access rights that a specific fan segment holds against a specific ticket inventory block, including the quantity allocated to that segment, its priority rank among competing segments, any segment-specific presale window overrides, and post-sale conversion performance. Each record links one hold_allocation to one fan_segment with attributes that exist only in the context of this per-segment access entitlement and cannot be stored on either parent entity.. Existence Justification: In sports entertainment operations, a presale hold allocation is deliberately made accessible to multiple fan segments simultaneously — for example, a sponsor comp block may be opened to both \'Season Ticket Holders\' and \'Credit Card Partner Members\' with different priority ranks and quantities per segment. Conversely, a single fan segment (e.g., \'High-Value Loyalists\') can have access to multiple hold allocations across different events and hold types throughout a season. The business actively manages these per-segment access grants as operational records, tracking allocation quantities, priority ordering, presale window overrides, and post-sale conversion rates for each segment-allocation pairing.'
}

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: digital|analog|IP|satellite|cable|terrestrial|fiber|microwave — promote to reference product]']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational system of record from which this channel record was originated or last updated (e.g., DALET for Dalet Galaxy MAM, SALESFORCE for Salesforce CRM). Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and Silver layer provenance tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.']
  stream_url varchar [note: 'Primary ingest or origin stream URL for OTT, IPTV, or DTC channel types. Confidential as it represents a direct access endpoint to live feed infrastructure. Used by broadcast operations and CDN configuration teams.']
  subscriber_count varchar [note: 'Current number of active subscribers or authorized viewers for this channel. For OTT/DTC/IPTV channels, reflects platform subscription count. For linear channels, reflects reported household reach. Used for ARPU (Average Revenue Per User) calculation and rights fee negotiations.']
  time_zone varchar [note: 'IANA time zone identifier for the channel\'s primary broadcast schedule reference (e.g., \'America/New_York\', \'Europe/London\'). Used for EPG scheduling, live event timing, and blackout rule time-window enforcement.']
  uptime_sla_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Contractually committed uptime percentage for this channel as defined in the SLA (Service Level Agreement) with the platform operator or CDN provider (e.g., 99.95). Used for operational performance monitoring and penalty clause management.']

Captures channel name, type (linear/OTT/IPTV/DTC), platform operator, geographic coverage, language, resolution tier (SD/HD/4K), and active status.'
}

Table broadcast.broadcast_drm_policy {
  broadcast_drm_policy_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for a Digital Rights Management (DRM) policy record governing content protection and playback restrictions across OTT, IPTV, and DTC streaming platforms.']
  parent_policy_broadcast_drm_policy_id varchar [note: 'Reference to a parent DRM policy from which this policy inherits base settings. Supports hierarchical policy structures where sport-specific or event-specific policies extend a master DRM policy template.']

  approved_by varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the rights management or legal authority who approved this DRM policy for production deployment. Supports governance and audit trail requirements for IP protection compliance.']
  approved_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this DRM policy was formally approved for production use. Distinct from created_timestamp; captures the approval lifecycle event for governance and audit purposes.']
  blackout_rule_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether local or regional blackout rules are enforced under this DRM policy. Blackout rules restrict live event streaming in local broadcast markets to protect RSN and linear TV rights agreements.']
  cdn_profile_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the CDN delivery profile associated with this DRM policy. CDN profiles define token authentication, signed URL parameters, and edge caching rules that complement DRM enforcement.']
  compliance_standard varchar [note: 'Regulatory or industry compliance standard that this DRM policy is designed to satisfy (e.g., \'GDPR\', \'CCPA\', \'PCI-DSS\', \'FCC\'). Supports compliance reporting and audit trail requirements for content protection governance.']
  concurrent_stream_limit varchar [note: 'Maximum number of simultaneous active streams permitted per subscriber entitlement under this DRM policy. Enforced at the CDN and streaming platform level to prevent credential sharing and protect media rights revenue.']
  content_tier varchar [note: 'Content access tier to which this DRM policy applies, aligning with subscription or entitlement levels. VIP tiers may include exclusive live events or athlete content; PPV tiers apply to pay-per-view events such as UFC or boxing matches.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this DRM policy record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance reporting. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  device_authentication_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether device-level authentication and registration is required before DRM license issuance. When true, only registered and authenticated devices may receive license keys for protected content.']
  download_permitted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether offline download of protected content is permitted under this DRM policy. When true, download-to-own or rental download workflows are enabled subject to license expiry rules.']
  drm_technology varchar [note: 'The DRM technology stack applied to enforce content protection. Widevine is used for Android/Chrome, FairPlay for Apple devices, PlayReady for Microsoft/Smart TVs, and multi_drm indicates a combined approach for cross-platform delivery.']
  effective_from date [note: 'Date from which this DRM policy becomes active and enforceable on streaming platforms. Aligns with the start of the associated media rights agreement or broadcast season.']
  effective_until date [note: 'Date on which this DRM policy expires and is no longer enforceable. Null for open-ended policies. Aligns with the expiry of the associated media rights agreement.']
  encryption_standard varchar [note: 'Cryptographic encryption standard applied to protected content streams. AES-128 and AES-256 are common for HLS, CENC (Common Encryption) is used for DASH multi-DRM, and CBCS is the Apple FairPlay encryption scheme.']
  geo_blocked_territories varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes explicitly blocked from content playback under this DRM policy. Supports blackout rules for RSN exclusivity and international rights restrictions.']
  geo_permitted_territories varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes (e.g., \'USA,CAN,GBR\') where content playback is permitted under this DRM policy. Used to enforce broadcast rights territorial restrictions for RSN, OTT, and DTC platforms.']
  geo_restriction_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether geographic access restrictions are enforced under this DRM policy. When true, content playback is limited to permitted territories defined in the geo_permitted_territories and geo_blocked_territories fields.']
  hdcp_version_required varchar [note: 'Minimum HDCP version required on the display output for content playback under this DRM policy. HDCP 2.2 or higher is typically required for 4K UHD premium sports content.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this DRM policy record was last updated. Tracks policy changes for audit, compliance, and version control purposes. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  license_duration_hours varchar [note: 'Duration in hours for which a DRM license key is valid after issuance to a device. After expiry, the device must re-request a license from the license server. Controls content access windows for rental and PPV models.']
  license_renewal_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the DRM license must be renewed (re-fetched from the license server) during active playback sessions. When true, the player must periodically contact the license server to maintain uninterrupted playback.']
  license_server_url varchar [note: 'HTTPS endpoint URL of the DRM license server responsible for issuing and validating license keys for content governed by this policy. Must use HTTPS. Configured per DRM technology (Widevine, FairPlay, PlayReady).']
  max_registered_devices varchar [note: 'Maximum number of devices a subscriber may register for DRM license delivery under this policy. Limits credential sharing and protects media rights revenue across OTT and DTC platforms.']
  offline_playback_duration_hours varchar [note: 'Maximum number of hours a downloaded content item may be played back offline before the DRM license expires and re-authentication is required. Null when download is not permitted.']
  output_protection_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether HDCP (High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection) or equivalent output protection is required on connected display outputs. Enforced for premium and PPV content to prevent unauthorized recording.']
  platform_type varchar [note: 'Delivery platform category to which this DRM policy applies. OTT (Over-The-Top), IPTV (Internet Protocol Television), DTC (Direct-To-Consumer), linear TV broadcast, mobile app, or web browser. Determines applicable DRM technology and encryption requirements.']
  policy_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the DRM policy, used in rights agreements, vendor contracts, and system integrations with Dalet Galaxy and CDN platforms. Format: DRM- followed by 4-20 uppercase alphanumeric characters.']
  policy_description varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the DRM policy\'s purpose, scope, and any special enforcement conditions. Used by rights management and broadcast operations teams for policy governance and documentation.']
  policy_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the DRM policy used for identification in broadcast operations, rights management workflows, and reporting dashboards (e.g., \'NFL Sunday Ticket PPV Standard\', \'OTT Premium Tier FairPlay\').']
  policy_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the DRM policy. Active policies are enforced on streaming platforms; deprecated policies are retained for historical audit and compliance purposes.']
  policy_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the DRM policy by monetization model: subscription (SVOD), pay-per-view (PPV), rental (TVOD), download-to-own (EST), free ad-supported (AVOD), or preview. Drives entitlement logic and revenue reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: subscription|ppv|rental|download_to_own|free_ad_supported|preview — promote to reference product]']
  policy_version varchar [note: 'Version number of the DRM policy definition, following semantic versioning (e.g., \'1.0\', \'2.1.3\'). Enables tracking of policy changes over time and supports rollback in case of compliance issues.']
  resolution_restriction varchar [note: 'Maximum video resolution permitted for playback under this DRM policy. Resolution restrictions may be applied based on device capability, subscription tier, or rights agreement terms (e.g., SD-only for non-authenticated devices).']
  rights_agreement_ref varchar [note: 'External reference code or contract number of the media rights agreement that mandates this DRM policy. Links DRM enforcement requirements back to the contractual obligation with leagues (NFL, NBA, FIFA) or broadcast partners.']
  rights_window_type varchar [note: 'Type of content rights window governed by this DRM policy: live (real-time broadcast), VOD (video on demand), replay (post-event catch-up), archive (long-term library), or preview (short promotional clip). Determines applicable DRM enforcement rules.']
  robustness_level varchar [note: 'Widevine/PlayReady robustness level required for license issuance, defining the security tier of the decryption environment. HW_SECURE_ALL requires hardware-level TEE (Trusted Execution Environment) and is mandated for 4K UHD premium sports content.']
  screen_capture_blocked boolean [note: 'Indicates whether screen capture and screen recording are blocked on supported platforms under this DRM policy. Enforced via OS-level DRM APIs on Android (Widevine) and iOS (FairPlay) to prevent unauthorized content capture.']
  token_auth_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a signed authentication token (e.g., JWT) is required when requesting a DRM license. Token authentication prevents unauthorized license acquisition and is standard for premium and PPV content.']
  token_expiry_seconds varchar [note: 'Duration in seconds after which the authentication token used for DRM license requests expires. Short expiry windows reduce the risk of token replay attacks on premium sports content.']
  watermark_type varchar [note: 'Type of watermarking applied to protected content: forensic (invisible, embedded in bitstream for piracy tracing), visible (on-screen overlay), both, or none. Forensic watermarking is standard for live PPV and premium sports events.']
  watermarking_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether forensic or visible watermarking must be applied to content streams under this DRM policy. Watermarking enables source tracing of unauthorized redistribution and piracy detection.']

  Note: 'Digital Rights Management policy definitions governing content protection, encryption standards, device authentication, and playback restrictions for OTT, IPTV, and DTC streaming platforms. Captures DRM technology (Widevine, FairPlay, PlayReady), content tier, geo-restriction rules, concurrent stream limits, download permissions, and watermarking requirements. Ensures IP protection and rights compliance.'
}

  encoding_format varchar [note: 'Video codec standard used to compress and encode the live feed signal. H.264 (AVC) and H.265 (HEVC) are the dominant standards for broadcast and OTT (Over-The-Top) streaming delivery. Impacts bandwidth, quality, and platform compatibility.']
  failover_activated boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the backup or redundancy failover mechanism was triggered during this live feed\'s transmission. Used for post-event incident analysis, SLA (Service Level Agreement) reporting, and broadcast reliability KPI (Key Performance Indicator) tracking.']
  failover_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time (UTC) when the failover mechanism was activated for this live feed. Null if failover_activated is false. Used for incident root cause analysis and SLA (Service Level Agreement) breach assessment.']
  feed_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this live feed within broadcast operations and Dalet Galaxy media asset management workflows. Used for signal routing, scheduling, and inter-system reference.']
  feed_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable descriptive name for the live feed, typically including event name, feed type, and language (e.g., \'NFL Championship - World Feed - English\'). Used in operational dashboards and scheduling systems.']
  feed_status varchar [note: 'Current operational lifecycle status of the live feed. Active indicates the feed is live and distributing; standby is ready but not transmitting; failed indicates a signal loss or error condition; backup indicates a redundancy feed has taken over; scheduled indicates pre-event readiness; terminated indicates the feed has ended.']
  feed_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the live feed by its production and distribution purpose. World feed is the primary international signal; clean feed has no graphics; ISO feed is an isolated camera angle; PPV (Pay-Per-View) and OTT (Over-The-Top) feeds are platform-specific variants. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: world_feed|clean_feed|commentary_feed|iso_feed|backup_feed|ppv_feed|ott_feed — promote to reference product]']
  frame_rate decimal(5,2) [note: 'Number of video frames per second (fps) for this live feed. Common values include 25, 29.97, 50, 59.94, and 60 fps. Affects motion smoothness, storage requirements, and compatibility with broadcast standards across regions (PAL vs NTSC).']
  hdr_format varchar [note: 'High Dynamic Range (HDR) format applied to the live feed for enhanced color and brightness reproduction. HDR10 and HLG (Hybrid Log-Gamma) are the broadcast standards; Dolby Vision is a premium streaming format. None indicates standard dynamic range (SDR).']
  is_iptv_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this live feed is authorized and configured for distribution via IPTV (Internet Protocol Television) networks, including managed IPTV services provided by telecommunications operators.']
  is_linear_tv_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this live feed is authorized and configured for distribution via traditional linear television broadcast channels, including RSN (Regional Sports Network) and national broadcast network affiliates.']
  is_ott_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this live feed is authorized and technically configured for distribution via OTT (Over-The-Top) streaming platforms, including DTC (Direct-To-Consumer) services and third-party streaming partners.']
  is_ppv boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this live feed is designated as a PPV (Pay-Per-View) event feed, requiring consumer purchase or entitlement before access is granted. Drives entitlement checks on DTC (Direct-To-Consumer) and OTT (Over-The-Top) platforms.']
  latency_mode varchar [note: 'Configured latency mode for this live feed delivery. Ultra-low latency (sub-3 seconds) is required for interactive and betting-adjacent use cases; low latency (3-10 seconds) for OTT (Over-The-Top) sports streaming; standard (10-30 seconds) for traditional broadcast; high for archive-quality delivery.']
  ob_unit_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the Outside Broadcast (OB) truck or mobile production unit assigned to capture and produce this live feed at the source venue. Critical for resource scheduling and operational accountability.']
  production_region varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the primary production region where this live feed is originated and managed. Used for regulatory compliance, rights territory management, and broadcast operations routing.']
  redundancy_config varchar [note: 'Redundancy architecture configured for this live feed to ensure continuity in case of primary signal failure. 1+1 means one active and one standby path; N+1 means N active feeds with one shared backup. Critical for broadcast SLA (Service Level Agreement) compliance.']
  replay_enabled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this live feed is authorized and configured to generate replay or catch-up content after the live event concludes. Drives post-event content ingest workflows in Dalet Galaxy and DRM (Digital Rights Management) policy application for replay windows.']
  replay_window_hours varchar [note: 'Number of hours after the live event ends during which replay content derived from this feed is available to authorized viewers. Defined by the media rights agreement and DRM (Digital Rights Management) policy. Null if replay_enabled is false.']
  resolution varchar [note: 'Video resolution tier of the live feed. SD (Standard Definition) is 480p/576p; HD (High Definition) is 720p; FHD (Full HD) is 1080p/1080i; 4K is 2160p; 8K is 4320p. Determines bandwidth requirements, CDN (Content Delivery Network) capacity planning, and platform delivery eligibility.']
  scheduled_start_time timestamp [note: 'Planned date and time (UTC) when this live feed is scheduled to begin transmission. Used for broadcast scheduling, CDN (Content Delivery Network) pre-warming, and OB (Outside Broadcast) unit coordination.']
  signal_type varchar [note: 'Physical or logical transport medium used to carry the live feed signal from the source venue to the broadcast facility or CDN (Content Delivery Network) origin. Determines redundancy planning and SLA (Service Level Agreement) requirements.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time (UTC) when this live feed record was most recently modified. Tracks operational changes such as status transitions, failover events, and configuration updates throughout the feed lifecycle.']

  Note: 'Operational record of each live broadcast feed produced and distributed for a scheduled event. Captures source venue, OB (Outside Broadcast) unit assignment, signal type (satellite, fiber, IP), encoding format (H.264/H.265), resolution (SD/HD/4K/8K), audio tracks, commentary language, feed status (active, standby, failed, backup), CDN origin endpoint, and redundancy configuration. Core operational entity for live broadcast production, distribution monitoring, and failover management.'
}

  content_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the nature of the content covered by this rights window. Distinguishes live broadcast rights from replay, highlight, documentary, PPV event, and magazine show rights, each carrying different fee structures and DRM policies.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this rights window record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under SOX financial controls and GDPR data lineage obligations.']
  effective_from date [note: 'The calendar date from which this rights window record is considered valid for business use. Supports slowly changing dimension (SCD) patterns on the Silver Layer and enables point-in-time rights queries.']
  effective_until date [note: 'The calendar date until which this rights window record is considered valid. Nullable for currently active records. Supports SCD Type 2 history management on the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  exclusivity_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the rights granted in this window are exclusive to the licensee within the defined territory and platform. True = exclusive; False = non-exclusive. Exclusive windows command premium rights fees and restrict sublicensing.']
  language_code varchar [note: 'ISO 639-1/639-2 language code specifying the language in which the content may be broadcast under this rights window (e.g., \'en\', \'es\', \'fr\'). Supports multi-language rights management for global markets.']
  max_broadcast_count varchar [note: 'The maximum number of times the content may be broadcast under this rights window. Null indicates unlimited broadcasts within the window period. Enforced by the DRM and broadcast scheduling systems.']
  min_lead_time_hours varchar [note: 'The minimum number of hours before the scheduled broadcast that the licensee must notify the rights holder or activate the content feed. Supports SLA (Service Level Agreement) compliance and OB (Outside Broadcast) logistics.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for capturing additional contractual conditions, special provisions, or operational notes associated with this rights window that are not captured in structured fields (e.g., specific event carve-outs, force majeure clauses).']
  payment_schedule_type varchar [note: 'Defines the payment cadence for the rights fee associated with this window. Drives accounts receivable scheduling in SAP S/4HANA and cash flow forecasting in Workday Adaptive Planning.']
  resolution_tier varchar [note: 'The maximum video resolution permitted for broadcast under this rights window (SD, HD, 4K, 8K). Higher resolution tiers typically command premium rights fees and require specific CDN and DRM capabilities.']
  revenue_share_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The percentage of broadcast revenue (e.g., subscription, PPV, advertising) that the licensee must remit to the rights holder under this window. Drives financial settlement and EBITDA reporting.']
  rights_category varchar [note: 'Broad classification of the rights type granted in this window. Distinguishes domestic broadcast rights from international, digital, mobile, radio, PPV (Pay-Per-View), and archive rights. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: domestic|international|digital|mobile|radio|ppv|archive — promote to reference product]']
  rights_conflict_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a rights conflict has been detected for this window (e.g., overlapping exclusivity with another window for the same content, platform, and territory). Triggers review workflow in the rights management system.']
  rights_fee_allocation_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The percentage of the total parent deal rights fee allocated to this specific window. Enables proportional revenue recognition and financial reporting across multiple windows derived from a single deal.']
  rights_fee_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The monetary value of the rights fee allocated to this specific window from the parent rights deal. Represents the portion of the total deal value attributable to this platform-territory-period combination. Used for revenue recognition and financial reporting.']
  rights_fee_currency varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the rights fee amount (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Required for multi-currency rights deals across global markets.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational system of record from which this rights window record was ingested (e.g., \'DALET_GALAXY\', \'SAP_SD\', \'SALESFORCE_CRM\'). Supports data lineage tracking on the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  sublicensing_permitted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the licensee is contractually permitted to sublicense the broadcast rights to third parties within this window. Drives downstream rights conflict detection and IP (Intellectual Property) protection enforcement.']
  territory_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code identifying the geographic territory in which this rights window is valid. Drives blackout rule enforcement and geo-restriction logic at the CDN layer.']
  territory_scope varchar [note: 'Indicates the geographic breadth of the rights window beyond a single country code. Supports multi-territory deal structures where a single window covers a defined group of markets.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this rights window record was last modified. Supports change data capture (CDC) pipelines on the Databricks Silver Layer and audit trail requirements under SOX.']
  window_end timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (exclusive) after which the licensee\'s broadcast rights under this window expire. Nullable for perpetual or open-ended windows. Critical for automated rights expiry enforcement.']
  window_reference_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for this rights window, used in contracts, invoices, and rights management systems. Enables cross-system reconciliation with SAP S/4HANA and Dalet Galaxy.']
  window_start timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (inclusive) from which the licensee is permitted to broadcast content under this rights window. Used for real-time rights enforcement at the CDN and DRM layer.']
  window_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the broadcast rights window. Drives rights enforcement logic: only \'active\' windows permit broadcast. Transitions follow deal negotiation and regulatory approval workflows.']

  Note: 'Granular rights window records derived from media rights deals, defining the specific time periods, platforms, and territories in which a rights holder may broadcast specific content. Captures rights deal reference, content category, platform type, territory, window start/end, exclusivity flag, sublicensing permission, and rights fee allocation. Enables precise rights enforcement at the content-platform-territory level.'
}

  broadcast_date date [note: 'Calendar date of the broadcast window in yyyy-MM-dd format. Used for day-level scheduling analysis, weekly ratings aggregation, and contractual audience guarantee reconciliation.']
  content_genre varchar [note: 'Genre classification of the broadcast content (e.g., Live Sport, Sports News, Sports Documentary, Concert, Esports, Magazine Show). Used for scheduling optimization and audience segmentation analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Live Sport|Sports News|Sports Documentary|Concert|Esports|Magazine Show|Highlights|Other — promote to reference product]']
  cpm_rate decimal(10,4) [note: 'Cost Per Mille — the advertising rate charged per 1,000 viewers for this broadcast window, in the applicable currency. Used for advertiser rate card justification and media rights deal valuation. Confidential as it reflects negotiated commercial pricing.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this audience rating record was first ingested into the Silver Layer data product. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and SLA (Service Level Agreement) compliance for measurement data delivery.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to the CPM rate and any monetary values in this record (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR, AUD). Required for multi-territory rights valuation and financial reporting.']
  demo_age_band varchar [note: 'Age band of the primary target demographic for this audience measurement record. Standard age groupings used by Nielsen and BARB for advertiser targeting and rate card segmentation (e.g., Adults 18-49 is the primary US broadcast demographic).']
  demo_gender varchar [note: 'Gender segment of the audience demographic breakdown for this measurement record. Used for targeted advertising rate card differentiation and sponsor demographic guarantee reporting.']
  demo_income_band varchar [note: 'Household income band of the measured audience segment (e.g., Under $50K, $50K-$100K, $100K-$150K, $150K+). Used for premium advertiser targeting and sponsorship package valuation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Under $50K|$50K-$100K|$100K-$150K|$150K-$200K|$200K+ — promote to reference product]']
  demo_viewers_count varchar [note: 'Number of viewers within the specific demographic segment (age band, gender, income band) defined for this record. Enables granular demographic reporting for advertiser guarantee reconciliation.']
  drm_protected boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the broadcast content was delivered with DRM (Digital Rights Management) protection active during the measurement window. Relevant for OTT and IPTV platform compliance and piracy impact assessment on audience figures.']
  frequency decimal(8,3) [note: 'Average number of times a unique viewer was exposed to the broadcast during the measurement period. Used alongside reach to calculate GRP (Gross Rating Point) and assess advertising campaign effectiveness.']
  grp_value decimal(10,3) [note: 'Gross Rating Point value for this broadcast window, representing the sum of ratings across the target audience. Calculated as rating_pct multiplied by frequency. Primary currency for advertising inventory pricing and sponsorship valuation.']
  guarantee_met boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the actual audience (total_viewers) met or exceeded the contractual audience guarantee target for this broadcast window. Drives make-good advertising inventory decisions and rights agreement penalty calculations.']
  live_viewers varchar [note: 'Number of viewers who watched the broadcast in real-time (live) as opposed to time-shifted. Distinguishes live audience from time-shifted for PPV event reporting and live sports rights valuation.']
  market_name varchar [note: 'Name of the designated market area (DMA) or broadcast market within the territory (e.g., New York DMA, London ITV Region, Sydney Metro). Used for sub-national audience reporting and RSN rate card justification.']
  measurement_methodology varchar [note: 'The data collection methodology used by the measurement source. Panel-based (Nielsen People Meter, BARB panel) uses a representative sample; Census measures all streams; Hybrid combines panel and census; Modeled uses statistical estimation; Self-Reported uses platform-provided data.']
  measurement_reference_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique identifier assigned by the measurement provider (e.g., Nielsen panel ID, BARB survey code, OzTAM report reference, Comscore stream ID) for cross-system reconciliation.']
  measurement_source varchar [note: 'The third-party or internal system that provided the audience measurement data. Determines methodology, panel composition, and credibility for advertiser and rights negotiations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Nielsen|BARB|OzTAM|Comscore|Internal Streaming Analytics|Other — promote to reference product if additional sources are onboarded]']
  measurement_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the audience rating record. Preliminary ratings are released within 24 hours; confirmed ratings are validated by the measurement provider; revised ratings incorporate late-reported data; final ratings are locked for contractual use; disputed ratings are under review.']
  peak_concurrent_viewers varchar [note: 'Maximum number of viewers simultaneously watching the broadcast at any single minute during the window. Key metric for streaming platform capacity planning, CDN (Content Delivery Network) provisioning, and PPV event valuation.']
  rating_pct decimal(6,3) [note: 'Percentage of the total universe of TV households or individuals that watched the broadcast, regardless of whether their TV was on. Distinct from share_pct which is based only on those actively viewing. Used for GRP (Gross Rating Point) calculation.']
  rating_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the audience measurement metric captured in this record. GRP (Gross Rating Point) represents total delivery; CPM (Cost Per Mille) supports advertiser rate card justification; Reach measures unique audience; Frequency measures average exposures; AMA (Average Minute Audience) is the standard linear TV metric; Share is the percentage of viewing universe. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GRP|CPM|Reach|Frequency|Viewership|AMA|Share — promote to reference product]']
  reach varchar [note: 'Total number of unique individuals who viewed at least one minute of the broadcast during the measured window. Distinct from total_viewers which may count repeat viewing. Used for unduplicated audience reporting to sponsors and rights holders.']
  reporting_period_type varchar [note: 'Defines the time-shifted viewing window included in this measurement record per Nielsen and BARB standards. Live = real-time only; Live+1 includes same-day DVR; Live+3 includes 3-day playback; Live+7 includes 7-day playback; Live+35 is the C35 standard; VOD is on-demand only.']
  share_pct decimal(6,3) [note: 'Percentage of the total viewing universe (all households/individuals with TV/streaming access) that watched this broadcast during the window. Expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 12.500 = 12.5%). Core metric for competitive scheduling analysis.']
  sport_type varchar [note: 'The sport or entertainment category of the broadcast content (e.g., NFL Football, NBA Basketball, FIFA Soccer, UFC MMA, Concert). Enables sport-specific audience trend analysis and rights valuation benchmarking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NFL Football|NBA Basketball|MLB Baseball|NHL Hockey|MLS Soccer|FIFA Soccer|UFC MMA|Tennis|Concert|Other — promote to reference product]']
  territory_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code identifying the geographic territory in which the audience measurement was conducted. Critical for regional rights valuation, blackout rule enforcement, and RSN (Regional Sports Network) reporting.']
  time_shifted_viewers varchar [note: 'Number of viewers who watched the broadcast on a time-shifted basis (DVR, catch-up, VOD replay) within the measurement window. Reported separately per Nielsen Live+3 and Live+7 standards for contractual audience guarantee reconciliation.']
  total_viewers varchar [note: 'Total number of individual viewers who watched the broadcast during the measured window. The primary headline metric used in media rights negotiations, advertiser rate cards, and contractual audience guarantees.']
  universe_size varchar [note: 'Total size of the viewing universe (total TV households or individuals) used as the denominator for rating_pct and share_pct calculations in the given territory and demographic. Provided by the measurement source.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this audience rating record was last modified, typically when preliminary ratings are revised or confirmed by the measurement provider. Supports audit trail and revised-rating reconciliation workflows.']
  window_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the measured broadcast window ended. Combined with window_start_timestamp to define the exact measurement interval for AMA and share calculations.']
  window_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the measured broadcast window began, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Used as the principal business event timestamp for scheduling optimization and rights valuation.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of broadcast audience measurement data per scheduled broadcast window. Captures channel, territory, measurement source (Nielsen, BARB, OzTAM, Comscore, internal streaming analytics), rating type (GRP, CPM, reach, frequency, viewership), total viewers, demographic breakdown (age, gender, income), peak concurrent viewers, average minute audience (AMA), share percentage, and time-shifted viewing. Operational data used for rights valuation, advertiser rate card justification, scheduling optimization, and contractual audience guarantee reconciliation.'
}

  royalty_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the royalty calculation methodology as defined in the rights agreement. Determines how the royalty amount is computed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: flat_fee|revenue_share|per_subscriber|per_view|minimum_guarantee|overage — promote to reference product]']

Table broadcast.rights_agreement {
  rights_agreement_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the broadcast_rights_agreement association']
  broadcast_channel_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this rights agreement to the specific broadcast channel authorized to carry the league content.']
  league_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this rights agreement to the specific league whose content is being distributed under this agreement.']
  media_rights_deal_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to broadcast.media_rights_deal. Business justification: Rights agreements (association between channel and league) are typically derived from or implement underlying media rights deals. Adding media_rights_deal_id enables tracking which master deal governs']
  broadcast_rights_tier varchar [note: 'Classification of the league\'s broadcast rights value tier, used to categorize RSN (Regional Sports Network), national, and OTT (Over-The-Top Streaming) rights packaging. Drives revenue forecasting, CPM rate card setting, and DTC platform strategy. [Moved from league: The league-level broadcast_rights_tier is a summary/default classification, but the actual rights tier is per-channel-per-league agreement and varies by channel, territory, and exclusivity. The authoritative value belongs on the association as rights_tier. The league-level attribute may be retained as a summary/default but should not be the system of record.]']
  effective_from date [note: 'Calendar date on which this channel-league broadcast rights agreement becomes active and the channel is authorized to distribute league content. Belongs to the agreement, not to either entity alone.']
  effective_until date [note: 'Calendar date on which this channel-league broadcast rights agreement expires or is scheduled to terminate. Drives rights window enforcement, blackout logic, and renewal workflows.']
  exclusivity_type varchar [note: 'Defines whether this channel holds exclusive rights to broadcast the league within the agreed territory and window, or whether other channels may simultaneously carry the same content. A core contractual term that belongs to the agreement itself.']
  primary_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this channel is the primary (flagship) broadcast partner for this league within the agreed territory. A league may have multiple channels but only one primary partner per territory. Belongs to the agreement, not to the channel or league independently.']
  rights_tier varchar [note: 'Classification of the broadcast rights value tier for this specific channel-league agreement. Determines revenue sharing, production obligations, and promotional commitments. Belongs to the agreement, not to the channel or league independently.']
  rights_window_end date [note: 'End date of the current media rights window during which this channel is authorized to distribute content. Nullable for perpetual or open-ended rights. Critical for rights expiry alerting and contract renewal workflows. [Moved from channel: Same reasoning as rights_window_start — the per-league rights expiry belongs on the association as effective_until, not as a single value on the channel master record.]']
  rights_window_start date [note: 'Start date of the current media rights window during which this channel is authorized to distribute content. Aligns with the rights agreement effective period. Used for rights compliance monitoring and revenue recognition. [Moved from channel: This attribute on the channel represents a channel-level default rights window, but the operationally meaningful rights window is per-channel-per-league agreement. The per-agreement effective_from on the association supersedes this. If the channel has a single global rights window independent of any league, it may remain on the channel; however, if it was intended to capture league-specific rights start dates, it belongs on the association as effective_from.]']
  territory_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code or structured region code defining the geographic territory within which this channel is authorized to broadcast the league under this agreement. Distinct from the channel\'s general geographic_coverage — this is the rights-specific territory.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between a broadcast channel and a league governing the rights to distribute league content. It captures the operational terms of each channel-league broadcast rights deal — including rights tier, exclusivity, territory, and effective dates — that exist only in the context of this specific channel-league pairing. Each record is a discrete, actively managed rights agreement that the business creates, renegotiates, and terminates as part of its media rights operations.. Existence Justification: In sports entertainment, a single broadcast channel (e.g., ESPN) simultaneously carries multiple leagues (NFL, NBA, MLB), and a single league (e.g., NFL) is distributed across multiple channels (ESPN, Fox, NBC, CBS) under distinct rights agreements. The business actively manages these channel-league broadcast rights relationships as named contracts with their own attributes — rights tier, exclusivity type, territory, and effective dates — that belong to neither the channel nor the league alone. This is a genuine operational M:N where rights deals are created, renegotiated, and terminated as discrete business events.'
}

Table broadcast.platform_rights_grant {
  platform_rights_grant_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the platform_rights_grant association']
  broadcast_rights_window_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to broadcast.broadcast_rights_window. Business justification: Platform rights grants (linking media_rights_deal to digital_touchpoint) may be scoped to specific broadcast rights windows for granular rights management. Adding broadcast_rights_window_id enables tr']
  digital_touchpoint_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the digital touchpoint authorized to deliver content under the rights deal.']
  media_rights_deal_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the media rights deal that grants the platform-level rights authorization.']
  effective_from date [note: 'The date on which this platform-level rights authorization becomes active. May differ from the parent deal\'s effective_date if the touchpoint was added mid-deal.']
  effective_until date [note: 'The date on which this platform-level rights authorization expires. May differ from the parent deal\'s expiry_date if the touchpoint authorization is terminated early.']
  exclusivity_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the rights granted to this specific digital touchpoint are exclusive within the deal\'s territory scope. Exclusivity may differ per touchpoint even within the same deal.']
  grant_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this platform rights authorization. Allows rights operations to suspend or terminate a specific touchpoint\'s authorization without affecting the parent deal or other touchpoint grants.']
  platform_rights_type varchar [note: 'The category of rights granted to this specific digital touchpoint under this deal (e.g., live streaming, replay, highlights). A deal may grant live rights to the OTT app but only highlights rights to the web portal.']
  revenue_share_pct decimal [note: 'The revenue share percentage applicable to content delivered through this specific digital touchpoint under this deal. Per-platform revenue share terms may differ from the deal-level revenue_share_pct on the parent media_rights_deal.']
  territory_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 territory code specifying the geographic scope of the rights grant for this specific touchpoint. A deal covering multiple territories may authorize different touchpoints per territory.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between media_rights_deal and digital_touchpoint. It captures the formal authorization granting a specific digital touchpoint the right to deliver content under a specific media rights deal, including the platform-level rights type, exclusivity terms, effective period, territory scope, and revenue share applicable to that specific deal-touchpoint combination. Each record links one media_rights_deal to one digital_touchpoint with attributes that exist only in the context of this per-platform rights authorization.. Existence Justification: A media rights deal licenses content delivery rights to multiple digital touchpoints simultaneously (e.g., an NFL deal may cover the OTT app, web portal, and IPTV endpoint under different terms), and each digital touchpoint can be covered by multiple rights deals across different sports, leagues, and territories. The business actively manages which touchpoints are authorized to deliver which rights, with per-touchpoint exclusivity flags, territory scopes, and revenue share terms that belong neither to the deal nor the touchpoint alone. This is a recognized operational concept in broadcast rights licensing — the authorization or \'platform rights grant\' — that rights operations teams create, update, and enforce.'
}

Business justification: Rights window channel authorizations enforce DRM policies for content protection. The authorization currently has drm_policy_code (STRING) but should reference the broadcast_drm_policy table for full ']
  broadcast_rights_window_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the broadcast rights window that grants the distribution authorization']
  platform_channel_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the platform channel authorized to distribute content under this rights window']
  authorization_end timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this channel authorization expires. May align with or precede the parent rights window end, supporting early termination of a specific channel\'s authorization without affecting the broader window.']
  authorization_start timestamp [note: 'The date and time from which this channel authorization is effective. May align with or be a subset of the parent rights window start, allowing phased channel rollouts within a single rights window.']
  authorization_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of this specific channel authorization. Drives whether the platform channel is permitted to distribute content under this rights window at any given moment.']
  concurrent_stream_limit varchar [note: 'Maximum number of simultaneous streams permitted on this platform channel under this specific rights window. This is a per-authorization term that may differ from the channel\'s default concurrent_stream_limit, representing negotiated terms for this window-channel combination. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']
  exclusivity_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the rights granted under this window are exclusive to this specific platform channel. Belongs to the authorization record because exclusivity is a per-channel-window term, not a property of the window or channel alone. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']
  platform_type varchar [note: 'The distribution platform category for which this rights window is valid. Distinguishes between linear TV, OTT (Over-The-Top Streaming), IPTV (Internet Protocol Television), PPV (Pay-Per-View), DTC (Direct-To-Consumer), RSN (Regional Sports Network), digital streaming, and radio. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear_tv|ott|iptv|ppv|dtc|rsn|digital_streaming|radio — promote to reference product] [Moved from broadcast_rights_window: platform_type on broadcast_rights_window is a string classification (e.g., \'OTT\', \'IPTV\') that was used as a proxy for channel targeting in the absence of a proper association table. With the rights_window_channel_authorization in place, the specific platform channel is identified via FK to platform_channel, making the string-based platform_type on the window redundant for routing purposes. However, platform_type may be retained on broadcast_rights_window as a broad classification of the intended platform class for the window overall — this is a judgment call for the rights operations team.]']
  territory_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code defining the geographic territory in which this specific channel is authorized under this rights window. May differ from the window-level territory scope when sub-territorial authorizations are issued. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between broadcast_rights_window and platform_channel. It captures the formal authorization record that grants a specific platform channel the right to distribute content under a specific broadcast rights window, including the technical compliance terms, exclusivity scope, DRM requirements, and stream limits that govern that specific channel-window combination. Each record links one broadcast_rights_window to one platform_channel with attributes that exist only in the context of this authorization relationship.. Existence Justification: In sports media rights operations, a single broadcast rights window (e.g., \'NFL Sunday Ticket, OTT, USA, 2024-2025\') is actively distributed across multiple platform channels simultaneously — an OTT app, an IPTV portal, and a DTC streaming endpoint may all be authorized under the same window. Conversely, a platform channel like ESPN+ carries content from dozens of distinct rights windows covering different leagues, territories, and time periods. Rights operations teams actively manage which channels are authorized under which windows, with per-combination terms such as exclusivity scope, DRM policy, and concurrent stream limits that belong to neither entity alone.'
}

  rofr_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the sponsor holds a Right of First Refusal (ROFR) on the renewal of this deal term, giving them priority to match any competing offer before the rights are offered to a third party. True = ROFR granted; False = no ROFR.']
  sap_billing_plan_type varchar [note: 'The SAP S/4HANA SD billing plan type code assigned to this deal term, controlling how and when invoices are generated (e.g., \'01\' for milestone billing, \'02\' for periodic billing). Directly maps to SAP billing plan configuration.']
  sap_contract_number varchar [note: 'The SAP S/4HANA SD sales contract document number associated with this deal term, used for billing plan integration, invoice generation, and revenue recognition. Enables traceability between the lakehouse Silver Layer and the ERP system of record.']
  signed_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which this deal term was formally executed and signed by all parties. Represents the principal business event timestamp for the contractual commitment. Used for SOX revenue recognition cutoff and audit trail.']
  term_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric reference code for this deal term record, used in SAP S/4HANA SD billing and contract correspondence. Format: <ORG_CODE>-DT-<SEQUENCE>.']
  term_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the deal term. Draft indicates terms under negotiation; active indicates binding and in-force; suspended indicates temporarily paused (e.g., force majeure); terminated indicates early exit via kill clause; expired indicates natural end-of-term; pending_renewal indicates renewal option under evaluation.']
  term_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the deal term by its commercial nature. Financial covers cash payment obligations; activation covers brand activation deliverables; naming_rights covers venue or event naming; broadcast_integration covers in-broadcast placements; digital_platform covers OTT/DTC digital integrations; jersey_sponsorship covers kit branding rights. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: financial|activation|naming_rights|broadcast_integration|digital_platform|jersey_sponsorship|merchandise_licensing|hospitality — promote to reference product]']
  total_contract_fee decimal(18,2) [note: 'Gross total monetary value of this deal term over its full effective period, expressed in the contract currency.   vik_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The portion of the total contract fee fulfilled through non-cash Value-in-Kind (VIK) contributions such as goods, services, media inventory, or hospitality provided by the sponsor. Tracked separately from cash for accounting and ROI analysis.']
