  picks_completed varchar [note: 'Running count of pick selections that have been exercised and confirmed during the draft event, used for real-time progress tracking and broadcast production.']
  salary_cap_year varchar [note: 'The salary cap fiscal year applicable to rookie contracts signed by athletes selected in this draft, governing rookie wage scale calculations and cap hit projections.']
  sport varchar [note: 'The professional sport discipline governed by this draft event, used to apply sport-specific eligibility rules, CBA provisions, and draft format configurations.']
  start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time at which the draft event officially begins (first pick clock starts), used for broadcast scheduling, OTT streaming activation, and real-time pick tracking.']
  supplemental_draft boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this draft event is a supplemental draft (True) rather than the primary annual draft (False), used for athletes who became eligible after the standard draft deadline.']
  total_picks varchar [note: 'Total number of pick slots in this draft event, including standard picks, compensatory picks, and supplemental picks as authorized by the governing league.']

  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this draft event record was most recently modified in the league governance system, supporting change tracking, audit compliance, and Silver layer delta processing.']
  wada_compliance_confirmed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether all athletes in the eligible draft class have been confirmed compliant with WADA anti-doping regulations prior to the draft event commencing.']
  year varchar [note: 'Calendar year in which the draft event takes place, used as the primary temporal classification for draft class cohort analysis and future pick valuation.']

  Note: 'Master record for a league player draft event and all individual pick selections. At the pick level: round number, overall pick number, current owning franchise, original owning franchise (if traded), full trade history chain, compensatory/conditional pick flags, pick protection level (top-N protected), pick status (available, traded, exercised, forfeited, voided), and selected athlete reference upon exercise. Supports draft asset management, trade analysis, and future pick valuation models.'
}

Table league.draft_pick {
  draft_pick_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each individual draft pick record within the league draft management system. Primary key for the draft_pick entity.']
  athlete_profile_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the athlete selected with this pick upon exercise. Null until the pick is exercised. Links to the athlete profile for post-draft roster and contract management.']
  broadcast_segment_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the broadcast production segment associated with the announcement of this pick. Supports content production, OTT/RSN distribution, and DAM workflows.']
  draft_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent draft event to which this pick belongs (e.g., 2024 NFL Draft, 2024 NBA Draft). Links the pick to its governing draft event.']
  last_trade_transaction_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the most recent trade transaction record in which this pick was transferred. Enables full trade audit trail linkage.']
  league_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the professional league (NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, MLS, FIFA, etc.) that governs this draft pick and its associated rules.']
  primary_draft_current_owner_franchise_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the franchise that currently holds the rights to exercise this draft pick. May differ from the original owning franchise if the pick has been traded.']
  season_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the league season associated with this draft pick. Links the pick to the competitive season calendar for standings-based draft order determination.']
  selected_athlete_athlete_profile_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the athlete selected with this pick upon exercise. Null until the pick is exercised. Links to the athlete profile for post-draft roster and contract management.']
  cba_compliance_status varchar [note: 'Current CBA compliance status of this draft pick record. \'compliant\' = meets all CBA requirements; \'under_review\' = pending league review; \'violation\' = CBA rule breach identified; \'waived\' = compliance requirement formally waived by league.']
  competitive_integrity_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this pick has been flagged for competitive integrity review by the league office (e.g., suspected tanking, collusion, or improper trade). Triggers compliance investigation workflow.']
  condition_description varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the conditions governing a conditional pick (e.g., \'Converts to 1st round if franchise wins division; otherwise 2nd round\'). Populated only when is_conditional is true.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp at which this draft pick record was first created in the system, including timezone offset. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.']
  draft_position_tier varchar [note: 'Categorical tier classification of this pick\'s position within the draft (e.g., \'lottery\' for NBA lottery picks, \'top_10\', \'first_round\', \'second_round\', \'later_round\'). Used for pick valuation segmentation and trade analysis.']
  draft_year varchar [note: 'The calendar year of the draft event in which this pick is to be exercised. Critical for future pick tracking and multi-year trade asset management.']
  exercise_date date [note: 'The date on which this pick was exercised (i.e., used to select an athlete during the draft event). Null until the pick is exercised.']
  exercise_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time at which this pick was exercised during the draft event, including timezone offset. Supports real-time draft broadcast and pick clock compliance tracking.']
  external_ref varchar [note: 'The externally-known identifier for this pick as published by the league office or official transaction systems (e.g., league transaction ID, official pick number code). Supports system-of-record reconciliation.']
  forfeiture_reason varchar [note: 'Description of the reason this pick was forfeited, if applicable (e.g., salary cap violation, tampering penalty, CBA non-compliance). Populated only when pick_status is \'forfeited\'.']
  forfeiture_ruling_date date [note: 'The date on which the league office issued the ruling to forfeit this pick. Populated only when pick_status is \'forfeited\'.']
  is_compensatory_pick boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this pick was awarded as a compensatory pick by the league office (e.g., NFL compensatory picks for lost free agents). Compensatory picks are subject to special trade restrictions in some leagues.']
  is_conditional boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this pick is subject to conditions that may alter its round, year, or validity (e.g., \'becomes a 1st round pick if team makes playoffs\'). When true, condition_description provides the governing terms.']
  is_lottery_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this pick is eligible to be determined by a lottery mechanism (e.g., NBA Draft Lottery). Relevant for protected pick valuation and conditional pick resolution.']
  is_tradeable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this pick is currently eligible to be traded under league rules. Some picks (e.g., compensatory picks in certain leagues, picks under CBA restrictions) may be non-tradeable.']
  last_trade_date date [note: 'The date on which this pick was most recently traded to its current owning franchise. Null if the pick has never been traded.']
  pick_announcement_name varchar [note: 'The official name announced for this pick during the draft broadcast (e.g., \'The Dallas Cowboys select...\'). Used for broadcast production, content, and DAM (Digital Asset Management) workflows.']
  pick_clock_seconds_remaining varchar [note: 'The number of seconds remaining on the pick clock when the pick was submitted. Used for draft broadcast analytics and compliance with league pick clock rules.']
  pick_number varchar [note: 'The sequential overall pick number within the entire draft event (e.g., pick #1 through #259 in the NFL Draft). Used for pick valuation models and historical analysis.']
  pick_source_league_rule varchar [note: 'The specific league rule, CBA article, or governing provision under which this pick was created or awarded (e.g., \'CBA Article 5, Section 3 - Compensatory Pick Formula\', \'Expansion Draft Rule 12\'). Supports compliance and audit.']
  pick_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the draft pick. \'available\' = held and ready to use; \'traded\' = transferred to another franchise; \'exercised\' = used to select an athlete; \'forfeited\' = surrendered as penalty; \'voided\' = invalidated by league ruling.']
  pick_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the pick by its origin type. \'standard\' = regular draft order pick; \'compensatory\' = awarded by league for free agent losses; \'supplemental\' = mid-year supplemental draft; \'expansion\' = awarded to expansion franchise; \'traded\' = acquired via trade.']
  pick_valuation_score decimal(10,4) [note: 'Quantitative valuation score assigned to this pick based on the league\'s or franchise\'s draft pick value chart (e.g., NFL Jimmy Johnson Chart, Chase Stuart Chart). Used for trade analysis and asset management. Not a calculated aggregate — represents the chart-assigned value for this pick position.']
  pick_within_round varchar [note: 'The sequential pick number within the specific round (e.g., 3rd pick in Round 2). Combined with round_number provides the full pick address (e.g., Round 2, Pick 3).']
  protection_level varchar [note: 'The top-N protection threshold for this pick (e.g., 3 = top-3 protected, meaning if the pick falls in the top 3 overall, it does not convey to the trading partner and rolls over). Null if unprotected.']
  protection_rollover_year_limit varchar [note: 'The maximum number of years a protected pick can roll over before it must convey regardless of protection status. Governs the expiry of pick protection in multi-year trade agreements.']
  round_number varchar [note: 'The round within the draft event in which this pick falls (e.g., Round 1, Round 2, Round 7). Determines pick tier and associated contract slot values in CBA-governed leagues.']
  salary_cap_currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the salary cap slot value (e.g., USD for NFL/NBA/MLB/NHL, EUR for FIFA leagues). Supports multi-league and international operations.']
  salary_cap_slot_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'The CBA-mandated salary cap slot value associated with this pick position, expressed in the league\'s designated currency. Governs the rookie contract value for the selected athlete. Critical for salary cap compliance reporting.']
  trade_count varchar [note: 'Total number of times this pick has been traded between franchises. Used for trade complexity analysis and pick valuation models.']
  trade_history varchar [note: 'Serialized summary of the full trade chain for this pick, recording each franchise that has held the pick in sequence (e.g., \'FranchiseA → FranchiseB → FranchiseC\'). Supports trade analysis and pick provenance auditing.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp at which this draft pick record was most recently modified, including timezone offset. Supports change tracking, audit compliance, and silver layer incremental processing.']

  Note: 'Individual draft pick record within a draft event, tracking round number, overall pick number, current owning franchise, original owning franchise (if traded), full trade history chain, compensatory pick flag, conditional pick flag with conditions description, pick protection level (top-N protected), pick status (available, traded, exercised, forfeited, voided), and selected athlete reference upon exercise. Supports draft asset management, trade analysis, and future pick valuation models.'
}

  category_exclusivity_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator confirming whether the vendor holds exclusive rights within their product/service category for this league. TRUE means no competing vendor in the same category may hold official partner status with this league simultaneously.']
  end_date date [note: 'The contractual expiration date of the official partnership agreement. Used for renewal pipeline management, exclusivity expiry tracking, and procurement planning.']
  exclusivity_scope varchar [note: 'Defines the competitive exclusivity terms granted to the vendor within their product/service category for this league. Describes the scope of exclusivity (e.g., \'exclusive North America\', \'non-exclusive global\', \'exclusive broadcast technology category\').']
  official_designation varchar [note: 'The formal official title granted to the vendor by the league (e.g., \'Official Ball Supplier\', \'Official Timing Partner\', \'Official Apparel Partner\'). This designation is the core business artifact of the partnership and appears in marketing, broadcast, and licensing materials.']
  partnership_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the partnership agreement. Drives operational workflows including activation rights, payment schedules, and marketing usage permissions.']
  partnership_tier varchar [note: 'Tier classification of the official partnership indicating the strategic level and visibility of the vendor\'s association with the league. Drives sponsorship valuation, activation rights, and revenue recognition.']
  primary_broadcast_partner varchar [note: 'Name of the primary national or international broadcast rights holder for this league (e.g., \'ESPN/ABC\', \'NBC Sports\', \'Sky Sports\', \'beIN Sports\'). Used for rights management, content distribution planning, and sponsor activation. [Moved from league: This denormalized STRING attribute on the league master stores the name of the primary broadcast rights holder — a specific instance of a league-vendor partnership. The correct model is a record in league_partnership with official_designation = \'Official Broadcast Partner\' and category_exclusivity_flag = TRUE, linked via vendor_id to the vendor master. Storing a vendor name as a string on the league record violates normalization and creates a data quality risk when the broadcast partner changes. This attribute should be removed from league and replaced by a query against league_partnership filtered by official_designation category.]']
  start_date date [note: 'The contractual effective start date of the official partnership agreement between the league and the vendor. Used for partnership lifecycle management, renewal tracking, and financial accrual.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the official contracted Partnership between a league and a vendor. It captures the operational record of each league-vendor partnership agreement including designation category, exclusivity scope, financial terms, and partnership lifecycle dates. Each record links one league to one vendor and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this specific partnership relationship — not on the league or vendor master records alone.. Existence Justification: In professional sports entertainment, leagues actively manage official partnerships with vendors — the NFL has an official ball supplier (Wilson), an official timing partner (Daktronics), and an official apparel partner (Nike), while Nike simultaneously holds official partnerships with the NFL, NBA, and MLB. This is a genuine operational M:N relationship where the business creates, manages, and terminates partnership agreements that carry their own financial terms, exclusivity scopes, and official designation categories. The relationship is not derivable from transactional data — it is a first-class business contract that procurement and league operations teams actively govern.'
}

Table league.revenue_allocation {
  revenue_allocation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the revenue_allocation association']
  franchise_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the franchise that participates in or receives this revenue stream allocation.']
  revenue_stream_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the revenue stream classification record being allocated to this franchise.']
  allocation_pct decimal [note: 'The percentage of the total revenue stream amount allocated to this franchise for the given season. For league-wide streams (e.g., national broadcast), this reflects each franchise\'s contractual share.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'The calendar date from which this franchise-stream allocation record becomes contractually effective. Enables historical tracking of allocation changes over time.']
  effective_to_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which this franchise-stream allocation record expires or is superseded. A null value indicates the allocation is currently active.']
  revenue_category varchar [note: 'Classification of the revenue type for this allocation record, providing granular categorization at the franchise-stream intersection (e.g., local_broadcast, national_broadcast, gate_receipts, sponsorship, merchandise).']
  revenue_sharing_rate decimal [note: 'The contractually mandated revenue sharing rate applicable to this specific franchise-stream combination, which may differ from the stream-level default rate due to franchise tier or negotiated terms.']
  season_year varchar [note: 'The competitive season or fiscal year to which this franchise-stream allocation record applies. Allows tracking of allocation changes across seasons.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between franchise and revenue_stream. It captures the per-franchise, per-stream financial allocation record governing how each revenue stream is distributed to or generated by each franchise for a given season. Each record links one franchise to one revenue_stream with attributes — allocation percentage, revenue sharing rate, effective dates, and season year — that exist only in the context of this franchise-stream allocation agreement and cannot reside on either master entity alone.. Existence Justification: In sports entertainment, a franchise actively participates in multiple revenue streams simultaneously (local broadcast rights, gate receipts, sponsorship, merchandise, gaming) while each revenue stream (particularly national broadcast deals, league-wide sponsorships) is distributed across multiple franchises. The business explicitly tracks per-franchise-stream allocation percentages, revenue sharing rates, and effective date ranges — this is an operationally managed financial allocation record, not a derived analytical correlation. Finance and league operations teams actively create, update, and close these allocation records each season.'
}

Table league.crew_member_assignment {
  crew_member_assignment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the crew_member_assignment association']
  official_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the individual game official assigned to this crew']
  officiating_crew_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the officiating crew for the specific game']
  substituted_for_official_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the original official (official_id) whom this official replaced on this crew assignment. Null when substitution_flag is false. Supports substitution audit trail and workload adjustment calculations.']
  assignment_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which this individual official was formally assigned to this crew for this game. May differ from the crew-level assignment_date if officials are added or substituted after initial crew formation.']
  assignment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of this individual official\'s assignment to the crew. Tracks progression from initial proposal through conflict screening, confirmation, and post-game completion. Distinct from the crew-level assignment_status on officiating_crew.']
  conflict_of_interest_cleared boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this specific official has passed the conflict-of-interest screening for this game assignment. Per-official clearance is required in addition to the crew-level conflict_of_interest_cleared flag, as individual officials may have team-specific conflicts.']
  performance_score decimal [note: 'Composite numeric score (0.00–100.00) assigned to this individual official following post-game evaluation for this specific crew assignment. Distinct from the crew-level performance_score on officiating_crew. Feeds into the official\'s career performance_rating.']
  role_on_crew varchar [note: 'The specific officiating role this individual performs on this crew for this game. Determines responsibilities, positioning, and CBA compensation tier. Replaces the crew_chief_official_id and var_operator_official_id FKs on officiating_crew.']
  substitution_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this official was added as a substitute replacement for another official who was originally assigned to this crew. When true, substituted_for_official_id should be populated.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Role-based assignment between an individual official and an officiating crew for a specific game. It captures the full crew roster composition that the league officiating bureau actively manages — including each official\'s designated role, conflict-of-interest clearance status, individual performance evaluation, and substitution events. Each record links one official to one officiating crew with attributes that exist only in the context of this per-game, per-role assignment. Supports officiating quality management, CBA compliance, conflict-of-interest screening, and workload tracking at the individual official level.. Existence Justification: In professional sports, officiating crew composition is a genuine operational M:N relationship: each officiating crew is assembled from a pool of certified officials (a crew may have 5–8 officials), and each official works across many different crew assignments throughout a season. The league actively manages crew_member_assignment as a business concept — assigning specific roles (crew chief, referee, linesman, VAR operator), tracking conflict-of-interest clearance per assignment, and evaluating individual performance per game. The current officiating_crew product only captures crew_chief_official_id and var_operator_official_id as named FKs, which cannot represent the full crew roster and leaves all other officials untracked.'
}

Table league.franchise_distribution_right {
  franchise_distribution_right_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the franchise_distribution_right association']
  digital_touchpoint_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the digital touchpoint (channel) on which the franchise is authorized for distribution.']
  franchise_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the franchise whose content and brand is being distributed on the digital touchpoint.']
  content_rights_tier varchar [note: 'The tier of content rights granted to this digital touchpoint for this franchise — determines what content (live games, highlights, PPV events, archival) the touchpoint is authorized to deliver. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']
  distribution_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this franchise distribution right. Supports lifecycle management — rights may be pending approval, active, suspended due to compliance issues, or expired at term end.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'The date on which the franchise\'s authorization to be distributed on this digital touchpoint becomes effective. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']
  effective_until_date date [note: 'The date on which the franchise\'s authorization to be distributed on this digital touchpoint expires or was revoked. Null if the distribution right is open-ended. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']
  exclusivity_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this franchise-touchpoint pairing carries an exclusivity clause, meaning the franchise\'s content at this rights tier may not be simultaneously distributed on competing touchpoints. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']
  touchpoint_role varchar [note: 'The functional role this digital touchpoint plays in distributing the franchise\'s content — e.g., primary (full rights, main channel), syndicated (secondary distribution), preview_only (limited free content). Sourced from detection phase relationship data.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between a franchise and a digital touchpoint governing the official distribution of that franchise\'s content and brand on a specific fan-facing digital channel. It captures the authorized rights tier, exclusivity terms, touchpoint role, and effective period for each franchise-channel pairing. Each record links one franchise to one digital touchpoint with attributes that exist only in the context of this distribution rights arrangement — managed by digital rights and DTC operations teams.. Existence Justification: In sports entertainment DTC operations, a franchise (e.g., LA Lakers) is officially distributed across multiple digital touchpoints (team app, league OTT platform, web portal, venue kiosk), and each digital touchpoint hosts multiple franchises. This is not an analytical correlation — it is an actively managed distribution rights arrangement where the business must track which franchises are authorized on which channels, under what content rights tier, with what exclusivity terms, and for what effective period. Business stakeholders in digital distribution and rights management explicitly manage these pairings as \'franchise distribution agreements\' or \'channel distribution rights.\''
}

Table league.regulatory_oversight {
  regulatory_oversight_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the regulatory_oversight association']
  franchise_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the franchise that is subject to this regulatory oversight relationship.']
  governing_body_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the governing body or regulatory authority exercising oversight over the franchise.']
  compliance_status varchar [note: 'Current compliance standing of the franchise with respect to this governing body\'s requirements. Actively managed by the compliance team and updated following audits, filings, or enforcement actions.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which this oversight relationship became legally binding or operationally active for this franchise. May differ from registration_date if there is a grace or transition period.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which this oversight relationship expires, lapses, or is scheduled for renewal. Null if the relationship is open-ended or perpetual.']
  jurisdiction_scope varchar [note: 'The specific geographic or operational scope of this governing body\'s authority as it applies to this franchise. May differ from the governing body\'s general jurisdiction_scope when a franchise has a narrower or broader obligation.']
  oversight_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the type of regulatory authority this governing body exercises over this franchise (e.g., anti-doping, broadcast, labor-safety, franchise-governance). Drives which compliance obligations apply.']
  registration_date date [note: 'The date on which the franchise formally registered with, or became subject to the jurisdiction of, this governing body. Marks the start of the oversight relationship.']
  regulatory_oversight_status varchar [note: 'Lifecycle status of this specific franchise-governing body oversight record. Distinct from compliance_status — this tracks whether the oversight relationship itself is active, not whether the franchise is compliant.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the formal regulatory oversight relationship (Contract/Registration) between a franchise and a governing body. It captures the specific compliance obligations, registration standing, and jurisdictional scope that apply to each franchise-governing body pairing. Each record documents one governing body\'s authority over one franchise, including the type of oversight exercised, the franchise\'s registration or membership identifier with that body, current compliance status, and the effective dates of the oversight relationship. This is the system of record for franchise-level regulatory compliance tracking.. Existence Justification: A franchise is simultaneously subject to oversight from multiple governing bodies — the league office (NFL/NBA/etc.), anti-doping authorities (WADA), broadcast regulators (FCC), labor/safety bodies (OSHA/ADA), and potentially state athletic commissions — all at the same time. Conversely, each governing body (e.g., WADA, OSHA) oversees many franchises across the league. This is an active, operationally managed compliance relationship: franchises must register with each body, maintain compliance status per body, and track jurisdiction-specific obligations — none of which can be captured by a single FK on either entity.'
}

Table league.streaming_rights_authorization {
  streaming_rights_authorization_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the streaming_rights_authorization association']
  digital_touchpoint_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the digital touchpoint (channel) that is being granted streaming rights for the associated season.']
  league_season_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the league season whose content is being authorized for distribution on this digital touchpoint.']
  authorization_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of this streaming rights authorization. Enables rights compliance enforcement — only \'active\' authorizations permit content distribution. Supports suspension and revocation workflows without deleting the historical record.']
  broadcast_rights_tier varchar [note: 'The rights tier classification under which this digital touchpoint is authorized to stream the season\'s content. Determines content access level, quality caps, and commercial terms. Belongs to the authorization record, not to the season or touchpoint independently.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'The date on which this streaming rights authorization becomes active and the digital touchpoint may begin distributing the season\'s content. May precede the season start_date (e.g., preseason content) or align with it.']
  effective_until_date date [note: 'The date on which this streaming rights authorization expires and the digital touchpoint must cease distributing the season\'s content. May extend beyond the season end_date for archive/VOD windows.']
  geo_restriction_scope varchar [note: 'The specific geographic scope of this authorization — e.g., \'US_domestic\', \'EMEA\', \'global_ex_blackout_markets\'. Distinct from the touchpoint-level geo_restriction_enabled flag, which is a capability indicator. This attribute defines the actual authorized territory for this specific season-touchpoint rights grant.']
  streaming_rights_type varchar [note: 'Specifies the type of streaming rights granted: live (real-time broadcast), VOD (on-demand after broadcast), replay (full game replay), archive (historical season content), or highlights_only. A touchpoint may be authorized for live rights for the current season but only archive rights for prior seasons.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Contract between season and digital_touchpoint. It captures the formal authorization granting a specific digital touchpoint the right to distribute content from a specific league season under defined broadcast rights terms, geographic scope, and validity window. Each record links one season to one digital_touchpoint with attributes that exist only in the context of this rights grant — including the rights tier, streaming type, geo-restriction scope, and effective dates. This is the system of record for digital broadcast rights compliance across all fan-facing channels.. Existence Justification: In sports entertainment, broadcast rights are actively managed contracts that authorize specific digital touchpoints (OTT app, mobile app, web portal) to stream content from specific seasons under defined rights tiers, geo-restrictions, and time windows. A single season\'s content is distributed across multiple authorized digital channels simultaneously, and each digital touchpoint carries content from multiple seasons (live current season plus archived past seasons). This relationship — a broadcast rights authorization — is a core compliance and rights management operation that the business actively creates, updates, and audits.'
}

True = the settlement amount or terms are contested. Disputed settlements are excluded from netting runs until resolved and flagged for transfer pricing review.']

  elimination_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this intercompany settlement transaction must be eliminated in the preparation of Sports Entertainment\'s consolidated financial statements. Required for GAAP ASC 810 consolidation and SEC Regulation S-X compliance.']
  exchange_rate decimal(18,6) [note: 'The exchange rate applied to translate the transaction currency amount to the group reporting currency at the time of posting. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA FI exchange rate tables. Required for FX translation audit trail and GAAP ASC 830 compliance.']

  netting_status varchar [note: 'Indicates the current netting processing status of this intercompany settlement within its netting agreement cycle. \'included_in_netting\' means the transaction has been selected for the current netting run; \'netted\' means the settlement has been offset and the net cash movement has been executed.']

  posting_period varchar [note: 'The fiscal posting period in YYYY-MM format to which this intercompany settlement is assigned in SAP S/4HANA FI.   service_period_end date [note: 'The end date of the period during which the underlying service, rights usage, or shared resource was consumed, giving rise to this intercompany settlement. Used for revenue recognition alignment under GAAP ASC 606 and transfer pricing documentation.']
  service_period_start date [note: 'The start date of the period during which the underlying service, rights usage, or shared resource was consumed, giving rise to this intercompany settlement. Used for revenue recognition alignment under GAAP ASC 606 and transfer pricing documentation.']
  settlement_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The gross transaction amount of the intercompany settlement in the transaction currency, before any netting adjustments.   settlement_description varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative description of the intercompany settlement, providing business context for the transaction.   settlement_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the intercompany settlement transaction, formatted as ICT-{YEAR}-{SEQUENCE}.   settlement_status varchar [note: 'Current workflow lifecycle state of the intercompany settlement transaction.   tax_code varchar [note: 'The SAP S/4HANA FI tax code applied to this intercompany settlement, determining the applicable VAT/GST treatment for cross-border intercompany transactions. Relevant for Sports Entertainment entities operating across multiple tax jurisdictions globally.']
  transaction_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the intercompany settlement by business purpose. Examples include broadcast rights fees from network entity to league entity, shared services charges from corporate to venue subsidiaries, NIL (Name Image and Likeness) licensing fees between athlete management and franchise entities, and content licensing between streaming platform and production entities. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: broadcast_rights_fee|shared_services_charge|nil_licensing_fee|content_licensing|transfer_pricing|management_fee|intercompany_loan_interest|royalty — promote to reference product]']
  transfer_price_method varchar [note: 'The OECD-approved transfer pricing methodology used to determine the arm\'s-length price for this intercompany settlement.   testing_method varchar [note: 'The audit testing procedure applied to evaluate the operating effectiveness of the control. Reperformance and data analytics are preferred for high-risk controls; inquiry alone is insufficient per PCAOB standards. Drives the evidence collection approach.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this SOX control record was most recently modified. Tracks changes to control attributes, test results, or remediation status throughout the reporting period lifecycle.']

  Note: 'SOX internal control and period-end governance record documenting financial controls required under Sarbanes-Oxley Section 302/404 for publicly traded Sports Entertainment entities. Encompasses standing controls (segregation of duties, approval thresholds, system access reviews) and period-end close activities (accrual postings, depreciation runs, intercompany eliminations, financial statement preparation, flux analysis).   stream_category varchar [note: 'Top-level classification of the revenue stream aligned to Sports Entertainment\'s primary revenue pillars: ticketing (gate receipts, VIP, SRO), broadcast (RSN, OTT, PPV, DTC), sponsorship (naming rights, jersey, digital), merchandise (licensed SKUs, e-commerce), venue_rental (facility hire, HVAC services), gaming (fantasy, wagering), content (UGC licensing, DAM syndication), other. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ticketing|broadcast|sponsorship|merchandise|venue_rental|gaming|content|other — promote to reference product]']
  stream_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the revenue stream, used in SAP S/4HANA FI/CO chart of accounts mapping, Workday Adaptive Planning budget models, and cross-system reconciliation. Examples: TICK_GA, BCAST_OTT, SPON_NAMING.']

  revised_projected_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Updated projected cash flow amount following a mid-cycle reforecast or management adjustment. Captures the most current forecast estimate when the original projection has been revised.']
  scenario_type varchar [note: 'Planning scenario classification for this forecast record. Base is the primary operating plan; optimistic and pessimistic represent upside/downside sensitivities; stress is a regulatory or risk-driven scenario; actuals captures realised cash flows for variance analysis.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Operational system of record from which this forecast record originated. SAP_S4HANA for FI/CO actuals and liquidity planning; WORKDAY_ADAPTIVE for FP&A planning inputs; MANUAL for analyst-entered adjustments; TICKETMASTER for ticket sales projections; SALESFORCE_CRM for sponsorship pipeline forecasts.']

  variance_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Absolute difference between the projected (or revised projected) amount and the actual amount for the period. Positive variance indicates actuals exceeded forecast (favourable for inflows, unfavourable for outflows); negative indicates shortfall.']
  variance_pct decimal(8,4) [note: 'Variance expressed as a percentage of the projected amount. Enables proportional comparison across business units and periods for FP&A dashboards and KPI reporting.']

  Note: 'Cash flow forecasting records by period and business unit — projected inflows (ticket sales, broadcast payments, sponsorship installments) and outflows (payroll, venue ops, content production) with variance tracking.'

  budget_currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the operating budget of this organizational unit (e.g., \'USD\', \'GBP\', \'EUR\'). Used for multi-currency financial consolidation in SAP S/4HANA and Workday Adaptive Planning. [Moved from org_unit: The operating budget currency for an org unit is relevant only in the context of a specific budget allocation. As a static org_unit attribute it cannot accommodate multi-currency allocations across different fiscal years or budget scenarios. It belongs on the allocation record as \'currency_code\'.]']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this budget allocation record was first created in the source system, supporting audit trail and allocation history tracking.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the allocated amounts in this allocation record. Sourced from relationship_data \'budget_currency_code\'. May differ from the parent budget\'s currency_code if the org unit operates in a different functional currency.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'The date from which this budget allocation to the org unit is effective and valid for financial reporting and commitment purposes.']
  effective_to_date date [note: 'The date through which this budget allocation to the org unit remains valid. Aligns with the fiscal period end date of the parent budget record.']
  fiscal_year decimal [note: 'The fiscal year to which this org-unit-level budget allocation applies. Sourced from relationship_data \'fiscal_year\'. Retained on the association to support direct querying of allocations by fiscal year without joining back to the parent budget record.']
  fte_count_actual decimal [note: 'Actual full-time equivalent count for this org unit as recorded at the time of this budget allocation, used for variance analysis against allocated_headcount_budget. Sourced from relationship_data \'fte_count_actual\'. Moved from org_unit because actual FTE is point-in-time per fiscal period, not a static org unit property.']
  headcount_budget varchar [note: 'Approved full-time equivalent (FTE) headcount budget for this organizational unit as authorized in the annual workforce plan. Used for headcount variance reporting, recruitment approval workflows, and span-of-control governance. [Moved from org_unit: Approved FTE headcount budget is a planning-cycle attribute that changes with each annual budget and reforecast. It is not a static property of the org unit — it is a property of the allocation of headcount to that org unit for a specific fiscal year and budget version. Moving it to the association enables proper versioning and variance tracking against fte_count_actual.]']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Budget Allocation contract between a budget planning record and an organizational unit. It captures the formal assignment of planned, revised, committed, and forecast financial amounts — as well as approved headcount — to a specific org unit for a given fiscal period, budget version, and scenario. Each record links one budget to one org_unit and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this allocation relationship, including allocated amounts, headcount approvals, and allocation-level approval status. Managed jointly by Finance (FP&A) and HR as part of the annual budgeting, reforecast, and headcount planning cycles.. Existence Justification: In Sports Entertainment, a single budget record (e.g., FY2025 OPEX for Event Operations) is allocated across multiple org units (team ops, broadcast, venue, events), and each org unit receives funding from multiple budget line items across OPEX, CAPEX, and headcount categories. Finance and HR jointly manage these allocations as a formal business process — creating, revising, and approving budget allocations per org-unit-budget combination with tracked amounts, headcount approvals, and fiscal versioning. This is an operationally managed relationship, not an analytical derivation.'
}

  withholding_tax_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The total withholding tax amount deducted from payments in this run. Required for tax compliance and reporting to tax authorities.']

  Note: 'Master reference table for payment_run. Referenced by payment_run_id.'

Must not contain PHI (medical details should be captured via formal certification process only). Restricted to HR and the approving manager.']
  employee_work_schedule varchar [note: 'Work schedule classification of the employee at the time of the leave request. Determines applicable leave entitlements, proration rules, and staffing gap impact. Covers full-time staff, part-time event crew, broadcast crews, league officials, and seasonal workers per the workforce domain scope.']
  fmla_designation_notice_date date [note: 'The date on which HR issued the FMLA Designation Notice (WH-382) to the employee, confirming whether the leave qualifies as FMLA-protected. Must be issued within 5 business days of receiving sufficient information per DOL regulations. Null for non-FMLA leave types.']
  fmla_hours_used decimal(8,2) [note: 'Cumulative FMLA-designated hours consumed by this specific leave request against the employee\'s annual 480-hour (12-week) FMLA entitlement. Populated only when is_fmla_eligible = True. Used for FMLA entitlement balance tracking and DOL compliance reporting.']
  hr_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes entered by HR personnel during the review and processing of the leave request. May include documentation status, escalation notes, or compliance observations. Confidential HR data restricted to HR personnel only.']
  is_fmla_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the employee meets FMLA eligibility criteria at the time of the request: employed for at least 12 months, worked 1,250 hours in the prior 12 months, and works at a location with 50+ employees within 75 miles. True = eligible; False = not eligible. Drives FMLA compliance reporting.']
  is_intermittent boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this leave is taken intermittently (in separate blocks of time or by reducing the normal work schedule) rather than as a continuous absence. True = intermittent leave; False = continuous leave. Intermittent FMLA requires separate hourly tracking and is common for chronic conditions among event-day staff.']
  is_paid boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the approved leave is compensated (paid) or uncompensated (unpaid). True = paid leave; False = unpaid leave. Drives payroll processing in SAP SuccessFactors and determines whether PTO balance is decremented.']
  jury_duty_court_name varchar [note: 'Name of the court or tribunal issuing the jury summons for jury duty leave requests. Null for non-jury-duty leave types. Used to validate the legitimacy of the jury duty claim and for payroll differential calculations.']
  leave_end_date date [note: 'The last calendar date on which the employee is scheduled to be absent under this leave request. Null for open-ended leaves pending medical certification. Used to calculate approved leave duration and plan workforce coverage.']
  leave_reason varchar [note: 'General business reason or description provided by the employee for the leave request. Kept at a high level to avoid PHI exposure (e.g., \'personal medical\', \'family care\', \'military deployment\'). Confidential HR data restricted to HR personnel and the approving manager. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PERSONAL_MEDICAL|FAMILY_CARE|MILITARY_DEPLOYMENT|BEREAVEMENT|CIVIC_DUTY|PARENTAL_BONDING|PERSONAL — promote to reference product]']
  leave_start_date date [note: 'The first calendar date on which the employee is scheduled to be absent under this leave request. Used for event staffing gap analysis and payroll processing.']
  leave_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the leave category as defined by HR policy and applicable labor law. Values include: FMLA (Family and Medical Leave Act), PTO (Paid Time Off), SICK, BEREAVEMENT, JURY_DUTY, MILITARY, PARENTAL, COMP_TIME (event-day compensatory time). Drives eligibility rules, pay treatment, and regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FMLA|PTO|SICK|BEREAVEMENT|JURY_DUTY|MILITARY|PARENTAL|COMP_TIME — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  medical_certification_received boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the required medical certification documentation has been received and accepted by HR. True = received; False = pending or not received. Used to track FMLA compliance deadlines (employee has 15 calendar days to provide certification).']
  medical_certification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a medical certification form (e.g., FMLA WH-380-E or WH-380-F) is required to support this leave request. True = certification required; False = not required. Drives HR compliance workflow and document collection tracking.']
  military_order_number varchar [note: 'Official military deployment order number provided by the employee to support a military leave request under USERRA (Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act). Null for non-military leave types. Confidential HR document reference.']
  pay_treatment varchar [note: 'Specifies the compensation treatment applied during the leave period. FULL_PAY = 100% salary continuation; PARTIAL_PAY = reduced pay per policy or CBA; UNPAID = no compensation; STD = Short-Term Disability benefit; LTD = Long-Term Disability benefit. Used by payroll to apply correct earnings codes.']
  phased_return_plan boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the employee has an approved phased or gradual return-to-work plan following the leave (e.g., reduced hours for first two weeks). True = phased return approved; False = full-duty return. Common for medical and parental leave returns in sports operations.']
  pto_hours_deducted decimal(8,2) [note: 'Number of accrued PTO hours deducted from the employee\'s PTO balance for this leave request. Applicable when leave type is PTO or when employer requires concurrent PTO usage during FMLA leave. Feeds into SAP SuccessFactors leave balance management.']
  request_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the employee formally submitted the leave request. Used to measure advance notice compliance per CBA and FMLA notice requirements (typically 30-day advance notice for foreseeable leave).']
  request_number varchar [note: 'Externally visible, human-readable business identifier for the leave request, formatted as LR-{YEAR}-{SEQUENCE}. Used in employee communications, manager approvals, and FMLA compliance documentation.']
  return_to_work_date date [note: 'The confirmed or expected calendar date on which the employee is scheduled to return to active duty following the leave. May differ from leave_end_date + 1 due to weekends, holidays, or phased return arrangements. Critical for event staffing and broadcast crew scheduling.']
  source_system_record_code varchar [note: 'The native record identifier assigned by SAP SuccessFactors Time and Attendance to this leave request. Preserved for data lineage, reconciliation, and bi-directional sync between the Silver Layer and the system of record.']
  submitted_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (with timezone) at which the employee submitted the leave request in SAP SuccessFactors. Serves as the authoritative BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP for this transaction and is used to enforce advance notice compliance windows.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this leave request record was most recently modified in the Silver Layer data product. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED timestamp for change tracking, incremental ETL processing, and audit compliance.']

  Note: 'Employee leave and absence request record managing all time-off events at Sports Entertainment. Captures leave type (FMLA, PTO, sick, bereavement, jury duty, military, parental, event-day comp time), request date, leave start date, leave end date, approved hours/days, approval status, approving manager, FMLA eligibility flag, intermittent leave flag, and return-to-work date. Sourced from SAP SuccessFactors Time and Attendance. Supports FMLA compliance, absence trend analysis, and event staffing gap identification.'
}

  legal_first_name varchar [note: 'Legal given name of the contingent worker as it appears on government-issued identification. Required for payroll tax filings, background checks, and OSHA incident reporting.']
  legal_last_name varchar [note: 'Legal surname of the contingent worker as it appears on government-issued identification. Required for payroll tax filings, background checks, and OSHA incident reporting.']
  national_id_hash varchar [note: 'One-way cryptographic hash of the contingent worker\'s national identification number (e.g., SSN, SIN, NIN). Stored as a hash to enable deduplication and tax reporting linkage without exposing the raw identifier. Required for IRS 1099-NEC filing.']
  nationality_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the contingent worker\'s nationality. Required for international event staffing, visa processing, and WADA anti-doping jurisdiction determination for officiating staff.']
  onboarding_completion_date date [note: 'The date on which the contingent worker completed all required onboarding steps including identity verification, background check, safety training, and credential validation. Marks the worker as fully eligible for assignment.']
  osha_safety_trained boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the contingent worker has completed the mandatory OSHA safety training required for their assigned functional role and venue environment. Blocks event-day assignment if false for safety-sensitive roles.']
  osha_training_date date [note: 'The date on which the contingent worker most recently completed OSHA safety training. Used to track training currency and trigger renewal workflows per OSHA recertification schedules.']
  pay_currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the contingent worker\'s pay rate (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Required for multi-currency payroll processing and financial reporting.']
  pay_rate decimal(18,4) [note: 'The agreed compensation rate for this contingent worker. Interpretation depends on pay_rate_type (hourly, daily, flat fee). Used for labor cost forecasting, invoice validation, and CBA compliance checks.']
  pay_rate_type varchar [note: 'The basis on which the contingent worker\'s pay rate is calculated. Determines how labor costs are accrued and how timesheet hours translate to payable amounts.']
  preferred_name varchar [note: 'The name the contingent worker prefers to be addressed by in operational communications, scheduling systems, and event-day rosters. May differ from legal name.']
  rehire_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this contingent worker is eligible to be re-engaged for future events or assignments. Set to false for workers terminated for cause, failed background checks, or flagged under do-not-rehire policies.']
  role_during_event varchar [note: 'The specific functional role the contingent worker performs at this fixture. May differ from the worker\'s default functional_role on the master record — e.g., a worker whose default role is \'broadcast_crew\' may be assigned as \'operations\' for a specific event.']
  scheduled_end_time timestamp [note: 'The scheduled date and time the contingent worker\'s shift ends for this fixture. Used for hours calculation and payroll processing.']
  scheduled_start_time timestamp [note: 'The scheduled date and time the contingent worker\'s shift begins for this fixture. Distinct from the fixture\'s doors_open_timestamp — workers typically report earlier for setup and briefing.']
  successfactors_external_code varchar [note: 'The external worker identifier assigned by SAP SuccessFactors to this contingent worker record. Used to reconcile the silver-layer master record with the system of record.']
  tax_form_type varchar [note: 'The IRS or equivalent tax form type applicable to this contingent worker\'s engagement. Drives tax withholding logic, year-end reporting obligations, and vendor payment processing in SAP S/4HANA.']
  termination_reason varchar [note: 'The reason code for the termination of the contingent worker\'s engagement. Used for workforce analytics, rehire eligibility determination, and CBA grievance tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: contract_end|voluntary_resignation|performance|misconduct|redundancy|no_show|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  venue_access_level varchar [note: 'The maximum venue access level granted to this contingent worker based on their role, background check status, and credential verification. Controls physical access badge provisioning via Ticketmaster/AXS access control systems.']
  work_authorization_type varchar [note: 'The type of work authorization held by the contingent worker in the country of engagement. Required for I-9 compliance in the US and equivalent immigration compliance in other jurisdictions.']
  work_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the primary country where the contingent worker performs services. Determines applicable labor law, tax jurisdiction, and GDPR/CCPA data privacy obligations.']
  work_email varchar [note: 'Primary work email address used for scheduling communications, credential distribution, and broadcast crew coordination. May be a personal email for gig workers without a company domain.']
  work_phone varchar [note: 'Primary contact phone number for the contingent worker used for event-day coordination, last-minute scheduling changes, and emergency contact by venue operations.']
  worker_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the contingent worker record. Controls access provisioning, scheduling eligibility, and payroll processing. \'do_not_rehire\' flags workers barred from future engagements per HR or legal directive.']
  worker_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the contingent worker\'s engagement model. Drives tax treatment (1099 vs W-2 agency), CBA applicability, and onboarding workflow. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: freelance|event_day_contractor|gig_worker|temporary_staff|agency_worker|independent_contractor — promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Master record for non-employee contingent workforce members engaged by Sports Entertainment — freelance broadcast crew, event-day contractors, gig workers, and temporary staff not managed through standard employment contracts.'
}

Table workforce.position_cost_allocation {
  position_cost_allocation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the position_cost_allocation association']
  cost_center_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this allocation record to the cost center that funds a portion of the position\'s labor costs.']
  position_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this allocation record to the organizational position whose labor costs are being distributed.']
  allocation_percentage decimal [note: 'The proportion of the position\'s total FTE and labor cost charged to this cost center, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.60 = 60%). All allocation_percentage values for a given position_id must sum to 1.00 across active records.']
  budget_approval_status varchar [note: 'The current budget authorization state of this specific position-cost center funding split. Sourced from the detection phase relationship data. Distinct from the position-level budget_approval_status, as each funding line may be approved independently.']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'The date on which this position-to-cost-center funding allocation expires or was terminated. Null indicates the allocation is currently open-ended.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'The date on which this position-to-cost-center funding allocation became or becomes active. Sourced from the detection phase relationship data.']
  fte_allocation decimal [note: 'The Full-Time Equivalent value allocated to this cost center for this position, representing the fractional headcount charged. Sourced from the detection phase relationship data. Derived from position.fte_allocation × allocation_percentage but stored explicitly for SAP CO posting.']
  headcount_plan_year varchar [note: 'The fiscal year in which this position-cost center allocation was approved in the headcount plan. Sourced from the detection phase relationship data. Enables year-over-year workforce cost planning analysis.']
  is_primary_cost_center boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this cost center is the primary (majority) funding source for the position. Used to determine the default cost center for reporting and payroll posting when a single cost center must be nominated.']
  pay_grade varchar [note: 'The compensation band or pay grade code applicable to this position-cost center funding line. Sourced from the detection phase relationship data. May differ from the position-level pay_grade when a position spans multiple cost centers with different compensation structures.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the funding contract between a position and a cost center in Sports Entertainment\'s workforce and financial planning model. It captures the split-funding arrangement by which a position\'s labor costs are distributed across one or more cost centers at defined allocation percentages and effective date ranges. Each record links one position to one cost center with attributes — allocation percentage, effective dates, budget approval status, headcount plan year, and pay grade — that exist only in the context of this specific position-to-cost-center funding relationship. Sourced from SAP CO labor distribution and SuccessFactors Position Management.. Existence Justification: In Sports Entertainment organizations, positions are routinely split-funded across multiple cost centers — e.g., a Head of Broadcast Operations charged 60% to the Broadcast Production cost center and 40% to the Venue Operations cost center. Conversely, each cost center funds multiple positions simultaneously. This split-funding arrangement is an actively managed operational record with its own attributes (allocation percentage, effective dates, budget approval status) that belong to neither the position nor the cost center alone.'
}

Table workforce.jurisdiction_license {
  jurisdiction_license_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the jurisdiction_license association']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the licensed employee in the workforce master record.']
  jurisdiction_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the gaming regulatory jurisdiction in which the employee holds the license.']
  assigned_role varchar [note: 'The specific regulatory role or designation the employee holds under this jurisdiction license. Defined by the jurisdiction\'s licensing authority and determines the scope of the employee\'s authorized activities.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date on which this employee\'s license or authorization in the jurisdiction became legally effective. Used for compliance reporting and determining authorized operating windows.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which this employee\'s license or authorization in the jurisdiction expires and must be renewed. Drives renewal workflow triggers and compliance alerts.']
  license_number varchar [note: 'The unique license or authorization number issued by the gaming regulatory authority to this specific employee for this jurisdiction. Distinct from the entity-level license number stored on gaming_jurisdiction; this is the individual employee\'s credential.']
  license_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of this employee\'s license or authorization within the jurisdiction. Determines whether the employee is currently authorized to perform regulated activities in that jurisdiction.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the regulatory licensing contract between an employee and a gaming jurisdiction. It captures the specific license or authorization held by an individual workforce member within a given gaming regulatory jurisdiction, including their assigned compliance role, the jurisdiction-issued license number, the effective and expiry dates of the authorization, and the current license status. Each record is an independently managed compliance artifact — created when a license application is approved, updated on renewal or status change, and retired on expiry or revocation. This is the SSOT for employee-level gaming regulatory authorization across all jurisdictions.. Existence Justification: In Sports Entertainment\'s gaming compliance operations, specific employees (compliance officers, legal counsel, regulatory affairs staff) hold individual licenses or authorizations in multiple gaming jurisdictions simultaneously (e.g., NJ, PA, NV, CO), and each jurisdiction has multiple licensed employees operating within it. This is an actively managed operational relationship — the business must track which employee is licensed in which jurisdiction, under what role, with what license number, effective dates, and current status. This is not derivable from transactional data; it is a directly managed compliance record.'
}

  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the Anti-Doping Rule Violation (ADRV) record was most recently modified in the compliance system. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking for regulatory reporting.']
  violation_reference_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique alphanumeric reference code assigned to this Anti-Doping Rule Violation (ADRV) by the governing body or anti-doping organisation (ADO) for case tracking and correspondence.']

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|provisional_suspension|hearing_scheduled|sanctioned|appealed|overturned|closed — promote to reference product]']
  violation_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the Anti-Doping Rule Violation (ADRV) per WADA Code Article 2. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: adverse_analytical_finding|atypical_analytical_finding|whereabouts_failure|tampering|refusal|possession|trafficking|administration|complicity|prohibited_association — promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Record of an Anti-Doping Rule Violation (ADRV) issued against an athlete following an adverse or atypical analytical finding or non-analytical violation (whereabouts failure, tampering, refusal).   competition_start_date date [note: 'Start date of the scheduled competition or event during the filing period. Used to plan in-competition doping control and to validate athlete availability windows.']
  compliance_status varchar [note: 'Regulatory compliance determination for this filing period. Three MISSED or INCOMPLETE filings within 12 months trigger a WADA Code Article 2.4 violation.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this whereabouts filing record was first created in the compliance data platform. Provides the audit trail creation anchor for the Silver Layer lakehouse record.']

  filing_period_year varchar [note: 'Calendar year (e.g., 2024) to which this whereabouts filing applies. Combined with filing_period_quarter to uniquely identify the quarterly filing obligation period.']
  is_late_submission boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether the filing was submitted after the regulatory deadline (submission_date > filing_deadline). Late submissions may be treated as incomplete or missed filings depending on the anti-doping organisation\'s rules.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time of the most recent amendment or update to this whereabouts filing record. Supports audit trail requirements and compliance adjudication when disputes arise over filing completeness.']
  missed_filing_count_rolling_12m varchar [note: 'Running count of missed or non-compliant whereabouts filings by this athlete within the preceding 12-month rolling window at the time of this filing. PENDING = awaiting review; IN_REVIEW = under active compliance review; ACCEPTED = compliance determination finalised; DISPUTED = athlete or representative has contested the compliance determination; ESCALATED = referred to CAS or governing body for adjudication.']
  sixty_minute_slot_time timestamp [note: 'Specific 60-minute daily time window (HH:MM in 24-hour format, representing start of slot) during which the athlete guarantees availability for out-of-competition testing at the declared training venue.   sport_discipline varchar [note: 'Sport and discipline for which the athlete is registered in the testing pool (e.g., Athletics - 100m Sprint, Swimming - Freestyle, Football). Used for sport-specific whereabouts rule application and reporting to governing bodies such as FIFA, IOC, or relevant International Federation.']
  submission_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the athlete or their authorised representative submitted the whereabouts filing. Used to determine whether the filing was on-time or late relative to the filing_deadline.']
  submission_method varchar [note: 'Channel or mechanism through which the whereabouts filing was submitted. ADAMS_PORTAL and ADAMS_MOBILE are the primary WADA-approved electronic submission methods. Other methods may be accepted in exceptional circumstances per anti-doping organisation policy.']
  submission_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which the whereabouts filing was received and recorded in the ADAMS portal. Provides audit-grade precision for compliance adjudication.']
  submitted_by varchar [note: 'Role of the person who submitted the whereabouts filing on behalf of the athlete. Athletes may authorise agents, coaches, or team officials to submit on their behalf via ADAMS. Relevant for accountability and adjudication of missed filing disputes.']
  testing_pool_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the registered testing pool to which the athlete belongs. RTP = Registered Testing Pool (international-level, managed by International Federation or WADA); NRTP = National Registered Testing Pool (managed by National Anti-Doping Organisation); TP = Testing Pool (lower-tier, no whereabouts filing obligation but tracked for completeness).']
  training_schedule_end_time timestamp [note: 'Scheduled end time of the athlete\'s regular training sessions during the filing period. Together with training_schedule_start_time, defines the daily availability window for doping control officers.']
  training_schedule_start_time timestamp [note: 'Scheduled start time of the athlete\'s regular training sessions during the filing period. Combined with training_schedule_end_time, defines the 60-minute testing slot window required by WADA ISTI.']
  training_venue_address varchar [note: 'Full street address of the primary training venue for the filing period. Enables doping control officers to locate the athlete for unannounced out-of-competition testing.']
  training_venue_name varchar [note: 'Name of the primary training facility or venue where the athlete trains during the filing period. Required for out-of-competition testing planning and sample collection logistics.']
  update_count varchar [note: 'Number of times this whereabouts filing has been updated or amended after initial submission. Athletes may update filings up to the deadline without penalty; updates after the deadline may be flagged for review.']
  violation_threshold_reached boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether this filing caused the athlete\'s missed filing count to reach or exceed the WADA Code Article 2.4 threshold of three missed/incomplete filings within 12 months, triggering a formal whereabouts failure violation.']

  Note: 'WADA whereabouts information filing submitted by registered testing pool athletes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FIFA|IOC|NFL|NBA|MLB|NHL|MLS|WADA|CAS|FCC|SEC|OSHA|ADA|GDPR|CCPA|PCI_SSC|SOX — promote to reference product]']
  interim_measures_description varchar [note: 'Narrative description of any interim or provisional measures ordered, including scope, duration, and conditions. Populated only when interim_measures_granted is True.']
  interim_measures_granted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether interim or provisional measures (e.g., injunctions, stay of eligibility suspension, asset freezes) have been granted by the tribunal or court during the pendency of the case.']
  jurisdiction varchar [note: 'Legal jurisdiction governing the case proceedings (e.g., Switzerland for CAS, specific US state for civil litigation, EU for GDPR regulatory matters). Expressed as ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code or named jurisdiction where country code is insufficient.']
  latest_hearing_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent hearing, session, or proceeding. Tracks case progression and supports scheduling of subsequent hearings.']
  lead_external_counsel varchar [note: 'Name of the primary external law firm or lead attorney representing Sports Entertainment in the proceedings. Used for matter management, conflict-of-interest checks, and outside counsel spend tracking.']
  matter_management_ref varchar [note: 'Reference identifier from the enterprise legal matter management system (e.g., SAP S/4HANA legal module or external e-billing platform) linking this case record to the full matter file, billing records, and document repository.']
  outside_counsel_spend decimal(18,2) [note: 'Cumulative legal fees and disbursements paid to external counsel for this case to date.   panel_composition varchar [note: 'Names and roles of arbitrators, panel members, or presiding judge(s) assigned to the case. Stored as a structured text description (e.g., \'Sole Arbitrator: J.   regulatory_reporting_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this case requires mandatory disclosure or reporting to a regulatory body (e.g., SEC material litigation disclosure, WADA anti-doping result notification, FCC license compliance report).']
  resolution_date date [note: 'Actual date on which the case was resolved through award, judgment, settlement, withdrawal, or dismissal. Null if the case is still active.']
  respondent_name varchar [note: 'Full legal name of the respondent (arbitration) or defendant (litigation) against whom the dispute is brought. May be Sports Entertainment entity, an athlete, club, or third party. Classified confidential as it is a party to active legal proceedings.']
  respondent_type varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the respondent or defendant party. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: athlete|club|league|broadcaster|sponsor|employee|regulatory_body|third_party — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  settlement_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Agreed monetary settlement amount if the case was resolved through negotiated settlement rather than a formal award or judgment. Null if no settlement was reached.']
  settlement_terms varchar [note: 'Summary of the key terms and conditions of any negotiated settlement agreement, including confidentiality obligations, non-disparagement clauses, and performance requirements. Distinct from award_summary which covers tribunal-rendered decisions.']
  sport_or_league varchar [note: 'The specific sport, league, or competition context to which this case relates (e.g., NFL, NBA, FIFA, UFC, ATP). Enables domain-specific reporting and governing body alignment for multi-sport enterprises.']
  subject_matter varchar [note: 'Concise description of the primary legal or regulatory subject matter at issue (e.g., PED (Performance Enhancing Drug) violation, NIL (Name Image and Likeness) contract breach, broadcast IP (Intellectual Property) infringement, GDPR data privacy violation, ADA accessibility non-compliance, CBA grievance).']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this arbitration case record. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.']

  Note: 'Unified dispute resolution and case management record for all legal proceedings — CAS (Court of Arbitration for Sport) arbitration, internal arbitration, civil litigation, regulatory investigations, criminal referrals, IP infringement, employment disputes, and CBA grievances. Serves as the SSOT for all dispute proceedings regardless of forum.'
