Table platform.search_query {
  search_query_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each fan search query record captured across platform digital touchpoints.']
  ab_test_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the active A/B test experiment applied to this search query, enabling controlled measurement of search algorithm or UI variants on fan engagement.']
  auth_session_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the platform authentication session during which the search was performed, enabling session-level search behaviour analysis.']
  digital_touchpoint_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the digital touchpoint (mobile app, web portal, in-venue kiosk, OTT platform) on which the search was executed.']
  event_fixture_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific sports or entertainment event associated with the search context (e.g., the game or concert the fan is searching within). Null for non-event-contextual searches.']
  fan_account_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the authenticated fan account that submitted the search query. Null for unauthenticated/anonymous sessions.']
  fan_profile_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to fan.fan_profile. Business justification: Search behavior analysis for CRM segmentation, content gap reporting, and personalization requires linking search queries to the canonical fan profile. A digital analytics team in sports-entertainment']
  fan_segment_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the fan segment active at the time of the search, used by the Adobe Experience Platform personalisation engine to rank and filter search results.']
  fixture_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific sports or entertainment event associated with the search context (e.g., the game or concert the fan is searching within). Null for non-event-contextual searches.']
  personalization_profile_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to platform.personalization_profile. Business justification: search_query has no FK to personalization_profile despite search being a key personalization signal. Linking search queries to the fan\'s personalization profile enables search result personalization, ']
  refined_search_query_id varchar [note: 'Self-referencing FK on search_query (refined_search_query_id)']
  ab_test_variant_key varchar [note: 'The specific variant identifier (e.g., control, variant_a, variant_b) assigned to this search query within the referenced A/B test experiment.']
  aep_event_reference varchar [note: 'The Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) Experience Event identifier corresponding to this search query, enabling bi-directional reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver layer and AEP for personalisation and analytics.']
  app_version varchar [note: 'Version of the fan-facing application (mobile app or OTT app) from which the search was submitted. Used to correlate search quality issues with specific app releases.']
  autocomplete_triggered boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the search query was submitted via an autocomplete suggestion rather than a fully typed term. Autocomplete adoption rate is a key search UX metric.']
  ccpa_applicable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this search query record is subject to California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) obligations. Governs opt-out of sale and data deletion rights for California residents.']
  clicked_result_position varchar [note: 'The rank position (1-based) of the search result item that the fan clicked or tapped. Null if no result was selected. Used to measure search relevance and click-through quality.']
  clicked_result_reference varchar [note: 'The business entity identifier of the search result item that was clicked (e.g., event ID, athlete ID, content asset ID, merchandise SKU). Stored as STRING to accommodate cross-domain entity types.']
  clicked_result_type varchar [note: 'The entity type of the search result that was clicked, enabling cross-domain click analysis (e.g., event, athlete, content_asset, ticket, merchandise, venue, team). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: event|athlete|content_asset|ticket|merchandise|venue|team — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this search query record was first ingested into the Silver layer data product. Used for data lineage and audit trail.']
  data_retention_expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which this search query record is eligible for deletion or anonymisation per applicable data retention policies (GDPR, CCPA). Supports automated data lifecycle management.']
  device_type varchar [note: 'Category of device used to submit the search query. Supports device-level search experience optimisation and A/B test segmentation.']
  filter_applied boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the fan applied one or more faceted filters (e.g., sport type, date range, price range) in conjunction with this search query.']
  filter_criteria varchar [note: 'Serialised representation of the filter parameters applied alongside the search query (e.g., sport=NFL, date_from=2025-01-01, price_max=150). Stored as a delimited string for Silver layer compatibility.']
  gdpr_applicable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this search query record is subject to General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) obligations based on the fan\'s geographic location at query time. Governs data retention and erasure eligibility.']
  geo_country_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the fan\'s location at the time of the search, derived from IP geolocation or device locale. Supports geo-specific search relevance tuning and broadcast blackout compliance.']
  geo_region varchar [note: 'Sub-national region or state/province of the fan at the time of the search (e.g., CA, NY, ON). Supports Regional Sports Network (RSN) content relevance and venue proximity search ranking.']
  is_authenticated boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the fan was authenticated (logged in) at the time of the search. Authenticated searches enable personalised result ranking via AEP; unauthenticated searches use anonymous relevance models.']
  is_result_clicked boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the fan clicked on any search result following this query. False indicates a no-click search, which may signal poor relevance or fan abandonment.']
  is_zero_result boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the search query returned zero results. True when result_count = 0. Critical KPI for search quality monitoring, content gap identification, and fan experience improvement programmes.']
  normalised_query_text varchar [note: 'Lowercased, trimmed, and stop-word-reduced version of the raw query text used for search analytics, trending term identification, and personalisation engine (AEP) input.']
  platform_channel varchar [note: 'The digital channel through which the search was submitted: mobile_app, web_portal, smart_tv, in_venue_kiosk, OTT app, or voice_assistant. Supports omnichannel search analytics.']
  query_language_code varchar [note: 'BCP-47 language tag detected or declared for the search query (e.g., en-US, es-MX, fr-FR), supporting multilingual search analytics across global markets.']
  query_reference_code varchar [note: 'Business-facing externally referenceable code for this search query record, used in analytics reporting and Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) event correlation.']
  query_status varchar [note: 'Lifecycle status of the search query execution: completed (results returned), zero_result (no matches found), error (system failure), cancelled (fan abandoned before results), timeout (exceeded SLA threshold).']
  query_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which the fan submitted the search query. Principal business event timestamp for this record.']
  query_type varchar [note: 'Mechanism by which the search was initiated: keyword (typed text), voice (speech-to-text), barcode_scan (merchandise/ticket scan), filter_browse (faceted navigation), autocomplete_selection (suggestion tapped).']
  raw_query_text varchar [note: 'The verbatim search string entered by the fan, preserved exactly as submitted before any normalisation or stemming. May contain PII if a fan types a personal name; classified confidential for data governance. Subject to GDPR data minimisation review.']
  referrer_url varchar [note: 'The URL of the page or screen from which the fan navigated to the search interface. Supports funnel analysis and search entry-point optimisation.']
  response_time_ms varchar [note: 'End-to-end search response latency in milliseconds from query submission to results rendered on the fan\'s device. Used for SLA compliance monitoring against platform response time thresholds.']
  result_count varchar [note: 'Total number of results returned by the search engine for this query. A value of 0 indicates a zero-result query, which is a key signal for search quality and content gap analysis.']
  search_algorithm_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the search ranking algorithm or index configuration active at the time of the query. Enables retrospective analysis of algorithm changes on search quality metrics.']
  search_context varchar [note: 'Business context in which the search was performed: pre_event (fan planning before attending), in_venue (fan inside venue during event), content_browse (browsing broadcast/OTT content), post_event (reviewing after event), general (no specific event context).']
  search_domain varchar [note: 'The primary business domain scope of the search query: events, athletes, content (broadcast/OTT), tickets, merchandise, venues, teams, or general cross-domain. Drives search index routing and analytics segmentation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: events|athletes|content|tickets|merchandise|venues|teams|general|sponsors|news — promote to reference product]']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this search query record in the Silver layer, supporting incremental processing and audit.']
  utm_campaign varchar [note: 'Urchin Tracking Module (UTM) campaign tag present in the session at the time of the search, linking search behaviour to marketing campaign attribution.']

  Note: 'Fan search query records across platform properties — search term, results returned, result clicked, search context (pre-event, in-venue, content browse), and zero-result flags.'
}

  payment_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the payment by business purpose. \'standard\' = routine invoice payment; \'advance\' = prepayment before invoice; \'partial\' = partial settlement of invoice; \'final\' = final payment closing the payable; \'emergency\' = expedited out-of-cycle payment; \'intercompany\' = payment between related entities.']

  reversal_reason varchar [note: 'Business reason for reversing or voiding this payment (e.g., duplicate payment, incorrect amount, wrong vendor, bank rejection, contract cancellation). Populated only when reversal_flag is True. Required for audit and SOX compliance.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Operational system of record from which this payment record was sourced. Primarily SAP S/4HANA FI payment run (F110). Supports data lineage and Silver Layer provenance tracking.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this vendor payment record was last modified (e.g., status update, reversal posting, block removal). Supports data lineage tracking and Silver Layer change detection. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  value_date date [note: 'The bank value date on which funds are credited to the vendor\'s bank account. May differ from payment_date due to banking processing times. Critical for accurate cash position reporting and treasury management.']
  vendor_category varchar [note: 'Business category of the vendor receiving payment, reflecting the operational domain served (e.g., broadcast_partner, venue_services, merchandise_supplier, technology_vendor, event_contractor, media_production, catering, security). Supports spend analytics by vendor category and domain. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: broadcast_partner|venue_services|merchandise_supplier|technology_vendor|event_contractor|media_production|catering|security — promote to reference product]']
  withholding_tax_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Amount of withholding tax deducted from the gross payment before disbursement to the vendor. Applicable for certain vendor categories (e.g., athlete agents, international contractors). Required for tax compliance reporting.']

Captures payment date, payment method (ACH, wire, check, virtual card), payment amount, currency, bank account reference, payment run ID, clearing document number, and payment status.   regulatory_body varchar [note: 'Name of the regulatory authority that must be notified or has jurisdiction over this incident (e.g., FCC, GDPR supervisory authority, OSHA, PCI SSC). Populated when regulatory_notification_required is true.']
  regulatory_notification_date date [note: 'The date on which the regulatory authority was formally notified of the incident. Required for GDPR 72-hour breach notification compliance and FCC outage reporting.']
  regulatory_notification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the incident requires notification to a regulatory body (e.g., FCC for broadcast outages, GDPR/CCPA for data security breaches, OSHA for venue safety incidents). Triggers compliance workflow.']
  reported_by varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the internal staff member or system that first reported the vendor incident. Supports audit trail and accountability tracking.']
  resolution_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the vendor incident was fully resolved and normal service was restored. Used to calculate total incident duration and SLA resolution compliance.']
  resolution_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time when the vendor incident was resolved. Enables exact duration calculation for SLA breach determination and vendor performance scoring.']
  root_cause_category varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the root cause of the vendor incident. Used for trend analysis, corrective action planning, and vendor performance benchmarking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: equipment_failure|human_error|process_failure|third_party_dependency|capacity_overrun|cybersecurity|natural_event|supply_chain — promote to reference product]']
  root_cause_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the identified root cause of the vendor incident, as determined through investigation. Supports corrective action planning and vendor accountability documentation.']
  scorecard_deduction_points decimal(5,2) [note: 'Number of performance scorecard points deducted from the vendor\'s periodic scorecard as a result of this incident. Feeds the vendor scorecard calculation engine for contract renewal decisions.']
  severity_level varchar [note: 'Severity classification of the vendor incident indicating business impact magnitude. Critical indicates full service failure affecting live events; high indicates significant degradation; medium indicates partial impact; low indicates minor non-conformance.']
  sla_breach_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this incident resulted in a breach of the applicable Service Level Agreement (SLA). True triggers contract penalty calculation and vendor scorecard deduction workflows.']
  sla_resolution_target_minutes varchar [note: 'The contractually agreed maximum resolution time in minutes for this incident severity level, as defined in the applicable SLA. Compared against actual resolution time to determine breach.']
  sla_response_target_minutes varchar [note: 'The contractually agreed maximum response time in minutes for this incident severity level, as defined in the applicable SLA. Used to determine SLA breach status.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the vendor incident record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit compliance, and incremental data processing in the Databricks Silver layer.']
  vendor_contact_name varchar [note: 'Name of the primary vendor contact person responsible for responding to and resolving this incident. Captured for communication and accountability purposes.']

  Note: 'Operational incidents and non-conformance events attributed to vendor performance failures — including broadcast outages, venue service disruptions, merchandise quality defects, and security breaches. Captures incident date, incident type, severity level, affected event or venue, financial impact estimate, root cause classification, corrective action required, resolution date, and SLA breach linkage. Feeds vendor scorecard deductions and contract penalty calculations.'
}

Table partner.ip_license_grant {
  ip_license_grant_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the ip_license_grant association']

  vendor_contract_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking this IP license grant to the governing vendor contract under which the license is granted.']
  exclusivity_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this license grant is exclusive to the vendor within the defined territory and scope. When true, Sports Entertainment is contractually restricted from granting the same IP rights to another vendor in the same territory during the license term.']
  license_grant_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the license grant by exclusivity and sublicensing rights. Determines whether the vendor holds exclusive rights to the IP asset within the defined territory and scope, or whether Sports Entertainment may grant the same rights to other vendors concurrently.']
  license_scope varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the permitted uses of the IP asset under this specific vendor contract. Defines what the vendor is authorized to do with the IP (e.g., reproduce on merchandise, display in broadcast, embed in digital platform UI). Belongs to the grant, not to the contract or IP asset alone.']
  license_term_end date [note: 'The date on which this specific IP license grant expires. May differ from the parent vendor contract expiration_date if the IP licensing provision has a shorter or independently negotiated term.']
  license_term_start date [note: 'The date on which this specific IP license grant becomes effective. May differ from the parent vendor contract effective_date if the IP licensing provision has its own commencement date.']
  royalty_rate decimal [note: 'The royalty rate applicable to this specific IP license grant, expressed as a percentage of net sales or a flat per-unit fee as defined in the vendor contract. Belongs to the vendor-IP pairing, not to the contract or IP asset in isolation.']
  territory varchar [note: 'Geographic scope within which the vendor is authorized to exercise the licensed IP rights. May be a country code, region name, or \'worldwide\'. A single IP asset may be licensed to different vendors in different territories under separate grants.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the contractual IP License Grant between a vendor_contract and an ip_portfolio asset. It captures the specific authorization within a vendor agreement that grants a vendor rights to use a defined intellectual property asset under defined terms — including grant type, scope, territory, exclusivity, royalty rate, and license term dates. Each record links one vendor_contract to one ip_portfolio asset and carries attributes that exist only in the context of that specific vendor-IP pairing. Serves as the SSOT for all IP licensing provisions embedded within vendor commercial agreements.. Existence Justification: In sports entertainment, vendor contracts (e.g., broadcast technology, merchandise, digital platform agreements) routinely include IP licensing provisions that grant vendors rights to use specific trademarks, logos, broadcast rights, or other IP assets. A single vendor contract can license multiple IP assets simultaneously (e.g., a broadcast technology vendor licensed to use the league logo, team marks, and broadcast rights), and a single IP asset (e.g., the league trademark) can be licensed across many vendor contracts. The business actively manages these IP license grants as distinct operational records with their own terms, territory, exclusivity, and royalty rates.'
}

Each record links one fixture to one vendor for one service deployment, with attributes that exist only in the context of this fixture-vendor engagement and cannot reside on either the fixture or vendor master alone.. Existence Justification: In sports entertainment operations, a single fixture (match, concert, PPV event) requires MANY vendors simultaneously — catering, security, AV/broadcast, merchandise, medical, transportation — each activated for that specific event. Conversely, a single vendor (e.g., a security firm or catering company) operates across MANY fixtures per season.   grp decimal(10,4) [note: 'The sum of all ratings achieved by a broadcast schedule or campaign, calculated as reach multiplied by frequency. GRP (Gross Rating Points) is the standard advertising currency metric used by sponsors and media buyers to evaluate the total weight of a broadcast buy. Critical for sponsorship ROI and CPM (Cost Per Mille) reporting.']
  household_rating decimal(8,4) [note: 'The percentage of all television households in the measured market that were tuned to this broadcast during the measurement window. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0850 = 8.50%). The foundational Nielsen linear TV currency metric used in media rights deal negotiations and CPM (Cost Per Mille) calculations.']
  is_live_event boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this audience measurement record pertains to a live broadcast of a sports or entertainment event (True) or a recorded/replay/VOD broadcast (False). Live event measurements command premium CPM rates and are treated differently in rights valuation models.']
  is_ppv boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this audience measurement record is for a PPV (Pay-Per-View) broadcast (True) or a standard broadcast (False). PPV audience measurement uses different methodologies and is reported separately for rights valuation and revenue attribution.']
  live_viewers varchar [note: 'The number of viewers who watched the broadcast live (same-day, same-time as the original airing). Distinct from time-shifted viewers. Live viewership is the primary metric for live sports events and is used in real-time sponsorship exposure calculations.']
  measurement_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the audience measurement was recorded or the broadcast window occurred. Used for day-level reporting, trend analysis, and alignment with Nielsen overnight ratings release schedules.']
  measurement_methodology varchar [note: 'The statistical methodology used to derive the audience measurement. Panel-based uses a representative sample audience panel (Nielsen People Meter); census-based uses complete server-side stream counts; hybrid combines panel and census data; modeled uses statistical inference; self-reported relies on partner-submitted data.']
  measurement_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for capturing qualitative context about this audience measurement record, such as methodology caveats, data quality flags, extraordinary circumstances affecting viewership (e.g., weather events, competing programming), or notes from the measurement provider regarding revisions.']
  measurement_reference_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier assigned by the measurement provider (e.g., Nielsen report code, Comscore measurement ID, internal OTT telemetry batch reference). Used for cross-referencing with third-party measurement reports.']
  measurement_source varchar [note: 'The organization or system that produced this audience measurement. Nielsen provides linear TV panel-based ratings; Comscore provides digital and cross-platform measurement; internal_ott refers to first-party OTT telemetry from the Sports Entertainment streaming platform; Adobe_AEP refers to Adobe Experience Platform analytics; partner_reported refers to data submitted by broadcast partners; manual refers to manually entered estimates.']
  measurement_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the audience measurement record. Preliminary ratings are released within 24 hours; final ratings are certified after audience panel reconciliation; revised ratings reflect post-publication corrections; disputed records are under review; withdrawn records have been retracted by the measurement provider.']
  measurement_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The principal real-world date and time at which the audience measurement observation was captured or the measurement window began. Represents the business event time, distinct from record audit timestamps. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).']
  measurement_window_end timestamp [note: 'The end date and time of the audience measurement window. Combined with measurement_window_start to define the total measurement duration. Used for AMA (Average Minute Audience) calculation and broadcast window performance analysis.']
  measurement_window_start timestamp [note: 'The start date and time of the audience measurement window. For live events this is the broadcast start time; for time-shifted viewing this is the start of the measurement interval. Used to calculate AMA (Average Minute Audience) and other time-based metrics.']
  ott_concurrent_streams varchar [note: 'The number of simultaneous active OTT (Over-The-Top) streaming sessions at the peak measurement point during the broadcast window. Distinct from total unique viewers as one viewer may have multiple device streams. Sourced from internal OTT telemetry or Adobe Experience Platform.']
  peak_concurrent_viewers varchar [note: 'The maximum number of viewers simultaneously watching the broadcast at any single point during the measurement window. Critical for OTT (Over-The-Top) infrastructure capacity planning and for reporting record-breaking viewership moments to sponsors and rights holders.']
  persons_rating decimal(8,4) [note: 'The percentage of all persons in the measured demographic universe who were watching this broadcast during the measurement window. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0620 = 6.20%). Used alongside household_rating for demographic-specific advertising CPM (Cost Per Mille) pricing.']
  share_of_voice decimal(8,4) [note: 'The proportion of total sports broadcast viewership in the market captured by this event\'s broadcast, expressed as a decimal. Measures competitive dominance of the Sports Entertainment property relative to competing sports and entertainment programming. Key input for sponsorship ROI and media rights valuation.']
  sport_type varchar [note: 'The sport or entertainment category of the event being broadcast (e.g., \'NFL Football\', \'NBA Basketball\', \'MLB Baseball\', \'NHL Hockey\', \'MLS Soccer\', \'UFC MMA\', \'Concert\', \'Award Show\'). Used for cross-sport audience benchmarking and genre-level rights valuation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: nfl_football|nba_basketball|mlb_baseball|nhl_hockey|mls_soccer|ufc_mma|concert|award_show|tennis|golf — promote to reference product]']
  time_shifted_viewers varchar [note: 'The number of viewers who watched the broadcast on a time-shifted basis (DVR, VOD, catch-up TV) within the standard measurement window (typically C3 or C7 — 3 or 7 days post-broadcast). Time-shifted viewing is included in Nielsen C3/C7 ratings used for advertising currency.']
  total_unique_viewers varchar [note: 'The total count of unduplicated individual viewers who watched any portion of the broadcast during the measurement window. Represents reach — the number of distinct people exposed to the content. Core metric for broadcast rights valuation and sponsorship ROI reporting.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Audit timestamp recording when this audience measurement record was last modified, such as when preliminary ratings are replaced by final certified ratings or when a revision is applied.']
  viewing_duration_minutes decimal(10,2) [note: 'The average number of minutes that viewers in the measured audience spent watching the broadcast during the measurement window. Expressed in minutes. Used alongside AMA (Average Minute Audience) to assess audience engagement depth and content stickiness.']

  Note: 'Broadcast and digital audience measurement records capturing viewership, reach, and engagement metrics per event and broadcast window — Nielsen linear TV ratings, OTT concurrent streams, average minute audience (AMA), total unique viewers, peak concurrent viewers, completion rate, and share of voice. Captures measurement source (Nielsen, Comscore, internal OTT telemetry), measurement methodology, geographic market, demographic breakdown reference, broadcast channel reference, and event reference. SSOT for audience performance data consumed by broadcast rights valuation and sponsorship ROI.'
}

  promotion_decision varchar [note: 'Outcome decision made by the data science team and stakeholders upon experiment conclusion. \'promote\' triggers model registration and production deployment pipeline; \'abandon\' closes the experiment; \'iterate\' spawns a follow-on experiment; \'pending\' awaits review.']

  review_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes recorded by the reviewer during the promotion decision review. Captures concerns, conditions, or recommendations that informed the final promotion decision.']
  start_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the experiment was formally initiated and the first MLflow run was registered. Used for experiment duration tracking and sprint planning.']
  target_end_date date [note: 'Planned completion date for the experiment as agreed during sprint or project planning. Compared against actual end_date to measure delivery adherence.']

  training_data_start_date date [note: 'Earliest date of the historical data window used to train models in this experiment. Defines the temporal scope of the training dataset for reproducibility and data freshness assessment.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this experiment record. Conforms to ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used to detect stale records and support incremental Silver layer processing.']
  uses_pii boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this experiment uses personally identifiable information (PII) such as fan profiles, purchase history, or behavioral data. Triggers mandatory Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) review and GDPR/CCPA compliance checks.']
  wada_compliance_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this experiment involves athlete performance or biometric data subject to World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) regulations. When true, additional data handling restrictions and audit requirements apply.']

  Note: 'Data science experiment record tracking hypothesis-driven analytical investigations and model development experiments within the Sports Entertainment MLflow tracking environment. Distinct from platform.ab_test which covers fan-facing UX experiments — this covers internal data science model experiments.'

  attendance_score_weight decimal(5,4) [note: 'Weighting coefficient (0.0000–1.0000) applied to the attendance frequency score in the composite index calculation. Sum of all dimension weights must equal 1.0000. Enables model recalibration without reprocessing raw data.']
  broadcast_consumption_score decimal(7,4) [note: 'Normalized sub-score (0.0000–100.0000) representing fan broadcast and media consumption engagement including live TV viewership, OTT streaming hours, PPV purchases, and RSN viewing frequency. Sourced from broadcast audience rating systems.']
  broadcast_score_weight decimal(5,4) [note: 'Weighting coefficient (0.0000–1.0000) applied to the broadcast consumption score in the composite index calculation. Enables model recalibration without reprocessing raw data.']
  composite_score decimal(7,4) [note: 'Normalized composite engagement index value (0.0000–100.0000) aggregating all engagement dimension scores into a single health metric. Serves as the primary KPI on executive dashboards for fan engagement health.']
  computation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Exact date and time when the engagement index computation pipeline executed and produced this record. Distinct from the period dates; used for pipeline audit and SLA monitoring.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this engagement index record was first inserted into the Silver Layer table. System-generated audit field for data lineage and pipeline traceability.']
  data_classification varchar [note: 'Data sensitivity classification for this engagement index record per the enterprise data governance policy. Determines access controls and handling requirements.']
  data_completeness_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of expected input signals that were successfully received and processed for this index computation (0.00–100.00). Values below threshold may indicate data quality issues and should be flagged for review before publishing.']
  digital_activity_score decimal(7,4) [note: 'Normalized sub-score (0.0000–100.0000) representing fan engagement on owned digital platforms including app usage, website visits, OTT streaming sessions, and DTC content consumption. Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform.']
  digital_activity_score_weight decimal(5,4) [note: 'Weighting coefficient (0.0000–1.0000) applied to the digital platform activity score in the composite index calculation. Enables model recalibration without reprocessing raw data.']
  entity_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable display name of the entity for which the engagement index is computed (e.g., \'NBA Season Ticket Holders\', \'Los Angeles Lakers\', \'Staples Center\'). Denormalized for dashboard readability.']
  entity_type varchar [note: 'Discriminator indicating the type of business entity for which this engagement index is computed. Determines which entity reference FK is populated (fan_segment_id, league_id, venue_id, or event_id).']
  fan_population_count varchar [note: 'Number of distinct fans or fan accounts included in the engagement index computation for this entity and period. Provides denominator context for interpreting the composite score magnitude.']
  geographic_scope varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the primary geographic market for this engagement index record. Used for regional segmentation and GDPR/CCPA compliance scoping.']
  index_code varchar [note: 'Business-facing unique code identifying this engagement index record, encoding entity type, entity reference, and period (e.g., EI-NBAFAN-2024W12). Used as the externally-known identifier on executive dashboards.']
  index_model_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the engagement index computation model used to produce this record (e.g., \'v2.1.0\'). Enables reproducibility, audit, and comparison across model versions. Links to the fan_behavior_model registry.']
  index_period_type varchar [note: 'Granularity of the engagement index computation period. Determines whether the index represents a weekly, monthly, seasonal, or annual aggregation window.']
  index_status varchar [note: 'Lifecycle status of this engagement index record. \'draft\' indicates computation in progress; \'published\' indicates approved and available for dashboards; \'superseded\' indicates replaced by a revised record; \'retracted\' indicates withdrawn due to data quality issues.']
  is_baseline_period boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this index record represents the designated baseline period against which future engagement scores are benchmarked. True for the reference period established during model calibration.']
  is_published_to_dashboard boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this engagement index record has been approved and published to executive KPI dashboards. False for draft or retracted records.']
  loyalty_score decimal(7,4) [note: 'Normalized sub-score (0.0000–100.0000) representing fan loyalty program engagement including points earned, redemptions, tier progression, and program tenure. Sourced from Salesforce CRM.']
  loyalty_score_weight decimal(5,4) [note: 'Weighting coefficient (0.0000–1.0000) applied to the loyalty program participation score in the composite index calculation. Enables model recalibration without reprocessing raw data.']
  merchandise_score decimal(7,4) [note: 'Normalized sub-score (0.0000–100.0000) representing merchandise purchasing engagement based on recency, frequency, and breadth of SKU purchases. Sourced from Shopify Plus e-commerce platform.']
  merchandise_score_weight decimal(5,4) [note: 'Weighting coefficient (0.0000–1.0000) applied to the merchandise purchase recency score in the composite index calculation. Enables model recalibration without reprocessing raw data.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for analyst annotations, data quality observations, or contextual commentary about this engagement index record (e.g., \'Score impacted by venue closure during period\', \'Revised after broadcast data restatement\').']
  nps_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Net Promoter Score (-100.00 to 100.00) for the entity during the index period, representing fan likelihood to recommend. Sourced from fan survey data in Salesforce CRM and Adobe Experience Platform. Contextualizes the composite engagement index.']
  period_end_date date [note: 'Last calendar date of the engagement measurement window for this index record. Combined with period_start_date defines the exact aggregation interval.']
  period_start_date date [note: 'First calendar date of the engagement measurement window for this index record. Combined with period_end_date defines the exact aggregation interval.']
  prior_period_composite_score decimal(7,4) [note: 'Composite engagement score from the immediately preceding equivalent period (e.g., prior week, prior month, prior season). Stored to enable period-over-period variance analysis without requiring a self-join.']
  published_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this engagement index record was approved and published to executive dashboards. Null if index_status is not \'published\'. Supports audit trail for governance.']
  score_change_pct decimal(7,4) [note: 'Percentage change in composite engagement score versus the prior equivalent period. Positive values indicate improvement; negative values indicate decline. Used for trend alerting and executive reporting.']
  social_media_score decimal(7,4) [note: 'Normalized sub-score (0.0000–100.0000) representing fan social media engagement including mentions, shares, reactions, UGC creation, and hashtag participation related to the entity. Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform social listening.']
  social_media_score_weight decimal(5,4) [note: 'Weighting coefficient (0.0000–1.0000) applied to the social media interaction score in the composite index calculation. Enables model recalibration without reprocessing raw data.']
  trend_direction varchar [note: 'Directional indicator comparing the composite engagement score to the prior equivalent period. Derived from the delta between current and prior composite scores and used for executive traffic-light reporting.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this engagement index record was last modified (e.g., score revision, status change, weight recalibration). System-generated audit field for change tracking.']

  Note: 'Periodic fan engagement index record computing a composite engagement score for a fan segment, league, venue, or event — combining attendance frequency, digital platform activity, merchandise purchase recency, loyalty program participation, social media interaction, and broadcast consumption signals into a normalized index value. Captures index period (weekly, monthly, seasonal), entity type (fan segment, franchise, event), entity reference, composite index value, component score breakdown by dimension, and index trend direction vs. prior period. Serves as the Silver Layer engagement health record for executive dashboards.'
}

  is_resulted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the betting market has been officially resulted/settled (True) or is still open/pending (False). A resulted market has a confirmed outcome and all bets have been settled.']
  is_suspended boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the betting market was suspended at the time of this odds update (True = suspended, False = tradeable). Suspension may be triggered by significant events (e.g., red card, injury, VAR review, TMO decision) or risk management actions.']
  jurisdiction_code varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country/state code identifying the regulatory jurisdiction under which this odds feed record is governed. Critical for jurisdiction-specific compliance, licensing, and regulatory reporting (e.g., US state-level gaming regulations, GDPR for EU).']
  line_movement_direction varchar [note: 'Indicates the direction of the odds movement relative to the previous update for this selection. \'up\' means odds lengthened (selection less favoured); \'down\' means odds shortened (selection more favoured); \'unchanged\' means no movement; \'open\' is the first price; \'close\' is the final price before event start.']
  market_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the betting market type for this odds update (e.g., match_result, over_under, handicap, first_goalscorer, prop_bet, futures, outright). Supports market-level analytics and regulatory reporting segmentation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: match_result|over_under|handicap|first_goalscorer|prop_bet|futures|outright — promote to reference product]']
  max_stake_amount decimal(14,2) [note: 'The maximum single bet stake permitted on this selection at the time of this odds update, in the operating currency. Reflects risk management limits set by the trading desk. Confidential as it reveals internal risk appetite.']
  min_stake_amount decimal(14,2) [note: 'The minimum single bet stake permitted on this selection at the time of this odds update, in the operating currency. Enforced at point of bet acceptance.']
  odds_format varchar [note: 'The primary odds format in which this update was received from the provider. Determines which odds value field is the authoritative source. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: decimal|fractional|american|hongkong|malay|indonesian — promote to reference product]']
  overround_pct decimal(8,4) [note: 'The bookmaker\'s margin (vigorish/vig) expressed as a percentage, calculated as the sum of all implied probabilities for a market minus 100%. Represents the theoretical profit margin built into the odds. Used for pricing analytics and margin monitoring.']
  previous_decimal_odds decimal(10,6) [note: 'The decimal odds value from the immediately preceding odds update for this selection and market. Enables line movement magnitude calculation and trend analysis without requiring a self-join.']
  price_boost_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the odds for this selection have been artificially enhanced as part of a promotional price boost offer (True) or reflect standard market pricing (False). Price boosts are a common fan engagement and DTC acquisition tool.']
  provider_published_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which the odds provider published or generated this odds update on their end. Used to calculate feed latency (received_timestamp minus provider_published_timestamp) and for regulatory audit trails.']
  received_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (with millisecond precision and timezone offset) at which this odds update message was received from the provider feed. Principal business event timestamp for latency measurement and audit.']
  regulatory_reporting_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this odds feed record must be included in regulatory filings or reports to gaming authorities in the applicable jurisdiction (True). Supports automated regulatory reporting workflows and SOX/CCPA/GDPR compliance.']
  responsible_gaming_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this odds feed record has been flagged for responsible gaming review (True), for example due to unusual line movement that may indicate integrity concerns, or market conditions that trigger enhanced monitoring under WADA or governing body integrity frameworks.']
  result_outcome varchar [note: 'The official result outcome for this selection once the market has been resulted. \'win\' = selection won; \'lose\' = selection lost; \'void\' = bet voided; \'push\' = stake returned (tie); \'half_win\'/\'half_lose\' = Asian handicap partial outcomes. Null until market is resulted.']
  sequence_number varchar [note: 'Sequential message number assigned by the odds provider within their feed stream for this market or session. Used to detect out-of-order delivery, gaps in the feed, and to reconstruct the correct chronological order of odds updates.']
  source_market_reference varchar [note: 'The provider\'s own internal market identifier or reference code for this betting market, as supplied in the feed message. Enables direct reconciliation with the provider\'s system without requiring a reverse lookup.']
  sport_code varchar [note: 'Standardised short code identifying the sport associated with this odds feed record (e.g., NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, MLS, UFC, ATP). Enables cross-sport analytics and jurisdiction-specific regulatory reporting.']
  suspension_reason varchar [note: 'Descriptive reason for market suspension when is_suspended is True (e.g., \'VAR_REVIEW\', \'INJURY_STOPPAGE\', \'RISK_MANAGEMENT\', \'FEED_OUTAGE\', \'REGULATORY_HOLD\'). Null when market is not suspended. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: VAR_REVIEW|INJURY_STOPPAGE|RISK_MANAGEMENT|FEED_OUTAGE|REGULATORY_HOLD|MANUAL — promote to reference product]']
  total_line_value decimal(6,2) [note: 'The total points/goals/runs line value for over/under markets (e.g., 2.5 goals, 47.5 points). Null for non-totals markets. Used in conjunction with market_type to define the exact market being priced.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this odds feed record was last modified in the Silver layer lakehouse. Supports incremental processing and change data capture.']

  Note: 'High-frequency transactional record of odds price updates received from odds compilers and third-party odds providers (e.g., Sportradar, Kambi) for each betting market. Captures market ID, selection ID, decimal/fractional/American odds format values, implied probability, line movement direction, feed source, timestamp of update, and feed status. Supports real-time odds display, line movement analytics, and audit trails for regulatory compliance.'
}

  regulatory_report_id varchar [note: 'The identifier of the regulatory filing or suspicious activity report (SAR) that this wager was included in, if applicable. Used for AML compliance tracking and regulatory audit trail. Null if no regulatory report has been filed for this wager.']

Business justification: Wagers generate GGR attributed to revenue streams by sport_type, league_code, and distribution_channel. This link enables real-time GGR attribution to finance.revenue_stream for financial reporting, r']

  cashout_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'The monetary amount offered and accepted by the bettor when exercising the early cash-out option. Null if the wager was not cashed out. Represents the sportsbook\'s real-time liability reduction value.']
  cashout_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the bettor exercised the early cash-out option, if applicable. Null if the wager was not cashed out early. Used for cash-out feature analytics and liability management.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this wager record was first created in the sportsbook system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts on this wager (stake, payout, settlement). Supports multi-currency sportsbook operations across international jurisdictions (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR, CAD).']
  device_fingerprint varchar [note: 'Anonymized or hashed identifier of the device used to place the wager.   geolocation_country varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code where the bettor was physically located at time of wager placement. Used for international jurisdiction compliance and cross-border wagering restriction enforcement.']

  odds_at_placement decimal(10,4) [note: 'The decimal odds offered to the bettor at the exact moment the wager was placed. Locked in at placement time and used for payout calculation. Stored in decimal format (e.g., 2.50 = evens +100 American odds) regardless of display format shown to bettor.']
  odds_format varchar [note: 'The odds display format presented to the bettor at time of placement (e.g., \'american\' for +150/-110, \'decimal\' for 2.50, \'fractional\' for 3/2). Stored for display reconciliation and international market compliance.']

  placement_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time (with timezone) when the wager was accepted and confirmed by the sportsbook platform. This is the principal business event timestamp and is critical for in-play betting validation, regulatory reporting, and audit trails.']
  potential_payout decimal(18,4) [note: 'The maximum gross payout amount the bettor would receive if the wager wins, calculated as stake_amount multiplied by odds_at_placement. Captured at placement time for liability management and bettor communication.']
  potential_profit decimal(18,4) [note: 'The net profit the bettor would receive if the wager wins, calculated as potential_payout minus stake_amount. Represents the bettor\'s net gain and is used in responsible gaming exposure monitoring.']
  promotion_code varchar [note: 'The promotional or bonus code applied to this wager, if any. Used to track the effectiveness of marketing campaigns, bonus offers, and acquisition promotions. Null if no promotion was applied.']
  reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally visible alphanumeric reference number presented to the bettor on their bet slip or receipt. Used for customer service inquiries, dispute resolution, and regulatory audit trails.']
  responsible_gaming_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this wager triggered a responsible gaming alert or intervention at time of placement (e.g., exceeded deposit limit, velocity threshold, or self-exclusion proximity check). Used for regulatory compliance reporting and player protection monitoring.']
  selection_description varchar [note: 'Human-readable description of the bettor\'s selection within the betting market (e.g., \'Kansas City Chiefs to win\', \'Over 48.5 total points\', \'LeBron James to score 30+ points\'). Captured at time of placement for audit and display purposes.']
  self_exclusion_override boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this wager was placed despite a self-exclusion or cooling-off period being active on the bettor\'s account. Should always be False for compliant operations; True values require immediate regulatory escalation.']
  settlement_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'The actual monetary amount paid out to the bettor upon settlement. For winning wagers this equals the gross payout; for losing wagers this is zero; for void/push wagers this equals the stake returned. Null until the wager is settled.']
  settlement_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the wager outcome was determined and the settlement amount was applied to the bettor\'s account. Null for pending wagers. Used for settlement cycle reporting and regulatory compliance.']
  stake_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'The monetary amount wagered by the bettor at time of placement, in the transaction currency. Represents the bettor\'s financial exposure and is the basis for hold calculations and regulatory reporting.']
  tax_withheld_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'The amount of tax withheld from the settlement payout at source, as required by applicable jurisdiction tax laws (e.g., US federal withholding on large winnings per IRS Form W-2G thresholds). Zero if no withholding applies.']
  ticket_terminal_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the specific betting terminal, kiosk, or point-of-sale device used to place the wager. Used for terminal-level reconciliation, fraud detection, and equipment audit trails in retail and kiosk channels.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this wager record was last modified in the sportsbook system (e.g., status change from pending to settled). Used for change data capture and audit compliance.']
  void_reason varchar [note: 'The reason code explaining why a wager was voided. Null for non-voided wagers. Used for operational reporting, bettor communication, and regulatory audit. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: event_cancelled|event_postponed|market_error|odds_error|bettor_request|regulatory_order|system_error|integrity_concern — promote to reference product]']
  wager_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the wager. \'pending\' indicates the event has not yet concluded; \'won\'/\'lost\' reflect settled outcomes; \'void\' indicates cancellation (e.g., event postponed); \'cashed_out\' reflects early cash-out by bettor; \'pushed\' indicates a tie/refund outcome.']
  wager_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the wager structure. \'straight\' is a single-selection bet; \'parlay\' combines multiple selections for higher payout; \'teaser\' adjusts point spreads; \'prop\' is a proposition bet on specific in-game events; \'futures\' bets on season-long outcomes; \'round_robin\' is a series of parlays. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: straight|parlay|teaser|prop|futures|round_robin|if_bet|reverse — promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Core transactional record of every individual bet placed by a registered bettor across all wagering channels — retail sportsbook, mobile app, kiosk, and online platform. Captures bettor account ID, betting market ID, selection, stake amount, odds at time of placement, potential payout, wager type (straight, parlay, teaser, prop), placement channel, placement timestamp, wager status (pending, won, lost, void, cashed out), settlement amount, and settlement timestamp. Primary transactional entity for sportsbook operations and regulatory reporting.'

Table gaming.prop_bet {

  leg_odds_contribution decimal(10,6) [note: 'The decimal multiplier this leg contributes to the overall combined parlay odds. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|teaser|pleaser|if_bet|reverse|round_robin — promote to reference product]']

  pick_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time this individual pick selection was made during the draft. Supports pick-level audit, time-on-clock analytics, and draft replay functionality.']
  pick_value_score decimal(6,2) [note: 'A calculated draft value score representing the difference between the athlete\'s ADP and the actual overall pick number. Positive values indicate a value pick; negative values indicate a reach. Supports draft grade analytics.']
  pick_within_round varchar [note: 'The ordinal position of this pick within its specific round (e.g., 3rd pick in round 2). Supports snake-draft order validation and round-level pick sequencing.']
  pre_draft_rank varchar [note: 'The platform\'s consensus or algorithmic pre-draft ranking of the selected athlete prior to the draft event. Used for draft grade analytics, reach/value calculations, and pick quality scoring.']
  responsible_gaming_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a responsible gaming intervention or alert was triggered for the participating user during this draft event. Supports regulatory compliance reporting and player protection programs.']
  roster_slot varchar [note: 'The designated roster slot on the fantasy team to which this athlete was assigned at the time of the draft pick (e.g., FLEX, BENCH, STARTER). Supports roster construction analytics and lineup compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: starter|flex|bench|ir|taxi|reserve — promote to reference product]']
  round_number varchar [note: 'The round within the draft in which this pick was made. Used for draft grade analytics, positional scarcity analysis, and round-by-round pick distribution reporting.']
  scoring_format varchar [note: 'The scoring ruleset applied to this fantasy draft, such as standard, Points Per Reception (PPR), half-PPR, or auction. Determines athlete valuation and draft strategy context for analytics.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which this fantasy draft record originated (e.g., Adobe Experience Platform, internal gaming engine, third-party API). Supports data lineage and silver-layer reconciliation.']
  sport_type varchar [note: 'The professional sport associated with this fantasy draft, identifying the governing league and scoring ruleset context. Supports multi-sport platform analytics and regulatory jurisdiction mapping. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NFL|NBA|MLB|NHL|MLS|PGA|NASCAR|UFC — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  time_used_seconds varchar [note: 'The actual number of seconds the team manager used before submitting this pick. Enables pick-clock utilization analytics and identification of slow-draft patterns.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time this fantasy draft record was last modified in the data platform. Supports change data capture, audit trail, and data quality monitoring in the Databricks silver layer.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of the fantasy league draft event and all individual pick selections. Captures draft event date/time, draft type, draft order, each pick\'s round number, overall pick number, fantasy team making the pick, athlete selected, pick timestamp, and whether the pick was auto-selected. Supports draft history, draft grade analytics, and audit of athlete allocation across fantasy teams.'
}

  trade_value_score_receiving decimal(8,2) [note: 'Algorithmic trade fairness score representing the estimated fantasy value of assets received by the initiating team in a trade.   transaction_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally visible alphanumeric reference number assigned to this transaction, used in user-facing confirmations, dispute resolution, and audit trails. Follows the format TXN- followed by 8-20 alphanumeric characters.']

  transaction_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the fantasy team submitted or initiated this transaction. This is the principal business event timestamp used for waiver priority ordering, FAAB auction timing, and trade proposal sequencing.']
  transaction_type varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the roster move: waiver_claim (athlete claimed off waivers using priority), free_agent_pickup (athlete added from free agency without waiver process), drop (athlete released to waivers or free agency), trade (bilateral exchange between two fantasy teams), commissioner_move (administrative roster adjustment by commissioner).']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Audit timestamp recording when this transaction record was most recently modified, such as when status changed from pending to processed or when a commissioner override was applied.']

Linking to finance.tax_jurisdiction provides authoritative withholding rates for wallet-level tax compliance. Required for accurate ']

  kyc_verified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the bettor\'s identity has been fully verified through the Know Your Customer (KYC) process. True = verified; False = pending or failed. Unverified wallets may have restricted deposit and withdrawal capabilities.']

  real_money_balance decimal(18,4) [note: 'Current spendable real-money balance in the wallet denominated in currency_code. Represents deposited funds net of withdrawals, settled wager losses, and fees. Excludes bonus credits and pending holds.']
  reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally visible alphanumeric reference number for the gaming wallet, used in customer communications, support tickets, and regulatory filings. Distinct from the internal surrogate key.']
  reserved_withdrawal_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Amount currently reserved for a pending withdrawal request that has been initiated but not yet processed or cleared by the payment processor. Reduces available withdrawable_balance.']
  self_exclusion_end_date date [note: 'Date on which the bettor\'s self-exclusion period expires and the wallet may be reactivated, subject to a mandatory cooling-off review. NULL if self-exclusion is permanent or not active.']
  self_exclusion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the bettor has voluntarily enrolled in a self-exclusion program, prohibiting all wagering activity on this wallet. True = self-excluded; False = not self-excluded. Triggers immediate wallet suspension.']

  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational gaming platform or system of record from which this wallet record originates (e.g., SPORTSBOOK_PLATFORM, FANTASY_ENGINE). Supports data lineage and multi-platform reconciliation in the lakehouse.']
  tax_withholding_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether federal or state tax withholding is currently applied to winnings paid out from this wallet (e.g., IRS backup withholding for bettors who have not provided a valid TIN). True = withholding active.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this gaming wallet record in the platform ledger. Used for change data capture (CDC), audit trails, and Silver layer incremental processing.']
  wager_limit_daily decimal(18,4) [note: 'Maximum total wagering stake permitted within a rolling 24-hour period for this wallet. Enforced at bet placement to support responsible gaming compliance.']
  wallet_status varchar [note: 'Current operational lifecycle state of the gaming wallet. \'active\' = fully operational; \'suspended\' = temporarily restricted by operator or regulator; \'frozen\' = locked pending investigation or AML review; \'closed\' = permanently deactivated; \'pending_verification\' = KYC/AML checks incomplete.']
  wallet_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the wallet by gaming product line. Determines which bet types, markets, and regulatory rules apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sports_wagering|fantasy_sports|casino|poker|combined — promote to reference product if additional types emerge]']
  withdrawable_balance decimal(18,4) [note: 'Portion of the real-money balance that has met all wagering requirements and regulatory hold periods and is eligible for withdrawal to the bettor\'s registered payment method. May be less than or equal to real_money_balance.']

  Note: 'Financial ledger record for each bettor account\'s gaming wallet — tracking real-money balance, bonus balance, withdrawable balance, pending wager holds, and lifetime deposit/withdrawal totals. Distinct from fan.payment_method (stored payment instruments) — this is the in-platform gaming funds ledger.'

True = KYC complete; False = KYC pending or incomplete. Transactions processed without KYC may be subject to regulatory scrutiny.']
  net_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Net amount credited or debited to the bettor\'s wallet after deducting fees and tax withholding from the gross transaction_amount. Calculated as: transaction_amount - fee_amount - tax_withheld_amount. Represents the actual wallet impact and is the authoritative amount for balance reconciliation.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for operational notes added by gaming operations staff, such as manual adjustment justifications, customer service resolution notes, or compliance review comments. Supports audit trail for manual interventions.']
  payment_method_type varchar [note: 'The category of payment instrument used for deposit or withdrawal transactions (e.g., credit_card, debit_card, bank_transfer, e_wallet, prepaid_card, cryptocurrency, voucher). Not applicable for internal wallet movements such as wager_stake or wager_settlement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: credit_card|debit_card|bank_transfer|e_wallet|prepaid_card|cryptocurrency|voucher — promote to reference product]']
  payment_provider_reference varchar [note: 'External transaction identifier returned by the payment gateway or processor (e.g., Stripe charge ID, PayPal transaction ID, bank wire reference). Used for reconciliation with the payment provider and chargeback dispute management. Stored as a tokenized or masked reference per PCI DSS.']
  post_transaction_balance decimal(18,4) [note: 'The bettor\'s wallet balance immediately after this transaction was applied. Used to verify ledger consistency (pre_transaction_balance ± transaction_amount = post_transaction_balance) and for responsible gaming balance monitoring.']
  pre_transaction_balance decimal(18,4) [note: 'The bettor\'s wallet balance immediately before this transaction was applied. Captured as a point-in-time snapshot for ledger integrity verification, dispute resolution, and responsible gaming spend analysis.']
  processing_latency_ms varchar [note: 'Time in milliseconds between the transaction initiation timestamp and the completion/failure timestamp. Used for SLA monitoring of payment processing performance and identification of system degradation events affecting bettor experience.']
  responsible_gaming_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this transaction triggered a responsible gaming alert, such as exceeding the bettor\'s self-imposed deposit limit, spend limit, or session time limit. True = responsible gaming threshold breached; False = within limits. Supports regulatory responsible gaming compliance reporting.']
  reversal_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded reason explaining why a transaction was reversed or cancelled (e.g., chargeback, duplicate transaction, system error, fraud confirmed, bettor request). Populated only when transaction_status is reversed or cancelled. Required for dispute management and audit trail.']
  self_exclusion_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the bettor had an active self-exclusion or cooling-off period in effect at the time of this transaction. True = self-exclusion was active (transaction should have been blocked — used for compliance breach investigation); False = no active self-exclusion. Critical for responsible gaming regulatory compliance.']
  tax_withheld_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Amount of tax withheld from this transaction by the gaming operator on behalf of the applicable tax authority (e.g., federal withholding on large wager settlements in the US per IRS Form W-2G threshold). Zero for non-taxable transactions. Required for IRS and state tax regulatory reporting.']
  transaction_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Gross monetary value of the fund movement in the transaction currency. Always expressed as a positive number; the direction of the movement (debit or credit) is determined by transaction_type and debit_credit_indicator. Used for AML transaction monitoring thresholds and responsible gaming spend limits.']
  transaction_reference varchar [note: 'Externally visible, human-readable reference code assigned to this transaction. Used for customer service inquiries, reconciliation, and regulatory reporting. Sourced from the gaming platform ledger.']
  transaction_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the wallet transaction: pending (initiated, awaiting processing), completed (successfully settled), failed (processing error), reversed (rolled back after completion), cancelled (voided before processing), under_review (flagged for AML or responsible gaming review).']
  transaction_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which the fund movement event occurred in the gaming platform. This is the principal business event time used for financial reconciliation, AML monitoring, and responsible gaming spend tracking.']
  transaction_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the fund movement event: deposit (funds added from external payment method), withdrawal (funds sent to external account), wager_stake (funds deducted for a placed bet), wager_settlement (funds credited or debited upon bet outcome), bonus_credit (promotional funds added), bonus_forfeiture (unused bonus funds removed), adjustment (manual correction by operations). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: deposit|withdrawal|wager_stake|wager_settlement|bonus_credit|bonus_forfeiture|adjustment — promote to reference product]']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this wallet transaction record was last modified, such as a status change from pending to completed or a reversal event. Supports audit trail and Silver layer change tracking.']
  wallet_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the wallet segment affected by this transaction: real_money (actual deposited funds), bonus (promotional bonus credits), promotional (free-bet or free-play credits), pending_withdrawal (funds earmarked for withdrawal but not yet disbursed). Determines wagering eligibility and withdrawal rules.']

  Note: 'Transactional ledger entry for every movement of funds within a bettor\'s gaming wallet — deposits, withdrawals, wager stakes, wager settlements, bonus credits, bonus forfeitures, and adjustments. Captures transaction type, amount, currency, pre-transaction balance, post-transaction balance, reference wager ID or deposit ID, payment method reference, timestamp, and transaction status. Supports AML transaction monitoring, responsible gaming spend tracking, and financial reconciliation.'
}

  online_wagering_permitted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether online and mobile sports wagering is permitted in this jurisdiction, as distinct from retail (in-person) wagering. True = online/mobile wagering authorized; False = retail only.']
  promotional_deduction_allowed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the jurisdiction permits deduction of promotional credits and free-play bonuses from gross gaming revenue before calculating the taxable GGR base. True = deductions permitted; False = gross revenue taxed without promotional deductions.']
  prop_bet_permitted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether proposition bets (prop bets) on individual player or game-specific outcomes are permitted in this jurisdiction. Some jurisdictions restrict prop bets on college athletes or specific leagues. True = prop bets authorized; False = restricted.']
  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this gaming jurisdiction record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this gaming jurisdiction record was most recently modified. Used for change detection, incremental data pipeline processing, and audit compliance.']
  region_or_state varchar [note: 'Name of the sub-national administrative region, state, or province within the country (e.g., New Jersey, Nevada, Ontario, England). Null for country-level jurisdictions. Supports state-level regulatory mapping.']
  reporting_frequency varchar [note: 'Frequency at which Sports Entertainment must submit regulatory compliance and financial reports to the governing authority in this jurisdiction. Drives automated report generation scheduling.']
  responsible_gaming_mandates varchar [note: 'Free-text description of applicable responsible gaming compliance mandates imposed by the regulatory authority in this jurisdiction, including deposit limits, loss limits, session time limits, cooling-off periods, and problem gambling helpline display requirements.']

Operators must integrate with this program as a condition of licensure.']

SSOT for jurisdiction-level compliance configuration.'

  platform_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the specific gaming platform or product (e.g., sports wagering app, fantasy sports platform, online casino) from which the bettor is excluded. Relevant when exclusion_scope is single_platform.']
  regulatory_notification_status varchar [note: 'Tracks the status of the mandatory regulatory notification submission to the governing gaming authority.   reinstatement_approval_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the bettor\'s reinstatement request. not_requested indicates no request has been filed; pending indicates under review; approved indicates reinstatement granted; denied indicates request rejected; withdrawn indicates bettor withdrew the request.']
  reinstatement_approved_date date [note: 'The date on which the reinstatement request was formally approved by the operator and/or regulatory authority, allowing the bettor to resume gaming activities. Null if reinstatement has not been approved.']
  reinstatement_cooling_off_days varchar [note: 'The mandatory cooling-off period in days that must elapse after a reinstatement request before the bettor can be reinstated. Defined by jurisdictional regulation or operator policy.']
  reinstatement_request_date date [note: 'The date on which the excluded bettor formally submitted a request to be reinstated to gaming activities. Null if no reinstatement has been requested. Triggers the reinstatement review workflow.']
  responsible_gaming_counseling_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the bettor is required to complete a responsible gaming counseling or assessment program as a condition of reinstatement. Driven by operator policy or regulatory mandate.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Identifies the operational system of record from which this exclusion record originated (e.g., Salesforce CRM, Adobe Experience Platform, state regulatory portal, internal gaming platform). Supports data lineage and reconciliation in the Silver layer.']
  state_exclusion_list_match_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this bettor was identified via a state-level exclusion list (distinct from NCPG national list). True indicates the exclusion was triggered by a state gaming authority\'s exclusion registry match.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which this self-exclusion record was most recently modified in the data platform. Tracks reinstatement updates, status changes, and regulatory notification updates.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a bettor\'s self-exclusion election or operator-imposed exclusion from gaming activities. Captures bettor account ID, exclusion type (voluntary self-exclusion, operator exclusion, state-mandated exclusion via NCPG/state exclusion lists), exclusion scope (single platform, all platforms, statewide), exclusion start date, exclusion end date (or permanent flag), reinstatement request date, reinstatement approval status, and jurisdiction. Distinct from responsible_gaming_limit — self-exclusion is a full account suspension, not a limit adjustment.'
