  bonus_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the bonus redemption. \'active\' = credited and available; \'wagering_in_progress\' = bettor is working through wagering requirement; \'completed\' = wagering requirement met; \'expired\' = bonus lapsed before completion; \'forfeited\' = bettor or operator cancelled the bonus.']
  bonus_type_code varchar [note: 'Classification of the bonus offer type redeemed. Determines accounting treatment, wagering requirement calculation, and responsible gaming monitoring rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: deposit_match|free_bet|risk_free_bet|reload|referral|loyalty|no_deposit — promote to reference product]']
  completion_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time at which the bettor satisfied the full wagering requirement and the bonus was converted to real money. Null if the bonus has not yet reached \'completed\' status.']
  converted_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Actual monetary amount successfully converted from bonus funds to real-money balance upon completion of wagering requirements. Zero if forfeited; may be less than bonus_amount_credited for partial conversions.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time this bonus redemption record was first created in the Silver Layer data product. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SLA compliance monitoring.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to all monetary amounts on this redemption record (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR).']
  deposit_trigger_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'The qualifying deposit amount made by the bettor that triggered eligibility for this bonus offer (applicable for deposit-match and reload bonus types). Zero or null for no-deposit bonuses.']
  eligible_market_scope varchar [note: 'Scope of betting markets on which qualifying wagers may be placed to satisfy the wagering requirement for this bonus redemption. Restricts bonus usage to specific product verticals.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Calendar date by which the bettor must complete the wagering requirement; if not met, the bonus transitions to \'expired\' status and any unconverted balance is forfeited.']
  final_outcome varchar [note: 'Terminal result of the bonus redemption lifecycle: \'converted\' = bonus successfully converted to real money; \'forfeited\' = bonus lost due to expiry, violation, or cancellation; \'pending\' = lifecycle not yet concluded; \'partially_converted\' = portion converted before forfeiture.']
  forfeited_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Monetary value of the bonus that was forfeited rather than converted to real money, due to expiry, terms violation, or bettor cancellation. Used for promotional ROI and liability release accounting.']
  forfeiture_reason_code varchar [note: 'Coded reason explaining why the bonus was forfeited, if applicable. Supports regulatory reporting, customer service resolution, and responsible gaming audit trails.']
  kyc_status varchar [note: 'Know Your Customer (KYC) verification status of the bettor account at the time of bonus redemption. Ensures compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) regulations before bonus funds are credited.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time this bonus redemption record was most recently modified in the Silver Layer, reflecting status changes, wagering requirement updates, or outcome resolution.']
  min_odds_requirement decimal(8,4) [note: 'Minimum decimal odds threshold that qualifying wagers must meet to count toward the wagering requirement for this bonus. Prevents bettors from satisfying requirements with near-certain outcome bets.']
  opt_in_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time the bettor explicitly opted into the bonus offer prior to or at the point of redemption. Required for GDPR consent audit and responsible gaming compliance documentation.']
  qualifying_wager_ids varchar [note: 'Comma-delimited list of wager transaction IDs that have contributed toward satisfying the wagering requirement for this bonus redemption. Supports audit trail and dispute resolution.']
  redemption_reference_code varchar [note: 'Externally visible alphanumeric reference code assigned to this redemption event, used for customer service inquiries, audit trails, and regulatory reporting.']
  redemption_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which the bettor claimed and activated the bonus offer on the gaming platform.']
  responsible_gaming_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this bonus redemption has been flagged for responsible gaming review, such as when the bettor is on a self-exclusion watch list, has exceeded bonus frequency thresholds, or exhibits problem gambling indicators.']
  self_exclusion_check_passed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the bettor passed the self-exclusion registry check at the time of bonus redemption. A value of False indicates the redemption was flagged or blocked due to self-exclusion status.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational gaming platform or system of record that originated this bonus redemption event (e.g., the sportsbook platform, fantasy sports engine, or DTC digital platform).']
  terms_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the bonus terms and conditions accepted by the bettor at the time of redemption. Supports regulatory audit and dispute resolution by preserving the exact terms in force.']
  wagering_requirement_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Total monetary amount the bettor must wager to satisfy the bonus wagering requirement, calculated as bonus_amount_credited multiplied by wagering_requirement_multiplier at the time of redemption.']
  wagering_requirement_multiplier decimal(6,2) [note: 'The rollover multiplier applied to the bonus amount to determine the total wagering obligation (e.g., 10x means the bettor must wager 10 times the bonus amount before conversion to real money).']
  wagering_requirement_remaining decimal(18,4) [note: 'Outstanding monetary amount still required to be wagered before the bonus can be converted to real money. Decremented as qualifying wagers are placed. Used for real-time bonus liability tracking.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a bettor claiming and consuming a bonus offer. Captures bettor account ID, bonus offer ID, redemption timestamp, bonus amount credited, wagering requirement remaining, qualifying wager IDs, bonus expiry date, bonus status (active, wagering_in_progress, completed, expired, forfeited), and final bonus outcome (converted to real money or forfeited). Supports bonus liability tracking, promotional ROI measurement, and responsible gaming bonus monitoring.'
}

  bureau_provider_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the third-party identity verification bureau or data provider used for this verification (e.g., Jumio, Onfido, LexisNexis). Populated when verification_method is bureau_check or biometric. Used for vendor performance tracking and regulatory audit.']
  bureau_response_code varchar [note: 'The result or decision code returned by the third-party identity bureau following their verification check (e.g., CLEAR, CONSIDER, CAUTION, FAIL). Used to drive automated approval/rejection workflows and compliance reporting.']
  bureau_transaction_reference varchar [note: 'The unique transaction or case reference number returned by the third-party identity bureau (e.g., Jumio scan reference, Onfido check ID). Used for reconciliation, dispute resolution, and regulatory audit trail with the external provider.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this KYC verification record was first created in the system. Serves as the audit trail creation marker for data lineage and compliance purposes.']
  data_retention_expiry_date date [note: 'The date after which this KYC verification record and associated documents must be purged or anonymized in accordance with data retention policies. Calculated based on jurisdiction-specific retention requirements (typically 5-7 years post-account closure under AML regulations).']
  document_authenticity_score decimal(5,4) [note: 'Numeric confidence score (0.0000 to 1.0000) from the document verification system indicating the likelihood that the submitted document is genuine and unaltered. Derived from security feature checks, font analysis, and tamper detection by the bureau provider.']
  document_expiry_date date [note: 'The expiration date of the submitted identity document in yyyy-MM-dd format. Used to determine document validity at the time of verification and to flag expired documents that require re-submission.']
  document_issuing_country varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the authority that issued the submitted identity document. Used for jurisdiction-specific compliance checks and sanctions screening.']
  document_reference_number varchar [note: 'The official document number from the submitted identity document (e.g., passport number, national ID number, driver\'s license number). Classified as restricted PII as it directly identifies the individual and is subject to GDPR, CCPA, and gaming regulatory data protection requirements.']
  document_type varchar [note: 'Type of identity or supporting document submitted by the bettor for verification. Passport and national_id are primary identity documents; drivers_license serves dual identity/age purposes; utility_bill and bank_statement are used for address or source-of-funds verification; tax_document supports source-of-funds checks.']
  escalation_reason varchar [note: 'Narrative description of why this KYC verification was escalated to senior compliance review or regulatory authority. Populated when verification_status is escalated. Supports compliance audit trail and regulatory reporting obligations.']
  escalation_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this KYC verification was escalated to senior compliance review or regulatory authority. Distinct from verification_timestamp. Used for SLA tracking of escalation resolution timelines.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which this KYC verification record expires and the bettor\'s verified status lapses. Distinct from reverification_due_date (which is the deadline for completing a new check) and document_expiry_date (which is the document\'s own validity). Driven by jurisdiction-specific periodic review schedules.']
  is_initial_verification boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this is the first KYC verification performed for the bettor account (True) or a subsequent periodic re-verification or triggered re-check (False). Used to distinguish onboarding KYC from ongoing monitoring verifications in regulatory reporting.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this KYC verification record. Used for change tracking, data lineage, and audit trail in the Silver Layer lakehouse.']
  liveness_check_passed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the bettor passed the biometric liveness detection test, confirming the verification was performed by a live person and not a spoofing attempt (e.g., photo replay, deepfake). Populated when verification_method is biometric.']
  pep_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the bettor has been identified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) during KYC screening. PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence requirements under FATF guidelines and most gaming regulatory frameworks.']
  rejection_reason_code varchar [note: 'Standardized code indicating why a KYC verification was rejected (e.g., EXPIRED_DOC, MISMATCH_NAME, POOR_IMAGE_QUALITY, SANCTIONS_HIT, FRAUD_SUSPECTED, INCOMPLETE_SUBMISSION). Populated when verification_status is rejected or escalated. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EXPIRED_DOC|MISMATCH_NAME|POOR_IMAGE_QUALITY|SANCTIONS_HIT|FRAUD_SUSPECTED|INCOMPLETE_SUBMISSION|UNSUPPORTED_DOC_TYPE|ADDRESS_MISMATCH — promote to reference product]']
  rejection_reason_description varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative description of why the KYC verification was rejected or escalated. Complements the rejection_reason_code with additional context for compliance agents and regulatory reporting.']
  reverification_due_date date [note: 'The date by which the bettor must complete a new KYC verification cycle. Triggered by document expiry, regulatory periodic review requirements, risk-based re-screening schedules, or changes in bettor risk profile. Null if no re-verification is currently scheduled.']
  review_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes entered by the compliance agent during manual review of this KYC verification. Captures qualitative observations, decision rationale, and any additional context not captured in structured fields. Supports audit trail and regulatory examination.']
  risk_rating varchar [note: 'Risk classification assigned to the bettor account as a result of this KYC verification, based on AML risk-based approach guidelines. Drives enhanced due diligence requirements, monitoring frequency, and transaction limits. Aligned with FATF risk-based approach.']
  sanctions_hit_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the bettor matched any entry on a sanctions list (e.g., OFAC SDN, EU Consolidated List, UN Sanctions) during KYC screening. A confirmed sanctions hit requires immediate account restriction and regulatory notification.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the originating system or platform from which this KYC verification record was ingested into the Silver Layer lakehouse. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation between operational systems (e.g., Jumio, Onfido, Salesforce CRM) and the lakehouse.']
  submission_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the bettor submitted their KYC documents or initiated the verification request. Used to measure verification turnaround time and SLA compliance from submission to decision.']
  verification_attempt_number varchar [note: 'Sequential count of how many times the bettor has attempted KYC verification for this verification type on their account. Used to enforce maximum attempt limits, detect fraud patterns, and trigger escalation workflows after repeated failures.']
  verification_method varchar [note: 'The technical or procedural method used to perform the verification. document_upload involves bettor-submitted documents; biometric uses facial recognition or liveness checks; bureau_check uses third-party identity bureaus (Jumio, Onfido); database_check queries government or credit databases; manual_review involves a compliance agent.']
  verification_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to this KYC verification case, used for correspondence with regulators, third-party bureaus (e.g., Jumio, Onfido), and internal audit trails.']
  verification_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the KYC verification record. pending: awaiting review or processing; approved: verification passed and account cleared; rejected: verification failed; escalated: referred to senior compliance or regulator; expired: verification lapsed and re-verification is required.']
  verification_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The principal real-world timestamp when the KYC verification decision (approved, rejected, escalated) was made. Distinct from record creation timestamp. Critical for regulatory reporting of verification timelines and SLA compliance.']
  verification_type varchar [note: 'Category of KYC check being performed. Determines the regulatory obligation being fulfilled: identity confirms who the bettor is, age confirms legal gambling eligibility, address confirms residency, source_of_funds confirms AML compliance, enhanced_due_diligence applies to high-risk or high-value accounts.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Monotonically incrementing version counter for this KYC verification record, supporting optimistic concurrency control and change history tracking in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Incremented on each status change or material update.']

  Note: 'KYC (Know Your Customer) identity verification record for each bettor account — capturing verification type (identity, age, address, source of funds), verification method (document upload, biometric, third-party bureau check via Jumio/Onfido), document type submitted, verification status (pending, approved, rejected, escalated), verification timestamp, verifying agent or system, rejection reason, and re-verification due date. Mandatory for AML compliance and gaming license obligations across all jurisdictions.'
}

  projected_points decimal(10,4) [note: 'Total projected fantasy points for the submitted lineup at the time of entry lock, based on pre-game statistical projections. Used for contest analytics and bettor decision support.']
  promotion_code varchar [note: 'Promotional or referral code applied at the time of entry submission. Used for marketing attribution, bonus reconciliation, and campaign performance reporting.']
  responsible_gaming_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this entry triggered a responsible gaming alert at the time of submission, such as exceeding deposit limits, loss limits, or self-exclusion proximity thresholds. Supports operator compliance with responsible gaming mandates.']
  salary_cap_used decimal(12,2) [note: 'Total salary cap value consumed by the submitted lineup. Must not exceed the contest\'s maximum salary cap limit. Used for lineup validation and contest integrity checks.']
  settlement_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this contest entry was officially settled — final scores confirmed, rank assigned, and prize amount determined. Marks the transition to \'settled\' entry status.']
  sport_type varchar [note: 'Sport category for the DFS contest this entry participates in. Drives scoring rules, position eligibility, and regulatory jurisdiction mapping. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NFL|NBA|MLB|NHL|MLS|PGA|NASCAR|UFC|tennis|college_football|college_basketball|other — promote to reference product]']
  tax_withheld_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Amount of federal or state income tax withheld from the prize payout per applicable tax regulations. Relevant for IRS W-2G reporting when prize exceeds statutory thresholds.']
  void_reason varchar [note: 'Textual description of the reason this entry was voided or cancelled, if applicable (e.g., \'Contest cancelled due to insufficient entries\', \'Bettor self-exclusion triggered\', \'Geolocation violation\'). Null for non-voided entries.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a bettor\'s entry into a DFS contest — capturing contest ID, bettor account ID, entry timestamp, entry fee paid, lineup submitted (athlete selections by position), total projected points, actual points scored, final rank, prize won, and payout status. }

  payout_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the payout disbursement.   payout_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the payout by its originating business event. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: wager_settlement|dfs_contest_prize|fantasy_league_prize|bonus_conversion|promotional_credit|free_bet_winnings — promote to reference product]']

  processor_reference varchar [note: 'Transaction reference number returned by the external payment processor (ACH network, wire transfer system, check issuer, or digital wallet provider) upon submission of the payout instruction. Used for payment reconciliation and dispute resolution.']
  reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally visible alphanumeric reference number assigned to this payout transaction, used for bettor communications, customer service lookups, and reconciliation with payment processors.']
  responsible_gaming_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this payout was subject to a responsible gaming intervention, such as a deposit limit, loss limit, or self-exclusion check at the time of disbursement. Supports responsible gaming compliance reporting to state gaming commissions.']
  reversal_reason varchar [note: 'Reason for reversing a previously completed payout, such as voided wager settlement, fraud investigation, duplicate payout correction, or regulatory clawback. Populated only when payout_status is \'reversed\'.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'Identifies the originating operational system that generated this payout record. Supports data lineage tracking in the silver layer and reconciliation between platform systems.']
  stake_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'The original wager or contest entry fee amount placed by the bettor that generated this payout. Used for W-2G threshold ratio calculation (payout must be 300x stake for sports betting W-2G trigger) and GGR computation.']
  state_withholding_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'State income tax withheld from the gross payout amount per the applicable state gaming jurisdiction\'s withholding requirements. Separate from federal withholding. Zero if the jurisdiction does not require state withholding.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of all gaming prize and winnings payouts disbursed to bettor accounts — covering wager settlements, DFS contest prizes, fantasy league prize distributions, and bonus conversions. Table gaming.market_jurisdiction_availability {
  market_jurisdiction_availability_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the market_jurisdiction_availability association']
  betting_market_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the wagering market definition being authorized or restricted in this jurisdiction']
  jurisdiction_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the gaming regulatory jurisdiction in which this market\'s availability is being governed']
  availability_status varchar [note: 'Current regulatory lifecycle state of this wagering market within the specific jurisdiction. AVAILABLE = market is open and accepting wagers; SUSPENDED = temporarily halted pending review; RESTRICTED = available with conditions; EXCLUDED = explicitly prohibited; PENDING_APPROVAL = awaiting regulatory sign-off.']
  effective_from_date date [note: 'Date on which this market became (or is scheduled to become) available or restricted in this jurisdiction. Supports regulatory audit trails and effective-dated compliance configuration.']
  effective_until_date date [note: 'Date on which this market\'s availability authorization expires or was revoked in this jurisdiction. NULL indicates no scheduled expiry (open-ended authorization). Used for time-bounded regulatory approvals.']
  exclusion_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded reason explaining why this market is excluded or restricted in this jurisdiction (e.g., regulatory prohibition on prop bets, college sports wagering ban, integrity concern). Populated when availability_status is EXCLUDED or RESTRICTED.']
  jurisdiction_availability varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of jurisdiction codes (US state, country, or regulatory zone codes) where this market is legally available for wagering (e.g., \'NJ,NV,PA,CO,UK,MT\'). Drives geo-restriction logic at the platform layer for GDPR, CCPA, and state gaming compliance. [Moved from betting_market: This comma-separated STRING field is a denormalized multi-value encoding of the M:N relationship between betting_market and gaming_jurisdiction. It should be fully replaced by the market_jurisdiction_availability association entity, which provides normalized, queryable, and auditable per-jurisdiction availability records.]']
  jurisdiction_exclusion varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of jurisdiction codes explicitly excluded from this market due to regulatory prohibition or operator policy (e.g., \'UT,HI,WA\'). Complements jurisdiction_availability for precise geo-restriction enforcement. [Moved from betting_market: This comma-separated STRING field is a denormalized multi-value encoding of jurisdiction exclusions. It should be replaced by records in market_jurisdiction_availability with availability_status = EXCLUDED and a populated exclusion_reason, enabling proper regulatory audit trails and compliance reporting.]']
  jurisdiction_specific_max_stake decimal [note: 'Maximum wager amount permitted for this specific market within this specific jurisdiction, expressed in the jurisdiction\'s currency. Overrides the global max_stake_amount on betting_market when a jurisdiction imposes a stricter or different limit. NULL indicates the global market limit applies.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the Authorization contract between betting_market and gaming_jurisdiction. It captures the explicit regulatory authorization (or exclusion) of a specific wagering market within a specific gaming jurisdiction, including availability lifecycle status, effective date range, jurisdiction-specific stake overrides, and exclusion reasons. Each record links one betting_market to one gaming_jurisdiction and carries attributes that exist only in the context of that specific market-jurisdiction pairing. This entity replaces the denormalized jurisdiction_availability and jurisdiction_exclusion STRING fields on betting_market and serves as the SSOT for compliance teams managing market geo-restriction matrices.. Existence Justification: In licensed sportsbook operations, each betting market must be explicitly authorized for each jurisdiction where it is offered — a single market (e.g., NFL moneyline) is available in multiple jurisdictions (NJ, PA, CO), and each jurisdiction hosts hundreds of active markets. Compliance teams actively manage this matrix, controlling availability status, effective dates, jurisdiction-specific stake limits, and exclusion reasons. The relationship is a recognized operational concept called \'Market Jurisdiction Availability\' or \'Market Geo-Restriction\' that is created, updated, and audited as part of regulatory compliance workflows.'
}

Table gaming.selection {
  selection_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for selection']

  opening_odds_decimal decimal(10,4) [note: 'Initial odds offered for this selection when the market opened, expressed in decimal format (e.g., 2.50).']
  provider_name varchar [note: 'Name of the external odds feed provider supplying data for this selection (e.g., SportsRadar, Betgenius, Don Best).']
  restriction_reason varchar [note: 'Explanation for why betting restrictions are applied to this selection (e.g., regulatory requirement, integrity concern, responsible gaming measure). Null if not restricted.']
  result varchar [note: 'Final outcome of the selection after event completion and settlement (win, loss, push/tie, void, or pending settlement).']
  selection_category varchar [note: 'Broader categorization of the selection for market segmentation and reporting (moneyline, handicap, total, proposition, futures, live in-play).']
  selection_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique business identifier for the selection used across betting systems and odds feeds.']
  selection_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the selection indicating the nature of the wagering option (team, individual player, binary outcome, proposition bet, over/under total, point spread).']
  settlement_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the selection was officially settled and results were finalized for payout processing.']
  short_name varchar [note: 'Abbreviated name of the selection for display in constrained UI spaces (e.g., mobile betting slips).']
  status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the selection indicating availability for wagering and settlement state.']
  total_value decimal(10,2) [note: 'Numeric total or line value for over/under selections (e.g., 45.5 points). Null for non-total selections.']
  void_reason varchar [note: 'Explanation for why the selection was voided (e.g., event cancellation, participant withdrawal, rule violation). Null if not voided.']

  Note: 'Master reference table for selection. Referenced by selection_id.'
}

  biometric_linked boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this credential has been linked to a biometric profile (e.g., fingerprint, facial recognition) for enhanced identity verification at high-security access points. True = biometric data is enrolled and active for this credential.']
  biometric_type varchar [note: 'Type of biometric modality enrolled for this credential when biometric_linked is True. Classified as restricted PII/biometric per GDPR Article 9 and CCPA. Values: fingerprint, facial_recognition, iris_scan, palm_vein, none.']
  color_code varchar [note: 'Hex color code representing the physical color of the credential lanyard or card stock, used for rapid visual identification of access tier by security staff at checkpoints (e.g., #FF0000 for red = restricted zone, #00FF00 for green = general operations).']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this credential record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, chain-of-custody tracking, and compliance reporting. Conforms to ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  credential_number varchar [note: 'Externally visible, human-readable credential identifier printed on the physical badge or encoded in the digital pass (e.g., CRED-STAFF-000123). Used by security personnel and access control systems to reference a specific credential without exposing the internal surrogate key.']
  credential_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the credential. active: valid and in use; suspended: temporarily deactivated (e.g., investigation); revoked: permanently cancelled; expired: past validity end date; pending_activation: issued but not yet activated; lost_stolen: reported missing and deactivated for security.']
  credential_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the credential by the category of holder and access purpose. Drives access tier rules and issuance workflows. Values: staff_badge (venue/event staff), media_pass (accredited press/broadcast), vip_access_card (VIP guests and sponsors), contractor_id (third-party contractors), law_enforcement (police/security agencies), athlete_team (players, coaches, team officials).']
  emergency_contact_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the emergency contact person for the credential holder, used by venue medical and security staff in the event of an incident. Classified as restricted PII per GDPR and CCPA.']
  emergency_contact_phone varchar [note: 'Phone number of the emergency contact person for the credential holder. Classified as restricted PII per GDPR and CCPA. Used by venue medical and security staff in emergency situations.']
  escort_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the credential holder must be accompanied by an authorized escort when accessing certain zones. True = escort is mandatory. Used for contractor and visitor credentials in high-security areas.']
  holder_name varchar [note: 'Full legal name of the individual to whom the credential is issued, as printed on the physical credential. Retained for operational verification by security personnel at access points. Classified as restricted PII per GDPR and CCPA.']
  holder_organization varchar [note: 'Name of the organization, team, media outlet, agency, or employer that the credential holder represents (e.g., \'ESPN\', \'Dallas Cowboys\', \'ABC Security Services\'). Used for affiliation-based access grouping and sponsor/partner credential management.']
  holder_role varchar [note: 'Functional role or job title of the credential holder within the event or venue context (e.g., \'Head Coach\', \'Camera Operator\', \'Paramedic\', \'Venue Director\'). Informs access tier assignment and is displayed on the physical credential.']
  issued_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the credential was physically produced and issued to the holder. Distinct from valid_from (when access begins) — a credential may be issued days before it becomes active.']
  issuing_authority varchar [note: 'Name of the organizational unit or external body responsible for issuing and authorizing this credential (e.g., \'NFL Security Office\', \'FIFA Accreditation Centre\', \'Venue Security Manager\'). Establishes chain-of-custody accountability.']
  issuing_authority_code varchar [note: 'Standardized short code identifying the issuing authority (e.g., \'NFL_SEC\', \'FIFA_ACC\', \'VENUE_MGR\'). Used for system-level filtering and reporting across multi-league or multi-event deployments.']
  law_enforcement_agency varchar [note: 'Name of the law enforcement agency represented by the credential holder (e.g., \'NYPD\', \'FBI\', \'US Secret Service\'). Populated only for credential_type = law_enforcement. Used for coordination with venue security command.']
  law_enforcement_badge_number varchar [note: 'Official badge or shield number of the law enforcement officer, used to verify identity against agency records. Classified as confidential. Populated only for credential_type = law_enforcement.']
  multi_event_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this credential is valid across multiple events (e.g., a season-long staff badge or a tournament-wide media pass) rather than a single event. True = valid for multiple events within the validity period.']
  photo_url varchar [note: 'Secure URL pointing to the credential holder\'s photograph stored in the Digital Asset Management (DAM) system, used for visual identity verification by security personnel. Classified as restricted biometric PII per GDPR Article 9.']
  print_template_code varchar [note: 'Code referencing the physical credential print template used for this credential type (e.g., \'TMPL-MEDIA-2024\', \'TMPL-STAFF-VIP\'). Determines layout, branding, and security features printed on the badge.']
  revocation_date date [note: 'Date on which the credential was revoked or suspended. Populated only when credential_status is revoked, suspended, or lost_stolen. Part of the chain-of-custody audit trail.']
  revocation_reason varchar [note: 'Reason code explaining why the credential was revoked or suspended. Supports security incident analysis and compliance reporting. Values: lost, stolen, employment_terminated, event_concluded, policy_violation, voluntary_surrender, duplicate_issued. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: lost|stolen|employment_terminated|event_concluded|policy_violation|voluntary_surrender|duplicate_issued — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  rfid_tag_code varchar [note: 'Unique identifier of the RFID chip embedded in the credential card or wristband, used for contactless access control scanning. Classified as confidential as it is a physical access key. Null if the credential does not use RFID technology.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational system of record from which this credential record originated (e.g., TICKETMASTER_AXS for access control credentials, ARCHTICS for venue-managed credentials, MANUAL_ENTRY for credentials issued outside automated systems). Supports data lineage in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this credential record. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  valid_until date [note: 'Date on which the credential expires and access is automatically revoked. For event credentials, typically the day after the event concludes. For season credentials, the last day of the season. Null indicates an open-ended standing credential subject to manual review.']
  vehicle_access_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this credential also grants vehicle access to restricted parking or loading dock areas at the venue. True = vehicle access is authorized in addition to pedestrian access.']
  vehicle_plate_number varchar [note: 'License plate number of the vehicle authorized for venue access under this credential when vehicle_access_flag is True. Classified as confidential. Null if vehicle access is not granted.']
  valid_from date [note: 'Date from which the credential becomes active and grants access. For event credentials, typically the event setup/load-in date. For season credentials, the first day of the season.']

  Note: 'Master record for all security credentials issued to personnel operating at Sports Entertainment venues and events — staff badges, media passes, VIP access cards, contractor IDs, law enforcement credentials, and athlete/team credentials. Captures credential type, holder identity reference, issuing authority, validity period, access tier, biometric linkage flag, barcode/RFID identifier, revocation status, and chain-of-custody audit fields. SSOT for credential identity across all access control operations.'
}

  credential_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the credential (badge, card, biometric token, or digital pass) that was presented at the reader. Distinct from a fan ticket — covers staff, media, VIP, and operational credentials.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the security officer or staff member who performed a manual override or was stationed at the checkpoint. Null when no officer interaction occurred.']
  event_fixture_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the scheduled sports or entertainment event during which this access scan occurred. Links the access record to the event context for occupancy and security reporting.']
  fan_profile_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to fan.fan_profile. Business justification: Fan entry audit trails, loyalty point earning on gate entry, and security incident correlation all require linking access events to fan profiles. Standard sports venue access-control and CRM integrati']
  fixture_id varchar [note: 'FK to event.fixture.fixture_id — Event-correlated access control — security operations must correlate access scans to specific events for crowd management, capacity monitoring, and incident investigation.']
  officer_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the security officer or staff member who performed a manual override or was stationed at the checkpoint. Null when no officer interaction occurred.']
  override_of_access_event_id varchar [note: 'Self-referencing FK on access_event (override_of_access_event_id)']
  security_incident_id varchar [note: 'Reference to a security incident record if this access event triggered or was associated with a security incident. Null when no incident was raised. Supports post-event forensic review and incident management workflows.']
  venue_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the venue where the access event occurred. Used to associate the scan event with a specific Sports Entertainment facility.']
  access_direction varchar [note: 'Direction of movement at the checkpoint: \'entry\' = entering the zone or venue, \'exit\' = leaving the zone or venue, \'internal\' = movement between internal zones. Used for real-time occupancy tracking and crowd flow analysis.']
  ada_accommodation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the credential holder required an ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) accommodation at this access point (e.g., accessible gate routing). True = ADA accommodation applied; False = standard access.']
  anti_passback_zone varchar [note: 'Identifier of the anti-passback zone group assigned to this checkpoint. Anti-passback rules prevent a credential from being used to enter a zone it has not exited. Used for tailgating detection and occupancy integrity.']
  biometric_verified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether biometric verification (e.g., facial recognition, fingerprint) was used as part of the credential authentication for this scan event. True = biometric match confirmed; False = biometric not used or not matched.']
  checkpoint_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name or label of the physical access checkpoint (e.g., \'Gate A – North Entrance\', \'Field Level Door 3\', \'Media Tunnel\'). Supports operational reporting and post-event forensic review without requiring a zone lookup.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this access event record was first written to the Silver layer lakehouse. Distinct from scan_timestamp (the real-world event time). Used for data pipeline audit trails and SLA monitoring.']
  credential_holder_category varchar [note: 'Broad category of the person holding the credential. Distinct from credential_type (which describes the credential itself); this describes the person\'s role. Used for access pattern analytics and compliance reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: athlete|staff|media|vip|vendor|law_enforcement|official — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  credential_token varchar [note: 'Tokenized or masked representation of the physical credential identifier (e.g., RFID card number, barcode, NFC token) as presented to the reader. Stored in tokenized form to comply with PCI-DSS and GDPR. Not the raw credential number.']

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: staff_badge|media_pass|vip_credential|vendor_pass|law_enforcement|athlete_credential|digital_mobile — promote to reference product]']
  data_retention_expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which this access event record is scheduled for deletion or anonymization per applicable data retention policies (GDPR, CCPA). Supports automated data lifecycle management in the lakehouse.']
  denial_reason_code varchar [note: 'Standardized code indicating why access was denied or flagged. Null when scan_result is \'granted\' or \'override_granted\'. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: INVALID_CREDENTIAL|EXPIRED_CREDENTIAL|ZONE_NOT_AUTHORIZED|BLACKLISTED|DUPLICATE_SCAN|CAPACITY_EXCEEDED|SYSTEM_ERROR — promote to reference product]']
  duplicate_scan_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this scan event was detected as a duplicate presentation of the same credential within a short time window (anti-passback detection). True = duplicate detected; False = unique scan.']
  emergency_evacuation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this scan event occurred during an active emergency evacuation protocol. True = evacuation mode active at time of scan; False = normal operations. Critical for post-incident headcount reconciliation.']
  event_phase varchar [note: 'Operational phase of the event at the time of the scan. Used to segment access patterns by event lifecycle stage for crowd management analytics and post-event review.']
  gdpr_data_subject_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the credential holder associated with this scan event is a data subject under GDPR jurisdiction (e.g., EU resident). True = GDPR data subject protections apply; False = not subject to GDPR. Drives data retention and erasure workflows.']
  law_enforcement_notified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether law enforcement was notified as a result of this access event (e.g., blacklisted credential, flagged individual). True = law enforcement notification triggered; False = no notification.']
  network_zone varchar [note: 'Network segment or VLAN identifier of the reader device that processed this scan. Used for cybersecurity segmentation audits and forensic network analysis in the event of a security breach.']
  occupancy_count_at_scan varchar [note: 'Snapshot of the current occupancy count for the zone at the moment this scan event was processed. Captured at scan time to support real-time occupancy tracking and capacity compliance reporting.']
  officer_override_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a security officer manually overrode the system\'s access decision for this event. True = officer override applied; False = system decision was final. Critical for post-event forensic review and accountability audits.']
  override_justification varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded reason provided by the officer when performing a manual override. Required when officer_override_flag is True. Supports accountability and compliance audit trails.']
  reader_device_code varchar [note: 'Reference to the physical access control reader or scanner device that captured this scan event. Used for device-level diagnostics, tamper detection, and post-event forensic review.']
  reader_firmware_version varchar [note: 'Firmware version of the access control reader device at the time of the scan. Captured for forensic integrity, device audit trails, and vulnerability management compliance.']
  reader_location_code varchar [note: 'Alphanumeric code identifying the physical location of the reader device within the venue (e.g., \'NE-G1-R04\'). Supports device-level forensic analysis and maintenance tracking.']
  scan_duration_ms varchar [note: 'Time in milliseconds taken for the reader to process the credential and return a result. Used for throughput analysis, reader performance monitoring, and identifying bottlenecks at high-traffic checkpoints.']
  scan_result varchar [note: 'Outcome of the credential scan at the access point. \'granted\' = access permitted; \'denied\' = access refused; \'flagged\' = access held for secondary review; \'override_granted\' = officer manually permitted entry; \'timeout\' = reader did not receive a valid response. Core field for real-time occupancy tracking and compliance audit trails.']
  scan_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time (with timezone offset) when the credential was presented to the reader. The principal real-world event time for this access event. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  secondary_screening_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the credential holder was referred for secondary security screening (e.g., bag check, wand scan) at this access event. True = secondary screening triggered; False = standard throughput.']
  source_event_reference varchar [note: 'The original event transaction ID or record key from the source access control system (e.g., Ticketmaster/AXS transaction ID). Enables traceability back to the operational system of record for audit and reconciliation.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the access control system that originated this scan event record (e.g., AXS, Ticketmaster, Lenel, C-Cure, Genetec). Supports multi-system venue environments and data lineage tracking in the Silver layer.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this access event record was last modified in the Silver layer (e.g., enrichment, correction, incident linkage). Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.']
  watchlist_match_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the credential or credential holder matched an entry on a security watchlist at the time of the scan. True = watchlist match detected; False = no match. Triggers escalation workflows.']
  zone_capacity varchar [note: 'Maximum permitted occupancy for the zone at the time of the scan event, as configured in the access control system. Used alongside occupancy_count_at_scan to determine capacity compliance status.']
  zone_level varchar [note: 'Security classification level of the zone being accessed at the time of the scan. Captures the sensitivity of the zone for risk-tiered reporting and compliance. Values: public, restricted, highly_restricted, field_level, backstage.']

  Note: 'High-volume transactional record of every physical access control scan event at venue entry and internal zone checkpoints — credential presented, zone accessed, timestamp, scan result (granted/denied/flagged), reader device ID, officer override flag, and denial reason code. Feeds real-time occupancy tracking, post-event forensic review, and compliance audit trails. Distinct from ticketing.gate_scan which covers fan ticket entitlement scanning.'
}

  Note: 'Transactional record of individual fan or personnel screening interactions at security checkpoints — capturing checkpoint ID, timestamp, screening outcome (cleared/secondary screening/denied entry/prohibited item confiscated), prohibited item type if applicable, officer ID, and escalation flag. Supports post-event security review, prohibited item trend analysis, and checkpoint throughput reporting.'

  reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric case number assigned at the time of incident creation, used for cross-system tracking, law enforcement reporting, and insurance claims. Format: SEC-YYYY-NNNNNN.']

  response_time_minutes varchar [note: 'Elapsed time in minutes between the incident occurrence timestamp and the arrival of the first responding security officer. Key performance indicator (KPI) for security operations SLA compliance and staffing adequacy reviews.']
  section_identifier varchar [note: 'Specific section, block, or area designation within the venue zone where the incident took place (e.g., Section 112, Row G, Gate 4 Entry). Sourced from Archtics seating inventory for precise location mapping.']
  severity_tier varchar [note: 'Standardized severity classification assigned to the incident at time of reporting, used to prioritize response resources and escalation protocols. Tier 1 Critical requires immediate law enforcement; Tier 4 Low is handled by venue security staff.']
  surveillance_footage_available boolean [note: 'Indicates whether CCTV or surveillance camera footage is available and has been preserved for this incident. Critical for evidence management, legal proceedings, and post-incident review.']

  Note: 'Core transactional record for all security incidents occurring at Sports Entertainment venues and events — fan altercations, ejections, prohibited item seizures, field invasions, credentialing violations, threats, suspicious packages, and law enforcement interventions. Distinct from venue.safety_incident which covers physical safety/OSHA events.'

  plan_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable descriptive name for the crowd management plan, typically referencing the event name, venue, and season or date for easy identification by operations staff.']
  plan_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, or event-specific considerations not captured in structured fields. May include weather contingency notes, VIP movement protocols, or coordination notes with law enforcement.']
  plan_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the crowd management plan. Draft indicates initial authoring; under_review indicates pending security director sign-off; approved indicates authorized for use; active indicates currently in force on event day; superseded indicates replaced by a newer version; archived indicates retired.']
  plan_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the crowd management plan by event category, determining the baseline protocol template and regulatory scrutiny level applied. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: standard|high_risk|vip_event|concert|sporting_event|multi_day — promote to reference product]']
  plan_version varchar [note: 'Version number of the crowd management plan in major.minor format, tracking iterative revisions as event details, venue configurations, or regulatory requirements change prior to event day.']
  prohibited_items_list varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of items prohibited from entry under this crowd management plan (e.g., large bags, glass containers, laser pointers, professional cameras). Drives security screening protocols and public-facing communications.']
  security_staffing_count varchar [note: 'Total number of security personnel (including contracted and in-house staff) scheduled to be deployed for this event under this crowd management plan. Used for workforce planning and compliance with venue licensing conditions.']
  submitted_to_authority_date date [note: 'Date on which this crowd management plan was formally submitted to the relevant local authority, fire marshal, or governing body for review and licensing approval. Required for regulatory compliance tracking.']
  surveillance_camera_count varchar [note: 'Total number of CCTV and surveillance cameras active and covering the venue under this crowd management plan. Used to verify adequate coverage density per zone and compliance with venue licensing conditions.']
  surveillance_system_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the venue CCTV and surveillance system is confirmed active and operational for this event under this plan. A value of True confirms surveillance coverage is in place as required by the plan.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp at which this crowd management plan record was most recently modified. Tracks plan revisions and supports version control audit trails for regulatory compliance.']
  venue_configuration_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the specific seating and floor layout configuration of the venue for this event, as defined in the Archtics venue seating and inventory management system. Different configurations (e.g., end-stage, center-stage, full-capacity, reduced-capacity) drive different crowd flow strategies.']
  zone_occupancy_thresholds varchar [note: 'Structured description of maximum safe occupancy thresholds by venue zone (e.g., lower bowl, upper deck, floor/GA, concourse, VIP areas). Stored as a delimited key-value string (zone_code:max_persons) since complex types are not permitted. Drives real-time crowd density monitoring and gate hold decisions.']

  Note: 'Master record for crowd management and ingress/egress operational plans developed for each event or venue configuration. Captures plan version, event reference, venue configuration, crowd flow strategy, entry gate activation schedule, expected peak ingress time, maximum safe occupancy thresholds by zone, emergency evacuation routes, and approval sign-off by venue security director. Serves as the operational blueprint for event-day crowd control.'

Table security.occupancy_snapshot {

  access_zone_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific access control zone within the venue (e.g., GA floor, VIP suite level, concourse section) for which this snapshot records occupancy. Sourced from Archtics venue seating and inventory management.']
  emergency_response_plan_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the active emergency response plan governing this zone during the event. Links to the pre-approved evacuation and incident response procedures applicable to the current security level and event type.']
  event_fixture_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the live event (game, concert, match) for which this occupancy snapshot was captured. Links the snapshot to the event scheduling and planning context.']
  fixture_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the live event (game, concert, match) for which this occupancy snapshot was captured. Links the snapshot to the event scheduling and planning context.']
  franchise_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to league.franchise. Business justification: Occupancy snapshots at franchise home games feed franchise-level capacity compliance reporting, league safety audits, and insurance risk assessments. League operations benchmarks franchise capacity ma']
  league_season_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to league.season. Business justification: Season-scoped occupancy data supports league annual capacity compliance reporting, franchise safety benchmarking, and regulatory submissions covering fan safety across the full season lifecycle.']
  previous_occupancy_snapshot_id varchar [note: 'Self-referencing FK on occupancy_snapshot (previous_occupancy_snapshot_id)']
  previous_snapshot_occupancy_snapshot_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the immediately preceding occupancy snapshot record for the same event and zone. Enables delta calculation of occupancy changes between intervals without requiring a self-join on sequence number.']
  venue_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the venue where the event is being held. Enables venue-level occupancy aggregation and capacity benchmarking across facilities.']
  ada_accessible_zone boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this zone is designated as ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) accessible, with compliant pathways, seating, and egress routes. Relevant for emergency evacuation planning and accessibility compliance reporting.']
  alert_severity varchar [note: 'Categorical severity classification of the capacity alert for this snapshot. none = below threshold; advisory = approaching threshold; warning = at threshold; critical = at or exceeding maximum capacity. Informs escalation protocols for security and emergency response teams.']
  alert_threshold_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The occupancy percentage at which the capacity_alert_flag is set to True for this zone. Configurable per zone and event type to reflect different risk tolerances (e.g., 85% for GA floor, 95% for seated sections).']
  available_capacity varchar [note: 'The remaining number of persons that can be admitted to the zone before reaching maximum capacity (max_capacity minus current_occupancy_count). Used by gate staff and security supervisors for real-time admission control decisions.']
  capacity_alert_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this snapshot has triggered a capacity threshold alert (True) because occupancy is approaching or exceeding the defined alert threshold percentage. Drives real-time notifications to security operations and venue management.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this occupancy snapshot record was first written to the Silver Layer data product. Serves as the audit creation timestamp for data lineage and pipeline monitoring purposes.']
  credentialed_staff_count varchar [note: 'The number of credentialed staff (security personnel, event staff, medical, law enforcement) present within the zone at the time of the snapshot. Used to calculate staff-to-patron ratios for crowd management compliance and post-event safety reporting.']
  crowd_density_category varchar [note: 'Qualitative classification of crowd density in the zone based on occupancy percentage thresholds. low (<50%), moderate (50–74%), high (75–84%), very_high (85–94%), critical (95%+). Used by security operations for rapid situational awareness without requiring numeric interpretation.']
  current_occupancy_count varchar [note: 'The number of persons physically present within the access zone at the time of the snapshot. Derived from gate scan aggregation, manual count, or sensor feed as indicated by the data_source field.']
  data_quality_flag varchar [note: 'Indicates the reliability status of the occupancy count in this snapshot. valid = confirmed accurate reading; estimated = interpolated due to sensor gap; suspect = anomalous reading under review; missing = no data received; corrected = manually adjusted post-capture. Critical for emergency response decision-making confidence.']
  data_source varchar [note: 'The method or system used to collect the occupancy count for this snapshot. Values include gate_scan (Ticketmaster/AXS barcode scan aggregation), manual_count (security staff tally), sensor_feed (IoT crowd density sensor), ticketing_system (Archtics scan data), or hybrid (combination of sources).']
  egress_count varchar [note: 'The number of persons who exited the access zone since the previous snapshot interval. Sourced from gate scan aggregation or sensor directional flow data. Critical for monitoring evacuation progress during emergency response scenarios.']
  event_phase varchar [note: 'The operational phase of the event at the time of the snapshot. Enables phase-specific crowd density analysis and comparison of occupancy patterns across pre_event, ingress, in_progress, halftime, egress, and post_event periods.']
  gate_scan_count varchar [note: 'The number of valid ticket scans recorded at access gates for this zone since the previous snapshot interval. Sourced directly from Ticketmaster/AXS access control systems. Used to cross-validate sensor-based occupancy readings.']
  incident_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a security or safety incident is actively in progress within or adjacent to this zone at the time of the snapshot. When True, the snapshot is tagged for priority review by the security operations center and incident management teams.']
  incident_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the active incident type when incident_flag is True. Drives specific emergency response protocol activation: medical, crowd_crush, fire, evacuation, disturbance, suspicious_item, or none. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: medical|crowd_crush|fire|evacuation|disturbance|suspicious_item|none — promote to reference product]']
  ingress_count varchar [note: 'The number of persons who entered the access zone since the previous snapshot interval. Sourced from gate scan aggregation (Ticketmaster/AXS) or sensor directional flow data. Supports ingress rate monitoring during peak entry periods.']
  law_enforcement_present boolean [note: 'Indicates whether sworn law enforcement officers (police, sheriff, federal agents) are physically deployed in or immediately adjacent to this zone at the time of the snapshot. Relevant for incident response coordination and post-event security reporting.']
  manual_override boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the occupancy count in this snapshot was manually entered or adjusted by a security supervisor, overriding the automated system reading. When True, manual_override_reason should be populated.']
  manual_override_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text explanation provided by the security supervisor when manual_override is True. Documents the justification for overriding automated occupancy data (e.g., \'sensor malfunction in north corridor\', \'gate scanner offline\'). Required for audit trail compliance.']
  max_capacity varchar [note: 'The licensed or operationally approved maximum number of persons permitted in the access zone simultaneously. Established by venue fire code, local authority, and ADA compliance requirements. Sourced from Archtics venue inventory.']
  occupancy_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The ratio of current occupancy count to maximum zone capacity expressed as a percentage (0.00–100.00+). Used to trigger crowd density alerts and inform real-time security deployment decisions.']
  occupancy_trend varchar [note: 'Directional trend of occupancy compared to the previous snapshot for this zone: increasing (net ingress), stable (minimal change within ±2%), or decreasing (net egress). Provides rapid situational awareness for security supervisors without requiring numeric comparison.']
  security_level varchar [note: 'The operational security posture in effect for the zone at the time of the snapshot. Reflects threat assessment and law enforcement coordination status: standard, elevated, high, or critical. Aligned with DHS National Terrorism Advisory System levels adapted for venue operations.']
  sensor_device_code varchar [note: 'The unique identifier of the IoT sensor, gate scanner, or counting device that provided the primary occupancy reading for this snapshot. Enables device-level data quality auditing and fault isolation when readings are anomalous.']
  snapshot_interval_seconds varchar [note: 'The configured polling interval in seconds between successive occupancy snapshots for this zone during the event. Typical values: 30, 60, 120, 300. Shorter intervals are used during high-risk periods such as event ingress and egress.']
  snapshot_sequence_number varchar [note: 'Sequential ordinal number of this snapshot within the event and zone combination, starting at 1. Enables ordered time-series reconstruction of occupancy trends for a specific zone throughout the event lifecycle.']
  snapshot_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX) at which this occupancy count was recorded. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for time-series crowd density analysis and emergency response timelines.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The operational system of record from which this occupancy snapshot was originated. Enables data lineage tracing and source-specific data quality assessment across Ticketmaster/AXS, Archtics, IoT sensor platforms, manual entry, or Adobe Experience Platform integrations.']
  surveillance_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether CCTV or other surveillance systems are actively monitoring this zone at the time of the snapshot. A False value may indicate a system outage requiring manual security coverage escalation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this occupancy snapshot record was last modified in the Silver Layer, for example following a manual override correction or data quality reclassification. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.']
  weather_condition varchar [note: 'Prevailing weather condition at the venue at the time of the snapshot, applicable for outdoor or partially outdoor venues. Influences crowd behavior, ingress/egress rates, and emergency response planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clear|cloudy|rain|storm|extreme_heat|extreme_cold|fog — promote to reference product]']
  zone_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the access control zone at the time of the snapshot (e.g., \'GA Floor North\', \'VIP Club Level\', \'Section 101-110\'). Denormalized from Archtics for operational reporting without requiring a join.']
  zone_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the access zone by operational category. GA (General Admission), VIP (Very Important Person), seated, standing (SRO - Standing Room Only), concourse, restricted (staff/credential-only), or emergency_exit. Drives zone-specific crowd management protocols. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ga|vip|seated|standing|concourse|restricted|emergency_exit — promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Periodic transactional record capturing real-time venue occupancy counts by access zone during an event. Captures event reference, zone ID, snapshot timestamp, current occupancy count, maximum capacity, occupancy percentage, data source (gate scan aggregation, manual count, sensor feed), and alert flag when approaching capacity thresholds. Enables live crowd density monitoring and supports emergency response decision-making.'
}

  law_enforcement_notified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether law enforcement was notified as a result of this confiscation event. True = law enforcement contacted; False = handled internally. Triggers law enforcement handover workflow when True.']
  owner_provided_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the individual from whom the item was confiscated voluntarily provided their identity information. True = identity provided; False = identity not provided or refused. Governs whether owner identity fields are populated and affects retrieval eligibility.']
  owner_ticket_barcode varchar [note: 'Barcode or ticket reference number from the ticket held by the individual from whom the item was confiscated. Links the confiscation event to the ticketing system (Ticketmaster/AXS) for fan identity resolution and post-event ban enforcement.']
  receipt_issued_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a physical or digital confiscation receipt was issued to the item owner at the time of confiscation. True = receipt issued; False = no receipt issued (e.g., item immediately destroyed or owner refused). Supports retrieval claim validation.']
  receipt_number varchar [note: 'Unique receipt number printed on the confiscation receipt issued to the item owner. Used by the owner to claim the item post-event if disposition is \'held for retrieval\'. Populated only when receipt_issued_flag is True.']
  retrieval_date date [note: 'Date on which the confiscated item was retrieved by its owner from secure storage post-event. Populated only when confiscation_status transitions to \'retrieved_by_owner\'. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.']
  storage_location_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the secure storage location (locker, cage, evidence room) where the confiscated item is held when disposition_type is \'held_for_retrieval\'. Supports chain-of-custody tracking and retrieval operations.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this confiscation record, supporting audit trail and chain-of-custody integrity. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  wada_substance_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the confiscated item is classified as a prohibited substance under the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) prohibited list.   Note: 'Transactional record of every prohibited item confiscated at a Sports Entertainment venue screening checkpoint or during an in-venue security response. Supports post-event prohibited item trend reporting and policy calibration.'
}

Table security.footage_camera_scope {
  footage_camera_scope_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the footage_camera_scope association']
  surveillance_camera_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the specific surveillance camera whose footage is in scope for this request.']
  surveillance_footage_request_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the parent surveillance footage request that this camera scope record belongs to.']
  camera_ids_requested varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of surveillance camera identifiers whose footage is being requested. References the physical camera inventory within the venue security system. [Moved from surveillance_footage_request: This comma-separated STRING field is a denormalized multi-valued FK that encodes the M:N relationship in an anti-pattern. It must be decomposed into individual footage_camera_scope records, one per camera per request. The field should be removed from surveillance_footage_request once the association table is populated.]']
  footage_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'End date and time of the footage window requested from this specific camera. May differ per camera within the same request.']
  footage_file_size_gb decimal [note: 'Total size in gigabytes of the footage extracted from this specific camera for this request. Enables per-camera storage and delivery tracking.']
  footage_format varchar [note: 'Digital file format of the footage extracted from this specific camera. Format may vary per camera depending on the recording system it is connected to.']
  footage_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Start date and time of the footage window requested from this specific camera. May differ per camera within the same request if the incident scope varies by location.']
  redaction_completed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether redaction has been completed for the footage from this specific camera. Supports per-camera fulfillment tracking within a multi-camera request.']
  redaction_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the footage from this specific camera requires redaction (e.g., blurring of uninvolved individuals) before disclosure. Redaction requirements may differ per camera based on the areas captured.']
  retrieval_status varchar [note: 'Operational status of footage retrieval for this specific camera within the request. A request may be partially fulfilled if some cameras have been retrieved while others are still pending or failed (e.g., footage overwritten due to retention expiry).']

  Note: 'This association product represents the scoping event between a surveillance_footage_request and a surveillance_camera. It captures which specific cameras are included in a footage request and the per-camera retrieval details — time window, format, file size, and redaction status — that exist only in the context of a specific request-camera pairing. Each record links one surveillance_footage_request to one surveillance_camera and tracks the operational fulfillment state for that camera\'s footage within the request.. Existence Justification: In sports entertainment security operations, a single footage request routinely spans multiple cameras (e.g., an incident investigation covering entrance cameras, concourse cameras, and VIP area cameras simultaneously). Conversely, a single camera will be referenced by many different footage requests over time — law enforcement requests, internal investigations, insurance claims. The business actively manages which specific cameras are included in each request, with per-camera attributes such as the footage time window, file size, format, and redaction status that belong to neither the request nor the camera alone.'
}

  source_document_url varchar [note: 'Secure URL pointing to the authoritative template document stored in the legal document management system (e.g., SharePoint, iManage, or DAM).   template_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this template across business units (e.g., NIL-ATH-v2, VEN-RNT-v1). Used as the human-readable business identifier in legal workflows and document management systems.']

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: litigation|ip_trademark|contract_negotiation|regulatory_compliance|labor_employment|real_estate|corporate_governance|arbitration|mergers_acquisitions|tax — promote to reference product]']
